title: GH#37997: fix(plugin): stop runaway compaction summary loops and repair misanchored compaction boundaries
body:
## Summary

Root cause (incident session DB + OpenCode 1.19.5 source): the gpt-6-luna compaction summarizer copied a long verbatim user aim and fell into a copy loop, repeating one 91-char span (42,580 chars until the user aborted; a later attempt 9,551 chars). Only the 32K output cap bounded it. OpenCode then (a) replayed the aborted, looping summary into the next request and (b) ran the pending compaction with parentID = the user's next typed message (prompt.ts lastUser.id), which has no compaction part, so filterCompacted() skipped the boundary: the next Build+ request still sent 238,049 input tokens (32 messages, ~1.03M part chars) and triggered another compaction, which looped again.

Fix, in four small modules:

- `compaction-loop-detect.mjs` — pure tail detector and collapse.
- `compaction-history-repair.mjs` — messages.transform repair: drops failed/unfinished summaries and applies a summary anchored to a typed message as the boundary.
- `compaction-loop-recovery.mjs` — host actions: abort, rerun via session.summarize (so the new summary is correctly anchored), then continue an automatic compaction with the original agent/model/variant under the existing autocontinue policy. A `RecoveryLedger` keeps the first loop's identity for the whole rerun chain.
- `compaction-replay-collect.mjs` — the GH#35186 verbatim replay treats a typed summary parent that leads the repaired history as the boundary, so user turns trimmed before a misanchored summary are replayed.
- `compaction-loop-guard.mjs` — stream guard on message.part.delta; interactive: abort and rerun, max 2 reruns per 30 min; headless never aborted, completed summary collapsed instead. All hooks fail-open.

Opt-out `AIDEVOPS_COMPACTION_LOOP_GUARD=0`. Documented in reference/session.md.

## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-loop-detect.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-history-repair.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-loop-recovery.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-loop-guard.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-replay-collect.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-compaction-loop-guard.mjs, .agents/reference/session.md

## Decisions

Headless sessions are never aborted (opencode run would exit); they rely on the output cap plus text.complete collapse. Thresholds (2,000+ chars of one unit repeated 4+ times back-to-back) sit far above any legitimate summary repetition. Only compaction summaries are rewritten. The rerun uses the same configured compaction model; after 2 loops in 30 min the guard stops and the toast suggests /compact or pinning agent.compaction.model elsewhere. The module split keeps every new file and `AidevopsPlugin` under the Qlty complexity thresholds; `index.mjs` wiring is plain calls.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — read-only replay of the real incident session (426 messages, 11 compaction summaries) through the production guard and repair code, with a recording client in place of the host API: both looping summaries aborted at 4,714 and 4,822 streamed chars (period 91); each rerun called session.summarize with the parent turn's model (anthropic/claude-fable-5-2) and continued as Build+ with variant xhigh; the 9 clean summaries were neither aborted nor trimmed; the misanchored post-incident request was reduced from 32 messages/~1.03M part chars (238,049 recorded input tokens) to 3 messages/25,770 chars using a port of OpenCode 1.19.5 filterCompacted; on that repaired input the production verbatim replay (createCompactionInputReplay) now injects 6 parts / 5,426 chars of hidden user input, and the 8 clean boundaries are unchanged. Replay re-run after the module split and review fixes: abort points and continuations identical. Host event shape confirmed in OpenCode processor.ts (message.part.delta field text). 0 false positives across 526 clean compaction parts in the shared OpenCode DB. The production `continuation` adapter checked against the real compaction autocontinue guard (primary continues, finished child does not). tests/test-compaction-loop-guard.mjs plus compaction autocontinue tests (12 pass, including a looping rerun that keeps the original variant); the 11 index-loading suites (400 tests) pass; local `qlty smells` reports 0 smells on all changed plugin files; markdownlint clean. Live plugin load to be re-verified after release via aidevops update.

Resolves #37997

title: GH#37986: fix(pulse): bound label-maintenance starvation and re-check held issues first
body:
## Summary

Label maintenance is the only stage that removes needs-simplification and needs-consolidation holds, and it could be deferred on every cycle with no upper bound. When any substage has not started within AIDEVOPS_PULSE_LABEL_MAINTENANCE_STARVATION_S (default 7200s; 0 keeps the legacy order), the engine now runs one bounded slice (default 180s) ahead of early dispatch and skips the normal slot for that cycle. Each re-evaluation substage first re-checks the open issues that carry its label, found with one search call per group of five owners, then runs the per-repository sweep, which skips what was already re-checked and keeps at least a third of the substage time. Refill-reserve deferral lines now state remaining and required seconds.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh

## Decisions

Promotion costs early dispatch at most one 180s slice per bound and per substage. A cycle that already promoted prefetch promotes this stage only at twice the bound. A budget-deferred promoted slice leaves the normal slot free to try. A failed, incomplete or empty search never counts as proof that nothing is held: the sweep remains the safety net. The held-first step resumes after the last issue it reached, so a long held list is not re-checked from the top each run.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified (read-only) on a live runner: the stalest substage attempt was 249028s old and the starvation check returned starved at x1 and x2 and not-starved when disabled; the held-first search answered for 70 repos / 5 owners in about 1s and agreed with gh issue list for the checked repo. bash -n and shellcheck clean on the four changed files. test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh: 6 new assertions pass (starvation contract, held-first contract, 9l5-9l8); its 2 failures (stages clamp/defer/opt out of cycle deadline; dispatch budget admission) reproduce unchanged on the base revision. first-wave, maintenance-selector-contract, reeval-stale-continuation, simplification-auto-dispatch-backfill, consolidation-dispatch, large-file-dependency-lifecycle-canary, consolidation-multi-runner and consolidation-skip-resolved pass. Not yet observed: a deployed pulse cycle promoting the stage; verify after release from the pulse log line 'Label maintenance starvation bound reached'.

Resolves #37986

title: GH#38013: feat(cloudron): routine policy for commit-tracked upstreams

Explicit signed commit-mode Cloudron standing policies bind the upstream repository, trusted open finding and exact resolved SHA, then require strict forward ancestry. Whole-token substitution rejects partial SHA matches. Existing semver policy bodies and boundaries remain unchanged.

title: GH#38021: fix(pulse): restore auto-dispatch removed by a draft checkpoint on a consolidated spec
body:
## Summary

A draft checkpoint on a canonical consolidated spec had auto-dispatch removed by the escalation and never restored, so dispatch filtered the spec until a person re-added the label. The run now records that it is about to remove the label and restores it after the release projection only with that same-run receipt and only when the issue is available, unowned and carries no hold. A deferred release carries the receipt in the private release-retry row, bound into the row digest, so a replay in another process restores it too. The consolidated checkpoint attention comment is deduplicated by the author's resolved write permission, because GitHub App installation reads report a private organization member as CONTRIBUTOR and the association-only test reposted the comment every TTL.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-release-retry.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-output.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-release-retry.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-open-done-nonclosing-regression.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh

## Decisions

Restore only from same-run pre-removal evidence, never inferred from timeline or comments; _has_consolidated_label is unchanged, so a consolidated issue without the label is still not dispatched. Retry rows written before this change carry no receipt and keep their binding. A failed permission lookup with no confirmed writer suppresses the attention comment for that TTL rather than reposting. Also gives the launched-runtime fixture in test-open-done-nonclosing-regression.sh the session evidence GH#37708 requires; that test was failing on main before this change.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Existing release path exercised with only GitHub transport stubbed: test-claim-release-retry.sh 46/0 (record, deferred replay in a second process, edited receipt rejected by the row binding); test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh 178/0 (restore guards for holds, owner, non-available status, missing or foreign receipt, return codes 0/1/2); test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh 14/0 (permission-aware dedup, unverified lookup suppresses posting); checkpoint lifecycle cases from test-headless-runtime-helper.sh 3/0; test-open-done-nonclosing-regression.sh passes; test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh passes with AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_AUTH_ISOLATION=0; linters-local.sh clean including function-complexity. Not yet observed on a live Pulse cycle; that check follows release and deploy.

Resolves #38021

title: GH#38031: fix(pulse-merge): fetch the CI repair PR head from a linked-worktree context
body:
## Summary

CI repair fetched a missing PR head with git fetch against the canonical checkout. The canonical Git guard denies that (exit 42), so on one runner 7 of 10 repair leases ended in pr_head_fetch_failed and each PR waited for a person. The fetch now runs through scratch_worktree_fetch, a new shared helper that borrows an unlocked linked worktree, or creates and removes an owned scratch worktree when none is usable. A missing fetch context is recorded as pr_head_fetch_context_unavailable. Exact-SHA validation after the fetch is unchanged. test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh failed on main: its fixture never created the lifecycle registry parent and inherited the invoking session's lifecycle variables. It is now isolated and passes.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-ci-repair.sh, .agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing-cases.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh

## Decisions

The fetch helper lives in scratch-worktree-helper.sh rather than the CI repair module so the three other canonical fetch sites named in the issue can reuse it. Those sites are not changed here. A linked worktree is borrowed before a scratch one is created, to avoid a checkout per repair; locked worktrees are skipped and --no-write-fetch-head leaves the borrowed worktree's FETCH_HEAD alone. The routing fixture disables generation enrollment; the scratch helper test covers creation and removal with it enabled.

## Runtime Testing

- **Verification:** runtime-verified — test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh: 95 run, 0 failed. Five new cases run _ci_repair_create_worktree against real Git repositories behind a git that refuses fetch in a main worktree: absent head fetched through an owned scratch worktree; absent head fetched through a borrowed sibling worktree; no fetch when the head is already local; scratch context removed after success and after a failed fetch; a moved head still fails closed with pr_head_commit_unavailable. test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh: 11 of 11 pass with the lifecycle enabled (it fails on main). Both test files were run before the rebase onto the current main, which changed only dispatch files. Not verified: the live pulse path, which needs this change deployed. The REST check moved out of the new _dispatch_max_compute_base_parallel (ceremony cap, slot cap, throttle file), so recovery only qualifies when the REST reserve is the sole serial cause: throttle-file and slot-budget serial rounds stay serial. Concurrent priority pools disable recovery so they cannot exceed their share of the ceremony cap. The parallel loop keeps the stop flag, cooperative drain, GraphQL breaker, REST progress and slot fences.

title: GH#38048: fix(pulse): hand a completed full dispatch census across a cooperative bundle drain
body:
## Summary

A cooperatively drained pulse cycle (GH#37907) deleted its completed full dispatch census with the rest of its cycle cache, so the activated bundle started discovery from scratch with free slots and a ranked backlog. The drained cycle now moves the full-census snapshot and its attempt ledger to a bundle-independent handoff slot (`_dispatch_hand_off_candidate_snapshots`) while it still owns the instance lock and the drain marker exists: `_pulse_run_supervisor_phase` runs the cycle-cache cleanup before `release_instance_lock`, because the EXIT-trap cleanup only runs after the marker is gone. The activated bundle's first wave, or any bounded census, adopts the handoff as its durable snapshot (`_dispatch_adopt_candidate_handoff`) when it is inside its existing reuse window, carries the reader's snapshot schema and has a compatible normalization mode, then serves the unattempted remainder without a scan. Snapshots now carry a `schema` field. A handoff that is stale, in another format or on an unsafe path is removed unserved; an eligibility mutation invalidates an unadopted handoff with the other snapshots. The drained cycle still launches nothing, and every adopted candidate still passes the registry/schedule recheck and all live dispatch gates.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh

## Decisions

Handoff happens only under a cooperative drain, so full-census snapshots stay cycle-scoped in every other case. Only a first wave or bounded census adopts; a full round still scans for itself. The existing captured_at/census_seconds reuse window is unchanged, which means a short census can expire before the next first wave (about 6 to 13 minutes after capture in the log) and is then discarded. Snapshots written before this change have no schema field and are never adopted across bundles. The refill-only path is not changed: no refill-only census appears in the current log window. test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh was not extended because its drain case covers the no-launch guarantee and the handoff contract is covered in the snapshot suite.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — shellcheck clean on pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh, pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, pulse-wrapper.sh and the snapshot test. test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh passes with a new GH#38048 case run against the real functions and files: a foreign-owner marker hands nothing over; a drained cycle hands over census plus ledger; a full round scans for itself and an event refill keeps the handoff; the first wave serves the unattempted remainder with no scan and records dispatch_candidate_handoff_adopted and dispatch_candidate_snapshot_hit; stale and foreign-schema handoffs are removed and the wave scans; a normalize round refuses a skip census while a skip round takes it; a label mutation discards an unadopted handoff. test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh passes. test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh 81 passed, 0 failed (GH#37907 drain case unchanged). test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh 5/0, test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh 28/0, test-permission-block-breaker.sh pass. Checked against the 2026-11-13 pulse.log: two drains followed a completed full census (894s, 89 candidates, captured about 04:51:52Z; 915s, 130 candidates, captured about 07:32:36Z). The activated bundle's first wave started about 344s and 800s after capture, inside each census's reuse window (894s and 915s), so both handoffs would have been adopted in place of the 200s first-wave census that ran. Not yet observed on a live drain: the first one that can exercise it is the activation after the release that ships this change, because the bundle being drained must already contain the handoff.

Resolves #38048

title: GH#38055: perf(dispatch): fetch open PR list once per footprint rebuild
body:
## Summary

The in-flight footprint rebuild now fetches the repository's open-PR list once and reuses it for every `status:claimed` issue that needs PR evidence, instead of one `gh pr list --limit 100` call per claimed issue.

Resolves #38055

## Why

Since GH#36817, every claimed issue without ledger or stamp evidence reaches Evidence 2 in `_footprint_claimed_coordinator_has_evidence`. With 22 such issues in the product repository and about 12s per `gh pr list` (56 open PRs with bodies), `dedup.footprint` averaged 93s (max 263s) per candidate and caused per-candidate stage timeouts. Parallel candidates run in separate processes, so every candidate paid the full cost.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
  - Adds a per-rebuild memo (`_FOOTPRINT_OPEN_PRS_*`), activated and cleared by `_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache`.
  - Evidence 2 reuses the memo inside a rebuild. Outside a rebuild it always reads the live PR list, as before.
  - Evidence order and rules, the cache TTL and log lines are unchanged. A failed fetch keeps the existing "no PR evidence" semantics, now for that rebuild only rather than being retried once per claimed issue.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`
  - Test 11d: four claimed issues in one rebuild cause exactly one open-PR fetch. The issue with a `gh<N>` branch keeps its reservation, those without evidence are skipped, and the memo is cleared afterwards.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`: 56 run, 0 failed, including the existing GH#33293/GH#36817 evidence cases.
- `shellcheck` is clean for both files, and the pre-commit quality validation passed.

## Runtime check after deploy

`dedup.footprint` in `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv` should drop from about 93s to the single-fetch cost (about 12s plus the issue read) on runners with many claimed issues. Baseline evidence is in the #38055 comments.

title: GH#38060: fix(worktree): repeat the base-ref fetch after a lost concurrent ref update
body:
## Summary

When several processes fetch the same remote-tracking ref at once, Git rejects all but one ref update with: incorrect old value provided. The worktree helper treated that as a stale base and aborted worktree creation, after the dispatch candidate had already won its claim. _worktree_fetch_origin_branch now repeats the fetch at most twice when Git reports that message. Only a fetch that succeeds counts as a fresh base. Every other failure keeps its single attempt, the SSH-to-HTTPS retry and its exit code. Each repeat is recorded as the precreate.base_fetch_retry sub-stage and documented in reference/dispatch-timing.md. The test fixture now resolves its temp root with pwd -P, because on macOS mktemp returns a path under the /var symlink and the existing recreated-path section failed there before this change.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh

## Decisions

The classifier matches only: incorrect old value provided. That is the one message the reproduction produced. The broader cannot lock ref also covers conflicts a repeat cannot fix, so it is left out. The second repeat waits 1 second; the first is immediate, because the winning fetch has already written the ref.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Real helper under a real race, throwaway repositories, Git 2.53.0 on macOS, 40 rounds of 6 concurrent _worktree_fetch_origin_branch calls after the remote advanced. This branch: 240 of 240 calls returned 0, 200 needed one repeat, at most 2 fetches per call, local origin/main equal to the remote tip in 40 of 40 rounds. main without the change: 40 of 240 returned 0, 200 returned 1 with the race message. test-worktree-fresh-base.sh prints PASS for the new section (one repeat recovers, a persistent rejection stops after 3 fetches, an unrelated failure gets 1 fetch) and, with the pwd -P line, for the recreated-path section. The file still exits 1 at its registration-failure section; that section fails the same way with and without this change and is tracked in GH#38072. No workflow runs this file. Resolves #38060

title: GH#38082: fix(pulse-merge): stop logging successful public-repo approvals as failures
body:
## Summary

privacy_scan_secret_material_text compared text with a command substitution that strips trailing newlines, so every gh-shim body (always newline-ended) printed the script-reference advisory to stderr; no current script basename is even on that allowlist. _pulse_approve_pr_at_head merged that stderr into the review JSON before jq and returned 1 after GitHub had recorded the approval, so every public-repo pulse approval was logged as 'failed to approve' with an empty reason (4/4 on marcusquinn/aidevops on 2026-11-13, each confirmed APPROVED on the exact head via the reviews API). Fix: keep trailing newlines with a sentinel so the advisory fires only on a real redaction; parse stdout only in _pulse_approve_pr_at_head so stderr reaches the caller's log; log state/commit_id when a response does not match. The exact-head trust check is unchanged. Also repairs tests/test-gh-write-privacy-reporting.sh, which has failed on main since GH#37664 made the wrapper block bare private-repo basenames before the shim (CI does not run it): shim-only denials keep GH#34400 coverage via a dedicated marker, and the basename cases now expect the wrapper-layer block.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-write-privacy-reporting.sh

## Decisions

Kept both fixes: the sentinel removes the false advisory at its source, and stdout-only parsing stops any future stderr advisory from turning a recorded approval into a logged failure. The stale test is fixed here because the issue's acceptance criteria require it to pass.

## Runtime Testing

- **Verification:** self-assessed — Runtime (no GitHub write): the real gh shim from this worktree with a stub native gh answering the review POST now gives stderr_bytes=0 and jq_exit=0 state=APPROVED (deployed main: one advisory line, jq_exit=5). privacy_scan_secret_material_text: no advisory for text ending in one or two newlines (main: advisory); advisory still fires for a real allowlisted reference with or without a trailing newline, with no finding. title: GH#38089: perf(dispatch): single-pass jq extraction in footprint in-flight rebuild
body:
## Summary

`_footprint_refresh_inflight_cache` re-parsed the whole in-flight issue JSON array 4 times per issue (number, body, parent-task flag, status:claimed flag). For a repo with about 80 in-flight enrichment briefs (1.2 MB), that is about 394 MB of JSON parsed per rebuild. Because the 30 s cache TTL is shorter than a rebuild under load, and each dispatch candidate runs in its own subshell, every candidate paid this cost. `dedup.footprint` took 50–76 s per candidate on a loaded runner, even after GH#38055.

This change emits one TSV row per issue from a single `jq` pass (number, parent-task flag, status:claimed flag, base64 body) and reads it in the current shell. The parent-task skip, the GH#36817 claimed-evidence check, the GH#38055 open-PR memo and the cache variables are unchanged. Issues without a number are filtered in `jq`; they contributed nothing before either.

## Verification

- Frozen live snapshot (79 in-flight issues, 62 open PRs; `gh` and `_footprint_fetch_active_issues` stubbed to the snapshot), old module vs new module:
  - cache output identical: sha256 prefix `2ff1e4bb852c401a`, 101 `path|issue` entries in both
  - rebuild 5915 ms → 1521 ms
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`: 56 run, 0 failed (includes parent-task exclusion, claimed-evidence, PR memo, in-process cache TTL and repo isolation cases)
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`: clean; pre-commit Bash 3.2 parse check passed

Out of scope (noted in the issue): cache TTL and cross-subshell cache sharing, since both change staleness semantics relative to GH#32977 reservations.

Resolves #38089

title: GH#38095: fix(pulse-dispatch): surface why cleanup-receipt reconciliation refused worktree pre-creation
body:
## Summary

Pulse skipped dispatch for three issues, and pulse.log recorded only `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_LIFECYCLE_DISPOSITION=RECONCILIATION_FAILED`. A merge's receipt write also hit `receipt-lock-timeout (holder 51312, held 85s)`, and that holder had exited before anyone could identify it. This PR makes both failures self-explaining.

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`
  - New `_full_loop_receipt_holder_command`: on a lock timeout with a live holder, records the holder's executable basename plus, for an interpreter, its script basename (for example `bash full-loop-helper.sh`). Argument values are never kept, since they may carry credentials. Output is restricted to a safe charset and capped at 80 chars, so no local paths or argv values reach logs.
  - New `_full_loop_receipt_lock_failure_detail`: used by the supersede refusal (which previously dropped the reason entirely) and by `cleanup-receipt-failure:`.
  - `_FULL_LOOP_RECEIPT_LOCK_FAILURE` keeps its format, so the test pin and the merge-cleanup `receipt-lock-timeout*` retry prefix still hold.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`: `_dlw_precreate_helper_reason` now ranks `Cleanup-receipt reconciliation refused:` above the generic disposition, as GH#36142 did for enrollment refusals.

## Evidence

- Receipt scans under the lock are not the slow path: three passes over 5,107 live receipts take about 0.16 s each. A long holder exists elsewhere, and this change makes it identifiable the next time it happens.
- Ad-hoc verification against a live `sleep 30` lock holder:
  - supersede stderr: `Cleanup-receipt reconciliation refused: could not acquire the receipt lock: receipt-lock-timeout (holder 83253, held 1s) holder-cmd=sleep`
  - `_dlw_precreate_helper_reason` returns that line instead of the generic disposition.
  - A holder started as `bash <tmp>/fake-helper.sh --token=<value> <bare-value>` is summarised as exactly `bash fake-helper.sh` (CodeRabbit finding, fixed in 6878589d6c).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`: all PASS, exit 0 (macOS).
- `test-worktree-add-managed-symlink-base.sh` uses the Linux `pulse-cgroup-v1` backend. On macOS it fails identically on unmodified `main` (`FileNotFoundError` in native create), so Linux CI is the authority for it.
- ShellCheck is clean; pre-commit ratchets pass, including the Bash 3.2 parse check.

Resolves #38098.

- Add an isolated, bounded Darwin pulse stage for trusted same-repository PRs labelled needs-macos-verification.
- Use owned detached scratch worktrees at exact head SHAs, persistent attempts and deduplicated failure diagnostics.
- Keep dispatch-engine integration to one source line and one stage registration; document automatic and manual paths.

## Files and reference patterns

`.agents/scripts/pulse-macos-verification.sh` uses the async launcher from `pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh` and the sanctioned `scratch-worktree-helper.sh` creation/removal path. `macos-local-checks.sh` adds suite diagnostics. `.agents/reference/platform-support.md` describes operation.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — orchestration exercised on Linux using synthetic API/Git/scratch/suite inputs; this does not claim native Darwin suite execution.
- Exact verified head: `d52dac3a2f0013c5788fe0e0cdc59533d4014177`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-macos-local-checks.sh`: passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh`: passed (13 checks). One combined verification invocation exceeded its 60-second tool budget; isolated bounded rerun passed in 15.4 seconds.
- Bash syntax and pre-commit ShellCheck/quality ratchets: passed.
- 31 synthetic production-function scenarios passed: exact-SHA required checks, absent required contexts, app mismatch, classic protection and active rulesets, unknown/fork/untrusted skips, head-change rejection, one attempt per cycle, persisted success/failure, guarded cleanup, comment deduplication/40-line cap, identity/duplicate registration and one-second timeout.
- Three additional helper scenarios passed: stale no-sensitive label reconciliation, post-removal API-failure label restoration and named failing-suite diagnostics.
- Live read-only API queries validated the installed GitHub GraphQL fields and active-rules endpoint. Final independent review found no remaining blocking defect.

## Regression Evidence

No new repository test file is added. Regression coverage is the 31 synthetic production-function scenarios above plus the existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-macos-local-checks.sh` and `test-scratch-worktree-helper.sh` suites, which pass. Native Darwin suite execution cannot be automated on Linux CI; the pulse stage itself performs it on macOS.

## Decisions

- Required checks are evaluated at the immutable SHA and matched against classic branch-protection and active/inherited ruleset requirements, including app identity. Missing contexts, unknown rollups, truncated rollups and unsupported required-workflow rules fail closed.
- The existing isolated async launcher protects dispatch budget; a portable advisory lock prevents overlapping runs. Coreutils deadlines escalate to KILL after a five-second cleanup grace; stock Darwin uses the shared process-group timeout fallback.
- Controlled scratch creation declares this verifier's PID/session and uses the existing guarded non-force removal path. No canonical reset or direct worktree-add command is introduced.
- Failed/interrupted heads are not executed again. Failure-comment delivery can retry without rerunning PR code. Manual verification remains available.
- Engine changes are exactly one source line and one stage registration; no pulse-wrapper changes. Only the four authorized files are changed.

## Limitations

Native Darwin execution is unavailable on this Linux runner. The pre-push hook deferred TypeScript typecheck to CI because the existing development dependencies are absent; no TypeScript files changed.

title: GH#38101: perf(dispatch): time each dedup layer-4 PR-evidence step
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of GH#38101. Records dedup.layer4.<check> sub-stages in dispatch-stages.tsv for each of the six parallel has_open_pr checks (healthy_sibling, open_commits, open_body_keyword, merged_keywords, task_id_title, superseded_issue_pr), the whole parallel block (parallel_checks), the helper process seen from the dispatcher (has_open_pr), and the post-evidence routing (revised_checkpoint, stalled_checkpoint). Timing turns on only when the dispatcher has the stage recorder loaded and hands the helper AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_STAGE_ISSUE/REPO; every other caller runs exactly as before. The parallel launcher moved into _has_open_pr_run_checks so has_open_pr stays under the 100-line function gate. Why phase 1 only: on 2026-11-13 dedup.layer4_pr_evidence for candidates that passed layer 4 (helper call only, no routing) had p50 8.4 s and p90 45.9 s over n=276, yet the same helper run directly takes about 1.0-1.6 s end to end and each check finishes in about 1.4 s or less (live samples: allow case open_commits 793 ms, parallel block 811 ms; block case merged_keywords 1389 ms, parallel block 1413 ms). The production tail therefore comes from contention during pulse cycles, not from one slow query, so serving one check from the prefetched snapshot is not yet justified. The deployed sub-stages will show whether the time sits in helper startup, a specific check, or transport waits; phase 2 acts on that data.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh

## Decisions

Routing steps run through a current-shell wrapper, not a subshell, so _DEDUP_STALLED_CHECKPOINT_SIGNAL and other globals still propagate. The snapshot fallback from the brief step 2 is deferred to phase 2 until the deployed data names a dominant cost.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — shellcheck -x clean on both files. test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh 47/47, test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh 70/70. test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh 10/11 and test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh 37/38: the same single failures reproduce on unchanged main c87f35c4f5, so they predate this change. title: GH#38026: fix: cap the 5% free-space floor at 50 GiB and add a read-only Time Machine snapshot hint
body:
## Summary

The worktree admission gate required 5 GiB and 5% free. The 5% floor grew without bound, so a ~2 TB APFS volume needed ~100 GiB free and every worker slot idled with 80 GiB available. The percentage floor is now capped at 50 GiB (AIDEVOPS_MIN_WORKTREE_FREE_PERCENT_CEILING_KB); volumes up to 1 TB keep identical behaviour and the 5 GiB absolute floor and quota logic are unchanged. When the gate blocks on macOS, a read-only advisory names Time Machine local snapshots (whose blocks df excludes) and the owner's supported reclaim path; aidevops never thins or deletes backups. Pulse emits the hint once per process; worktree add prints it to stderr.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/throughput-throttling-policy.md, .agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-disk-capacity-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh

## Decisions

Ceiling (not purgeable-space accounting): counting snapshot blocks as free would trust an OS reclaim promise inside a fail-closed gate. Ceiling default 50 GiB equals 5% of 1 TB so smaller volumes are unaffected. Ceiling also bounds an operator-raised percentage; raise the ceiling variable to restore pure-percentage behaviour. The 15% cleanup trigger is intentionally unchanged because cleanup reclaims rather than restricts.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified on macOS (APFS, 4 real local snapshots): forced block prints the advisory, tmutil snapshot count unchanged 4->4, no hint when admission passes, default check on a 3.9 TB volume uses the 50 GiB capped floor. test-disk-capacity-lib.sh 18/18 (new rows: 2000 GiB/80 GiB admits, 2000 GiB/40 GiB blocks; existing 1000 GiB/40 GiB still blocks). test-pulse-dispatch-worktree-cap-cleanup.sh passes. shellcheck clean on all touched scripts. test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh and test-codegraph-worktree-init-helper.sh fail identically on unmodified main (pre-existing, unrelated).

Resolves #38026

title: GH#38111: fix(dispatch): restore For precedence in checkpoint linkage; repair drifted stale-recovery fixtures
body:
## Summary

Issue #37915 widened worker checkpoint linkage to inline For/Ref references, but it also merged the For and Ref sets. A canonical commit-and-pr checkpoint body (one standalone For line plus the parent under ## Related as a Ref line) therefore became ambiguous, so continuation rejected it while has-open-pr still blocked ordinary redispatch, the same deadlock issue #37915 set out to remove. This restores For precedence (Ref only counts when no For reference exists) and keeps the inline word-bounded matching. It also repairs four drifted test expectations: two bare-mention fixtures that now contain an explicit inline reference, an ambiguous-linkage fixture whose second issue had no keyword, and a no-worker liveness fixture that hit the unreadable-comments input-circuit fail-closed path (stubs extracted to a helper to keep the test under the 100-line function limit).

## Decisions

Kept inline matching (issue #37915 Option A) and only restored precedence, because the framework's own checkpoint body shape (issue #36864) puts a related parent Ref beside the For line. A body naming two For issues stays ambiguous. has-open-pr still matches any explicit reference, so a Ref-only related issue or an ambiguous two-For draft can still be blocked by dedup while continuation rejects it; that alignment is filed as a separate follow-up rather than widened here.

title: GH#38107: feat(reclaim): observe owners through the lifecycle registry, retire idle review trees
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of the Reclaim subsystem (parent #38051). Reclaim no longer scans `/proc` to find worktree owners; it reads them from the lifecycle registry, which was built for that purpose.

- **New `reclaim/owners.py`** (read-only): opens `LifecycleRegistry` and a ready `ProcessAdapter` once per pass. For each candidate, `GenerationEnrollment.inspect_retirement` → generation runs (`cleanup_plan._runs`) → `adapter.observe` for every run not recorded as ended. Refusals: `owner-alive`, `owner-unobservable`, `owner-not-enrolled`, `owner-registry-unreadable`. If the registry or adapter is unusable, every candidate refuses with `owner-observation-unavailable`.
- **`evidence.py`**: `Census` replaced by the owner check. Order is unchanged: GitHub first, and the registry is read only for finished candidates.
- **Review-tree rule** (new `reclaim/review.py`; decision recorded in https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38107#issuecomment-6860246995). A `<repo>-pr<N>-review-<slug>` tree whose PR is confirmed `OPEN` qualifies as `review-idle` only when all of these hold: Git `HEAD`/index have been idle ≥ 2 h, no live registered owner, and `nothing_to_lose` passes (no changes, no unpushed commits). An unknown PR state still refuses. `ci-repair-prNNN` and worker trees are unaffected.
- **`host.py`**: `Census`, `process_census`, `_arguments` and `_live_same_user` are removed. `remove()` re-reads owners immediately before deletion and refuses with `owners-appeared`.
- **`sweep.py`**: adds `--state-dir`. The receipt drops `unplaceable_processes` and gains `residual_risk: unregistered-processes-unobserved` plus `owner_observation: registry|unavailable`.
- **`pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`**: passes the state dir already resolved by `worker_lifecycle_state_dir`.
- **`.agents/reference/worktree-registry.md`**: documents the registry contract and the remaining risk.

Out of scope (later phases of #38051): decision journal/CAS, the archive stage, removal of `legacy_*`, `decide_cleanup`, `cleanup_authorized`.

## Verification

- `uvx ruff@0.11.13 check --no-cache`: all checks passed.
- `uvx mypy@1.15.0 --config-file mypy.ini --platform linux` and `--platform darwin`: no issues in 59 files.
- `python3 -B .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reclaim.py -v`: 43 tests OK. Existing census tests were adapted to owner checks; review-rule and `owners-appeared` cases were added to the same file, with no new infrastructure.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`: clean.
- `rg -i "census|/proc" .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim`: no matches.
- Live dry run on a busy host (real registry, no `--apply`): scanned 92, authorized 26 (9 `work-finished`, 17 `review-idle`), refused 66, `owner_observation: registry`. Review trees with unpushed commits or activity in the last 2 h were refused.
- Read-only owner probe over 89 worktrees: 10 `owner-alive`, 1 `owner-not-enrolled`, 1 `owner-registry-unreadable`, 77 without a live owner, 13.8 s total.

Resolves #38107

title: GH#38138: fix(gh): expire orphaned single-flight lease.reclaim markers

## Summary

A reclaimer killed inside the lease.reclaim critical section left the marker forever, so every reclaim of that key failed and each follower waited the full 10 s single-flight timeout before fetching anyway. The reclaim marker is now age-gated: a fresh marker (live reclaimer) is preserved; one older than AIDEVOPS_GH_SINGLEFLIGHT_RECLAIM_GRACE_SECONDS (default 10) is expired and the reclaim retried once, with a reclaim-marker-expired coordination record. title: GH#38142: perf(dispatch): cache layer-4 PR-evidence blocks across cycles
body:
## Summary

Layer-4 PR evidence (approved/mergeable open PR, PR commits targeting the issue, closing keyword in a PR body, non-worker draft, merged PR reference) previously printed nothing, so dispatch logged it as dedup_active_claim. That reason is ignored on an empty local pool for self-owned issues (GH#37780) and is never cached for unassigned issues, so the same unchanged PR-held issues re-ran the 50-120 s pre-launch ceremony every round (about 5,400 candidate-slot seconds in 16 h on the maintainer host). _dedup_layer4_pr_evidence now prints `pr_evidence_block: <evidence>` on the non-worker block path; classify_dispatch_blocker_reason maps that prefix to the new dedup_pr_evidence reason (benign block + stats registries, diagnostics inventory). _dispatch_cache_confirmed_block records it only when the evidence names exactly one PR; the record fingerprints that PR (state, merged_at, draft, updated_at, head SHA) through one bounded REST read. _dispatch_negative_cache_reason honours it only while the issue updatedAt is unchanged, the 1800 s TTL holds, and the live PR fingerprint still matches (_dispatch_pr_evidence_hint_valid); it skips the owner-label gate and the empty-pool recheck, which only apply to claims. The owner-gate exemptions now live in one helper (_dispatch_negative_cache_self_validating_reason), and the exact-PR REST read is one shared helper (_dispatch_exact_pr_rest_json) used by all three fingerprint paths; this keeps the reader under the 100-line function limit.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh

## Decisions

Only evidence naming one exact PR is cached; anything else and every lookup failure falls back to the full ceremony. Worker drafts keep their existing worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked path. A mergeability change without an updated_at bump is the only uninvalidated change and is bounded by the 30-minute TTL. The zero-worker active-claim recheck strips only exact dedup_active_claim, so PR blocks no longer inflate the zero_worker_infrastructure_hold diagnostic.

Three cheap housekeeping scanners could not finish their work within the 12 s lane slice (`PULSE_HOUSEKEEPING_BUDGET_SECONDS / 24`, GH#37501). This PR makes each one make progress again or yield cleanly:

title: GH#38169: repair worker PR conflicts on-branch before close-and-redispatch
body:
## Summary

When gh pr update-branch cannot resolve a conflict on a worker-origin PR, the merge pass now dispatches one bounded on-branch repair worker (new pulse-merge-conflict-repair.sh) instead of closing the PR. The worker merges origin/<base> into the existing head (merge commit only, never rebase or force-push), resolves hunks preserving both sides, runs focused checks, fences the head before pushing, posts a resolution summary, and records mark-complete/mark-blocked. The PR stays open (rc 77) while the attempt is live. Attempts are deduplicated per head via trusted marker comments plus launcher state; a new head gets a fresh attempt up to PULSE_CONFLICT_REPAIR_MAX_ATTEMPTS (3). After PULSE_CONFLICT_REPAIR_TTL_SECONDS (2h), when the worker stops without advancing the head, or on launch failure, the route falls back unchanged to _dispatch_conflict_fix_worker, behind a fallback-time head fence. Interactive, external, no-takeover, hold-for-review and maintainer-held PRs keep today's behaviour (labels checked from router context and live PR). ## Summary

The post-merge review scanner had scanned no repository since 2026-11-09. Its per-repo setup (REST-core gate probe, merged-PR list, review-followup issue index) takes 6-28s before the first cursor write, so the 12s cheap housekeeping slice killed every run and repo.cursor resumed at the same repo forever. The stage now uses the 72s batch ceiling (as auto_decomposer_scanner does; explicit lower caller ceilings still win). repo.cursor line 2 counts consecutive interrupted starts: the count is raised before the child launches, reset on any return, and at AIDEVOPS_POST_MERGE_SCANNER_MAX_INTERRUPTED_STARTS (default 3) the repo is deferred to the next traversal with its PR cursor kept. title: GH#38200: perf(pulse): lead first waves with prefetch-visible new arrivals
body:
## Summary

Where the 554 s went: a census-fresh first-wave snapshot whose remainder was fully attempted fell through to a real re-enumeration. That rebuild keeps the original captured_at so the attempt ledger does not renew, and _dispatch_enumeration_served_snapshot therefore logged a real scan as sample=snapshot_hit. The freshness window was not the cause; the scan order was. Changes: (1) _dispatch_first_wave_arrival_repos (pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh) builds a zero-API hint from the issue prefetch cache. It counts open, unassigned auto-dispatch + status:available issues per repository whose entry is fresh (PULSE_FIRST_WAVE_ARRIVAL_HINT_MAX_AGE_S, default 1800 s, 0 disables) and newer than the census's last poll (pulse-last-per-repo.json). Issues with attempt-recency stamps, and issues already held by the first-wave snapshot or its ledger, are left out. (2) _dispatch_repository_rows puts arrival repositories first, then the GH#38022 backlog, then plain rotation. Lead repositories no longer move the rotation cursor (new helper _dispatch_first_wave_note_polled), so GH#33647 fairness holds for quiet repositories. (3) When a fresh remainder is smaller than the free slots and a pollable arrival repository exists (schedule and interval gates checked), the wave re-enumerates instead of serving it, and the remainder is merged back. Each re-census polls those repositories, which clears their hint until the next prefetch, so the refresh cannot loop. (4) Snapshots record enumerated_at, so re-enumerations count as census samples rather than snapshot reads. (5) pulse-health.json gains first_wave_new_arrival_lead: per-cycle events of that pulse-stats counter; each lead is also logged as 'First-wave new-arrival lead: repo=... launchable=...'. Scope: pulse-logging.sh was added to the issue's Files Scope before editing, with evidence (integration scope recovery). pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh needed no change, because its existing cache already carries labels and assignees.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh: passes. title: GH#38211: perf(pulse): gate supervisor/refill/recycle on the fresh candidate census
body:
## Summary

The LLM supervisor launch (`_compute_initial_underfill`), active-pulse refill and early-exit recycle gates now use the cycle's fresh dispatch candidate census to count runnable work. Before this change they re-ran `count_runnable_candidates`, an all-repository enumeration that reconciles conversation locks and normalizes dependencies in every pulse repo. On 2026-11-14 one supervisor launch spent about 20 minutes in that count while the 20-slot pool sat at 0 workers. The delay also pushed the activated bundle's first cycle past the drain handoff's reuse window, so the 107-candidate census handed across the drain (GH#38048) was discarded as `stale_or_invalid`.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`: new `_dispatch_snapshot_runnable_count`. It is read-only and checks the cycle snapshot, the drain handoff (with a schema check) and the first-wave partial in both dependency-normalization modes. For each snapshot it applies the existing freshness rule (`_dispatch_candidate_snapshot_is_fresh` + `_dispatch_enumeration_expected_seconds`) and the consumed-attempt ledger. Cross-cycle censuses also get the first-wave registry/schedule recheck. It prints the largest unconsumed count with its source, and returns 1 when no fresh census holds candidates.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`: new `_pulse_gate_runnable_count`, which uses the snapshot count when it is positive and logs `Runnable gate (<caller>): census_snapshot count=N source=<wave>:<mode> (GH#38211)`. Otherwise it falls back to the original `count_runnable_candidates`. It replaces the four gating call sites.

Safety: these gates only decide whether to run `run_underfill_worker_recycler` / `dispatch_max`. `dispatch_max` keeps its own census and every live dispatch gate. Snapshots are never adopted, consumed or invalidated by the count. When no snapshot exists, a snapshot is stale or has a foreign schema, or snapshots are disabled (`PULSE_DISPATCH_CANDIDATE_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED=0`), the broad count still runs, so failing-PR and cold-cache behaviour does not change.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` clean on both files; the pre-commit ratchets (returns, positional params, string literals, bash 3.2 parse) pass.
- Existing suites, all exit 0: `test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh`, `test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh`.
- Throwaway smoke run (not committed) that sources the engine in an isolated HOME. All 7 cases pass:
  - No snapshot falls back to the broad count.
  - A cycle snapshot of 3 with 1 consumed gives 2.
  - A handoff-only census gives `1 handoff:normalize`: the registry filter drops the unknown repo and the file is left in place.
  - A foreign-schema handoff falls back.
  - An expired handoff falls back.
  - With snapshots disabled, the count falls back.
- Runtime check after deploy: the next supervisor launch logs `Runnable gate (supervisor_launch): census_snapshot ...`. The gap between `LLM supervisor: daily sweep due` / starvation-escape and `LLM supervisor attempt started` should fall from about 20 minutes to seconds.

Resolves #38211

title: t18986: fix(dispatch): planning-publication PRs are not open-PR dedup evidence (GH#38217)
body:
## Summary

When an interactive session creates an issue, `claim-task-id.sh` and `planning-commit-helper.sh` open a planning-publication PR. That PR has a `planning/*` head and only adds the TODO entry, under a title of the form `<task-id>: plan: ... (GH#N)`. `_has_open_pr_check_open_commits` matched the `GH#N` in that title and returned `dedup_pr_evidence`. Dispatch of the new issue was then blocked until the TODO PR merged.

Evidence from `pulse.log` on 2026-11-14:

```
Dedup: open PR #38216 has commits targeting issue #38215
DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_pr_evidence ... issue=#38215
Dispatch_max: dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=1 for #38215 elapsed_ms=68949
```

#38216 was the TODO-only planning PR for #38215. Dispatch was held for about 19 minutes, and each blocked attempt cost about 69 s. This happens to every interactively created auto-dispatch issue.

## Changes

`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`:

- `_ddpr_graphql_open_commits` now also fetches `headRefName`, `changedFiles` and the first 10 `files` with their pagination flag. These are optional evidence, not validated, so existing fixtures and responses stay valid. Absent evidence maps to "not exempt".
- `_has_open_pr_check_open_commits` gains a jq `planning_publication` predicate. A PR is excluded only when all of these hold:
  - its head is `planning/*`
  - it has a complete, non-truncated file list
  - the list length equals `changedFiles`
  - every path is `TODO.md` or under `todo/`
- The title is never used for the exemption (review follow-up). A `planning/*` PR that touches code, has truncated or absent file evidence, or has no `headRefName` is still evidence.

This mirrors the existing `complete_planning_only_scope` exclusion in the approved-or-mergeable sibling check.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` reports nothing.
- These suites pass: `test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh`, `test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`, `test-dispatch-dedup-fail-closed.sh`, `test-dispatch-dedup-gh-call-budget.sh`, and the other `test-dispatch-dedup-*.sh` suites.
- A local scratch harness drives `_has_open_pr_check_open_commits` through both the live projection (stubbed GraphQL read) and the snapshot path. All 8 cases pass:
  - live TODO-only planning PR: excluded
  - live `planning/` PR with code: still blocks
  - live `planning/` PR without file evidence: still blocks
  - snapshot planning-only PR: excluded
  - snapshot planning PR with truncated files: still blocks
  - snapshot `planning/` PR with code: still blocks
  - implementation PR: still blocks
  - PR with no `headRefName`: still blocks

body:
## Summary

Two changes so a cooperatively drained cycle's full census (GH#38048) survives until the activated bundle's first wave. (1) pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh: _dispatch_hand_off_candidate_snapshots stamps handed_off_at on the handoff; _dispatch_candidate_snapshot_is_fresh accepts a stamped census while now - handed_off_at < max(ttl, census_seconds) and now - captured_at < 2 x that window (hard cap); handed_off_at must lie between capture and now. An exhausted first-wave rebuild carries handed_off_at with the preserved captured_at. Unstamped snapshots keep the capture-based rule. (2) pulse-wrapper.sh: the GH#38162 drain starvation escape is deferred once via PULSE_DIR/llm_drain_escape_deferred, so the drained cycle exits without the ~15 min supervisor run; the next cycle evaluates the supervisor after its dispatch pipeline (normal path logs the deferred escape; a second drained cycle runs the escape itself). Delay is bounded at one cycle; PULSE_LLM_DRAIN_ESCAPE_DEFER=0 restores the immediate escape. dispatch_candidate_handoff_adopted/_discarded already exist as pulse-stats.json counters (pulse-stats-helper.sh), so pulse-health.json was not widened (outside Files Scope). Option 3 (skipping drained-cycle housekeeping) lives in pulse-dispatch-engine-housekeeping.sh, outside Files Scope, and was not needed for the incident timeline once the supervisor no longer runs first.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh

title: GH#38226: perf(pulse): lead new arrivals and bound census latency
body:
## Summary

Resolves #38226. Recovers both commits from #38208 on current main, preserving the newer runnable-census and drain-handoff integration.

- Lead first waves with zero-API prefetch-visible new arrivals while preserving quiet repositories' relative rotation.
- Refresh short first-wave snapshots when pollable arrivals are absent; retain known candidates even if refresh fails, subject to a renewed freshness check.
- Exclude expired snapshots from arrival hints and emit `first_wave_new_arrival_lead` from cycle counter events in `write_pulse_health_file`.
- Bound repository enumeration to 15 seconds and total census enumeration to 180 seconds by default. Stop all-empty scans too, retain partial candidates, and rotate full censuses separately so their unscanned tail remains reachable.
- Supervise the whole enumeration process group, including descendants retaining stdout after their adapter exits.

## Latency diagnosis and decisions

The exhausted-snapshot rebuild path preserved `captured_at` for attempt-ledger expiry. The old timing classifier inspected that retained timestamp, incorrectly classifying real enumeration as `snapshot_hit`. The regressions reproduce this path. A separate `enumerated_at` now dates real scans without renewing ledger expiry. This is a reproduced enumeration/misclassification explanation for the reported 554-second sample, not forensic proof of that historical run: this worker has no historical runner trace attributing all 554 seconds to scan, lock wait or prepass.

The budget controls are `PULSE_REPO_ENUMERATION_BUDGET_S` and `PULSE_CENSUS_ENUMERATION_BUDGET_S`; a smaller positive first-wave budget is also honored. All live schedules, interval throttles and dispatch gates remain binding. No deployment or release is requested or performed.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Testing level: runtime-verified for the changed dispatch paths.

- PASS: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` — 70 repositories, consumed product snapshot, 15 new arrivals, inverse rotation case, real process-tree timeout, empty-census deadline/rotation, failed-refresh fallback.
- PASS: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh` — snapshot reuse/expiry and a 107-candidate drain handoff served next wave without re-enumeration. The suite emits an existing `_pulse_ram_available_mb: command not found` diagnostic but exits 0.
- PASS: `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`, including complexity, nesting, Bash 3.2 portability and secret checks. Pre-commit hooks pass.
- PARTIAL / pre-existing failure: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh` successfully exercises the real health writer and lifecycle assertions, then exits 1 at line 607 in the foreign supervisor-lease fixture. The trace shows `_instance_lock_publication_age` returning age 0 for a fresh marker despite foreign LLM ownership; `_handle_existing_lock` consequently returns 1 rather than reclaiming. Both the test and `.agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh` are unchanged from `origin/main`; `git blame` attributes the fixture to `21d6adcfc2` and current instance-owner check to `ac961ad9ec`. Repair is outside this issue's scope.
- Local-tool limitation: direct `shellcheck` reports that its wrapper cannot find the real binary, although the local aggregate linter reports six files passed. Actual ShellCheck verification is left to `Code Quality Analysis / ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)`; no claim of a local binary run is made. The push hook likewise defers unavailable TypeScript dev-dependency validation to CI; no TypeScript files change here.

The rebase performed during PR finalization leaves all six changed target files byte-identical to the locally tested implementation. Independent review findings about descendant cleanup and failed-refresh retention were repaired; fallback freshness is rechecked after refresh failure.

## Acceptance and rollout

Code/regression criteria are implemented, including the 107-candidate reuse and health-stat paths. The whole cycle-state suite is not green because of the documented unchanged lease-recovery failure. Historical attribution of every second of the 554-second sample remains unverified beyond the reproduced timing-classification defect.

Live many-repository utilization within two cycles is **not yet verified** and remains a post-rollout observation: confirm `candidates >= min(free slots, new issues)`, inspect `first_wave_new_arrival_lead`, and compare active workers with their target. This PR does not publish or operate a live runner.

## Files Scope

Only the dispatch engine, candidate/capacity libraries, health writer, and the two issue-scoped regression suites change. The cycle-state test and instance-lock implementation are read-only reference evidence.

title: GH#38229: fix: torn audit line no longer blocks gh-audit anomaly scanning
body:
## Problem

One interrupted append to `gh-audit.log` permanently disabled GH audit anomaly scanning
on the affected runner.

`gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan` treated any unparsable line in its window as a reason to
abort and hold its checkpoint. With a torn line inside the window, every run replayed the
same corrupt window and refused to advance, so no later audit event was ever checked for
suspicious signals.

Observed before the fix (runner `alex-solovyev`, 2026-11-14):

```text
$ gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh status
Log lines:  12471
Last scan:  2026-10-31T09:03:28Z
Last line:  9511
Unscanned:  2960 entries

$ gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan --dry-run
[GH-ANOMALY] Scanning 2960 entries (Lines 9512–12471 of `gh-audit.log`)
[GH-ANOMALY WARN] Malformed audit NDJSON detected — checkpoint not advanced
[GH-ANOMALY WARN] Audit scan aborted without updating state
```

Cause: line 9605 held a truncated record (`{"ts":"2026-10-31T18`) with no trailing
newline, immediately followed on the same physical line by a complete later event. One
partial append plus the missing newline merged two events into one unparsable line, and
the checkpoint then stood still for 14 days.

## Changes

`.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh`

- New `_cmd_scan_partition_parsable()` writes only parsable NDJSON objects to the filter
  input and records the unparsable count in `_sc_malformed_count`.
- Malformed lines are reported, not suppressed: the report gains a `**Malformed lines:**`
  header field and a `## Log Integrity` section with the locate command and the
  write-fault vs tampering distinction. A window with only malformed lines still files an
  alert, titled `GH Audit Log Integrity Alert`.
- Fail-closed is kept where it belongs: `return 1` now happens only when the
  expected-transition filter fails on parsable records. `gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq` is
  unchanged, so no suppression decision is loosened.
- Issue rendering moved to `_cmd_scan_report_findings()` to keep `cmd_scan` under the
  function-length gate.

`.agents/scripts/gh-audit-log-helper.sh`

- New `_gh_audit_append_line()` writes a separating newline when the log's last byte is
  not one (detected via command substitution stripping trailing newlines) and warns that
  it repaired an unterminated line.
- New `_gh_audit_append_event()` wraps the append in `flock` when available, so concurrent
  audit writers cannot interleave. Without `flock` the newline repair still applies.

`.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md`

- Documents the malformed-line reporting contract, the append-only recovery rule (never
  edit the log to "repair" a torn line), and the locate command.

## Policy change

`test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh` previously asserted that malformed NDJSON
must fail the scan closed and must not advance the checkpoint. That is reversed here with
an explanatory comment: holding the checkpoint on corruption is strictly worse than
reporting it, because it converts one bad line into indefinite loss of detection. A torn
line is itself an audit finding, so it is counted and alerted while the rest of the window
is still scanned.

## Verification

```text
$ shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh .agents/scripts/gh-audit-log-helper.sh
(clean)

$ .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh
PASS: verified lifecycle backlog 104 -> 4 alerts (96%); five filter negatives retained

$ .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-log-torn-append.sh
PASS: torn, clean, and concurrent audit appends stay parsable NDJSON

$ .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh
(all gates pass)
```

Against the real 12471-line log that previously aborted every run:

```text
[GH-ANOMALY] Scanning 12471 entries (Lines 1–12471 of `gh-audit.log`)
[GH-ANOMALY WARN] Malformed audit NDJSON: 1 unparsable line(s) reported, scan continues
[GH-ANOMALY] Found 2 anomalous entries
[GH-ANOMALY] Found 1 malformed audit line(s) — reported as a log-integrity finding
```

New test coverage: a window with a torn line plus a real anomaly reports both and exits 0;
a window with only a torn line reports 0 anomalies, 1 malformed line, and advances the
checkpoint to the end of the window; `record` against an unterminated log keeps both lines
parsable; eight concurrent `record` calls produce eight parsable lines.

Resolves #38229

title: GH#38234: fix(pulse-merge): treat check runs with conclusion+completed_at as terminal
body:
## Summary

After a GitHub Actions incident, GitHub can leave a finished check run with `status: in_progress`, even though the same record already has `conclusion: success` and a `completed_at` time. The pulse pre-merge snapshot counted these runs as active, so approved PRs that GitHub reports as `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` stayed open indefinitely. The log repeated `not ready (active=1, blocking_failures=0)` every cycle.

GitHub only sets a conclusion when a check run completes (supplying a conclusion forces `status: completed`). A conclusion together with `completed_at` is therefore terminal evidence. This PR makes the pulse use that evidence.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` `_pmrc_normalize_snapshot_checks_json`: a check run with a non-empty conclusion and a non-null `completed_at` now normalizes to `status: completed`. Its conclusion is still evaluated, so failure, cancelled and similar conclusions keep blocking.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh` `gh_pr_check_runs_rest`: the same normalization at the source, so branch-update and other consumers agree with the snapshot.

Runs that are really active have neither field set, so they stay `in_progress` or `queued`.

## Verification

- Live data: `gh api repos/<private>/commits/<head>/check-runs` with the new jq turned the stuck `Core Gate Summary` (`raw: in_progress, conclusion: success`) into `status: completed`.
- Probe of the normalizer: stale success → completed/success; real in-progress run (null conclusion) → in_progress; stale failure → completed/failure (still blocks); queued → queued.
- `shellcheck` passes on both files.
- These existing tests pass: `test-pulse-merge-preflight-snapshot.sh` (131), `test-pulse-merge-primary-first-diagnostics.sh` (14), `test-pulse-merge-stuck.sh` (85), `test-actions-queue-saturation.sh` (44), `test-shared-gh-wrappers-check-runs-outcomes.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-phantom-pending-checks.sh`, `test-gh-check-status-cache.sh`, `test-shared-gh-wrappers-checks-timeout.sh`, `test-pulse-nmr-approval.sh` and `test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing-cases.sh`.

title: GH#38240: archive terminal cleanup receipts
body:
## Summary

Resolves #38240

- Archive at most 128 old CLEANED receipts per housekeeping run, no more than hourly under the receipt lock; retain modes and leave malformed, recent and nonterminal receipts in the hot set.
- Resolve archived identities on canonical-path misses; serialize creation, migration and release updates against archival.

## Consumer audit

Recreated-path scans and their validators operate on the active hot set: absent old CLEANED history correctly yields no-history status 2. Reconciliation skips CLEANED receipts. Exact identity consumers use archive lookup on misses; creation and identity mutations are serialized with archival. title: GH#38248: fix(pulse-merge): stop human-gated retry hints starving merge-ready PRs
body:
## Summary

Stops human-gated PRs from starving merge-ready work in the pulse merge pass.

1. **No retry priority for human-gated PRs** (`_pmp_sort_prs_by_backlog_priority` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-backlog.sh`): a deferred retry hint only moves a PR to the front when it is not a draft and has no `hold-for-review` label.
2. **Human gates acknowledge the queue hint** (`_process_single_ready_pr` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`): when the list draft gate or the live draft/hold read in `_pm_gate_origin_authority` rejects the PR, the claimed dirty-queue hint finishes as handled (result 2). Before, it stayed due and was retried every cycle even though only a human could unblock it. Marking the PR ready, removing the hold, or the normal walk brings it back.
3. **No REST enrichment for drafts** (`_pmp_draft_enrichment_unneeded`): authoritative per-PR enrichment (`_pmp_prepare_pr_at_cursor`) and advisory backlog enrichment (`_pmp_prepare_enriched_pr_backlog`) skip list-draft PRs, because the evaluator and classifier reject drafts from list fields alone. Advisory mode still enriches worker-owned drafts, because duplicate consolidation scores them.
4. **Resume priority lane** (`_pmp_resume_cursor_with_priority_lane`): on cursor resume, up to `PULSE_MERGE_RESUME_PRIORITY_LIMIT` PRs before the cursor (default 2; 0 disables) go ahead of it if they are merge-ready now but this walk has not yet evaluated them merge-ready at that head. The walk keeps a `repo|number|head` record in `<cursor file>.lane-served`, cleared when the cursor clears or a new walk starts. Cursor writes and pauses during lane items keep the original resume item, so the walk never goes back over finished PRs. This changes order only; every gate still runs.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-backlog.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-cursor-resume.sh

title: GH#38261: fix(dispatch): make negative-cache reuse work for body-less candidates
body:
## Summary

PR #38241 (GH#38237) only reused a cached rejection hint when the stored material began with `body:`. Ranking candidates drop `body` unless they are consolidated (GH#35038), so in production the reuse path never fired and every coordination-comment bump re-ran the 60-85s dedup ceremony. This PR adds `_dispatch_negative_cache_load_source`, which returns body-bearing material from the candidate when it carries a body. Otherwise it makes one bounded `repos/{repo}/issues/{n}` REST read, memoised per repo#issue@updatedAt. Records use the read only when its `updated_at` equals the candidate's revision (`exact`), so a record never covers an edit its ceremony did not evaluate. Reads keep the cheap gate early and run the material and comment reads in the refresh step, after the TTL checks, so an expired hint costs no API call. Once refreshed, `cached == updatedAt`, so steady state makes no calls. Live-owner holds skip the read.

title: GH#38267: fix(full-loop): reclaim stale empty receipt-lock owner and publish owner atomically
body:
## Summary

Fixes a lock wedge in the full-loop cleanup receipts: an empty `owner` file left one host's receipt mutation lock stuck until someone deleted it by hand. While it was stuck, the governed merges of #38260 and #38262 both ended in `cleanup-receipt-failure: receipt-lock-timeout`, and both `adopt-merged-receipt` attempts were blocked.

Resolves #38267

## Root cause

`_full_loop_receipt_lock_acquire` checked liveness only for an owner file that parses as a numeric pid. `_full_loop_receipt_reclaim_stale_ownerless_lock` reclaimed only when no owner file existed. An empty owner file passed neither check. It came from the non-atomic `self_pid >owner` publication, which truncates the file and only writes after an `sh` fork, so a holder killed in between leaves 0 bytes. The existing ENOSPC branch covered only a write that failed, not a writer that was killed.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`
  - `_full_loop_receipt_owner_unparseable`: new helper. An owner file that is empty or has no leading decimal pid carries no liveness evidence.
  - The reclaim helper now also accepts a stale unparseable owner, dated by the owner file's own mtime under the existing `AIDEVOPS_FULL_LOOP_RECEIPT_LOCK_OWNERLESS_GRACE_SECONDS`.
  - Revalidation after electing `.reclaim` (`_full_loop_receipt_reclaim_still_valid`) requires the exact state seen before election. A missing owner must still be missing, which protects a holder that is publishing. An unparseable owner must still be unparseable and stale, which protects a legacy non-atomic writer, because truncation refreshes the mtime.
  - `_full_loop_receipt_lock_publish_owner`: new helper. It builds `pid start` in `${receipt_dir}/.mutation.lock.owner.<pid>` and renames it into the lock dir with `mv -f`. A writer killed mid-publication now leaves an ownerless lock, which can be reclaimed, instead of an empty owner. On failure it removes the temp file, the owner file and the lock dir, and keeps `receipt-lock-owner-write-failed`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`: four new cases (fresh empty owner protected, stale empty owner reclaimed, stale garbage owner reclaimed, acquire over a stale empty owner publishing a parseable owner with no leaked temp file).

## Verification

```text
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh   → exit 0, all PASS, including the 4 new cases
                                                                  and the existing concurrent-publication guard
shellcheck -x full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh → clean
/bin/bash -n full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh                       → clean
pre-commit ratchets                                             → passed
```

## Compatibility

- The owner line format (`pid start`) is unchanged, so readers on older versions still parse it.
- A holder on an older version still has a millisecond window where its owner file is empty. Revalidation refuses to reclaim while that file's mtime is fresh.
- No migration is needed. A host that is already wedged recovers on its first acquire after deploy.

title: GH#38274: perf(pulse): adaptive per-repo census budget and single-pass lock reconciliation
body:
## Summary

Large repositories (700+ open issues) timed out at the fixed GH#38226 15s census bound on every census (9/9 for the main product repo, 48 rc=124 events across 15 repos), so they contributed zero candidates and pulse idled at workers 0/20 with ~140 dispatchable issues waiting. (1) pulse-dispatch-engine.sh: per-repository adaptive enumeration budget via new _dispatch_census_enumerate_repo. A timeout raises that repo's budget to PULSE_REPO_ENUMERATION_BUDGET_MAX_S (default 60); a completed scan decays it to max(base, 1.5x elapsed) and clears the override at base. The census-deadline clamp is now per call, so one escalated budget never leaks to later repos. New log lines: 'enumeration budget raised' and 'enumeration slow'. (2) pulse-dispatch-locks.sh: reconcile_auto_dispatch_issue_locks classifies every issue in one jq pass (measured 3.4s to 0.03s for 505 issues). Already-locked issues with a recorded marker are skipped, removing ~500 'Reused existing verified conversation lock' lines per cycle; fail-closed on unknown state is unchanged. (3) pulse-diagnose-issue.sh: a positional owner/repo was silently dropped and the cwd origin substituted, so the helper diagnosed an unrelated same-number item during this investigation. It now accepts the positional slug and rejects extra arguments. (4) test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh: stub the Darwin-only GH#38098 macOS verification launch so the test is host-independent; before this it exited at its first assertion on macOS and never reached the GH#38226 census checks. Adds escalation/decay/per-repo isolation coverage. Follow-up: #38275 (in-census dependency normalization double-fetch).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-issue.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-locks.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Read-only benchmark on the affected repo: snapshot 7.0-8.9s, batch lock read 1.9s, per-issue loop 3.4s vs single pass 0.03s. Tests, all rc=0: test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh (19 PASS incl. new adaptive budget block; previously failing on macOS main at the first-wave ordering assertion), test-auto-dispatch-conversation-lock.sh (31/0), test-pulse-candidate-enumeration-recovery, test-pulse-dispatch-core-planning-filter, test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring, test-pulse-campaign-shadow, test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection, test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot, test-pulse-wrapper-characterization, test-pulse-current-state-guardrails, test-precreation-failure-skip. ShellCheck clean on all touched files; pre-commit and complexity ratchets passed. Runtime: pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue 23633 <private-repo> now resolves the correct repository's open issue. Post-deploy check: rg 'Candidate repository enumeration (unavailable|budget raised|slow)' pulse.log.

Resolves #38274
