title: GH#38282: Measure collaborator memo effectiveness
body:
Resolves #38282

## Outcome

Successful collaborator permission lookups now share a private per-run memo
across command substitutions and the merge routine's child shells. The live
candidate measurement meets the issue's **distinct-pair evidence alternative**;
the earlier quota blocker is cleared for this validation.

## Implementation and decisions

- `shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`: preserve process-only behavior when
  the optional file is unset. Shared files must be owned regular non-symlink
  files physically under the temp root; only valid successful verdicts are
  stored. Failed/deferred and explicitly routed retry/fallback calls remain
  outside the memo wrapper's cache path.
- `pulse-merge-routine.sh`: create fresh mode-600 memo/stats files in a private
  scratch directory after lock acquisition, export paths, log hit/miss and
  distinct-miss totals, and clean up through the existing EXIT lifecycle.
- No cross-run TTL cache: the next run must observe permission changes.
- Preserve the original draft instrumentation and mirrored cache/standalone
  coverage. This continuation changes only the durable measurement note;
  temporary diagnostics were removed and all implementation files match the
  previously verified head exactly.

## Live candidate evidence

Normal quota admission and the normal routine lock were used. The live
target-repo dry-run completed at **2026-11-15T01:40:11Z–01:44:02Z**, exit 0:

```text
collab_memo hits=0 misses=3
collab_memo distinct_miss_keys=3
```

The matching API-ledger window contains exactly three
`collaborator-permission-rest` attempts, all HTTP 200. The observed run scratch
directory was absent after exit, confirming memo/stats cleanup.

All three remaining misses were distinct `(repo, login)` pairs, not repeated
misses in this run. There were no live hits: **this is not a demonstrated
30-minute production reduction or a claim of live API savings**. The mirrored
test independently proves substitution-plus-parent reuse makes one request
instead of two. No global installation or release was performed.

### Measurement scope correction

The existing `--repo` shortcut drops configured role/maintainer metadata, so
this non-owner runner conservatively skipped that synthetic entry. Its zero
samples were not used as evidence. The valid measurement used a private,
JSON-equality-verified copy of only the operator's existing target entry via
`REPOS_JSON`, the normal `--dry-run` path, and private cursor/checkpoint files.
Live permission checks and quota gates were not bypassed. The unrelated,
pre-existing shortcut defect has a scoped follow-up brief in the evidence
note; no additional issue was created under this bounded contract.

## Verification

- Repeated cache suite: 29 assertions pass, including unchanged unset-file
  behavior, one-request substitution reuse, failures/deferrals, unsafe paths,
  malformed stored values and fresh-run permission changes.
- Repeated standalone suite: 37/37 pass using
  `env -u AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE_DIR bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh`.
  Unsetting the worker's inherited absolute cache path restores the existing
  isolated-HOME test environment; no assertion was weakened.
- Configured markdownlint, whitespace and pre-commit checks pass for the note.
- Prior focused verification: timeout 9/9, approval guard 14/14, current-user,
  Bash syntax and portability checks pass; implementation is unchanged.
- Local ShellCheck binary is unavailable. Covering CI job: **Code Quality
  Analysis / ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)**, delegated under GH#34758, succeeded
  on the unchanged implementation. Bash 3.2 compatibility also succeeded.

Durable receipts, ledger epochs, failed-attempt history, measurement method and
the shortcut follow-up brief:
`todo/research/gh38282-collaborator-memo-measurement.md`.

title: GH#38273: feat(github-auth): surface App-read routing opportunity when PAT REST quota is the pulse ceiling

## Summary

When the maintainer PAT's REST-core quota is what stops the pulse (observed: cycles ending blocker=rest-core-quota at 0/5000), aidevops now says how much of that load an App read binding would carry, and which owners lack one. `aidevops github auth usage` gains an `app_routing_opportunity` object. A new offline `aidevops github auth advise [--since 24h] [--write-advisory]` writes or removes `~/.aidevops/advisories/github-app-read-routing.advisory` (share >= 0.5, REST-core min_remaining 0 or below the hard floor, at least one pulse owner without an App read route). The existing session-start advisory display shows its first line, and `aidevops security dismiss github-app-read-routing` suppresses it. Pulse refreshes it in the background at most once every 6h (`AIDEVOPS_GITHUB_APP_ADVISE_INTERVAL`), only when REST quota defers a progress stage. It is fail-open and never changes the stage's return code.



## Files Changed

## Decisions

Advisory-only and offline: no GitHub calls, no change to routing, auth, or pulse decisions. Repo slugs stay out of the advisory text, and owners appear only in local JSON/advisory output. The threshold uses the window's minimum REST remaining, so one exhaustion in 24h is enough. The 6h stamp is set before spawning the job, so a failing helper cannot retry on every cycle.

title: GH#38259: perf(pulse-merge): skip merge gates for heads parked by the review-thread worker
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of GH#38259, from the stage attribution added in #38260. Across 68 stage-attributed merge passes on 4 owners, the slowest PR's time was review_and_gates 29%, pre_merge 26%, admin_merge 18% and required_checks 11%. No CI-repair worktree stage appears, so the original hypothesis does not hold. admin_merge is almost entirely the final trust gate (admin_merge ~= trust_gate_s). 11 of the 13 passes that reached it merged nothing. The main cause was the final exact-head snapshot finding the same unresolved review-bot threads on heads the review-thread worker had already parked with maintainer_attention=true: 54 blocks, with PRs re-evaluated at 60-300s per cycle and 3 PRs stuck for 7-23h. A parked head now gets one 1-point GraphQL thread read (the existing `_pmrc_snapshot_review_threads_clear`) at the start of review_and_gates. If bot threads remain, the PR is skipped and marked human-gated. A new head, resolved threads, human-only threads or a failed read fall through to the unchanged full gates. title: GH#38291: fix(pulse-merge): finish interactive PRs left idle by a still-running session
body:
## Summary

Interactive PRs stalled indefinitely when their owning TUI session stayed alive but idle: the claim stamp and status label kept Gates 2/3 of _interactive_pr_is_stale closed, so pulse never handed them to workers and the user had to re-open sessions to finish them. (1) pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh dispatch-pr now defers origin:interactive PRs unless origin:worker-takeover is confirmed. (2) pulse-merge-conflict.sh adds a fail-closed idle-session evidence chain (claim stamp pid+worktree -> worktree registry owner -> bounded session-bus record: same pid, status=idle, idle >= AIDEVOPS_IDLE_SESSION_HANDOVER_SECONDS default 4h, not on this issue/PR) that lets a held claim yield; the owner session gets one non-waking bus notice on handover. (3) pulse-merge.sh routes review-thread blockers on interactive PRs through confirmed handover. (4) pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh gives takeover workers their own repair/review-pr-<n>-<head12> worktree at the verified head so the interactive owner's worktree is never touched; push target is HEAD:<pr head ref>. Session-gate logic extracted into _interactive_pr_session_gates, prompt takeover note into _prrts_append_takeover_worktree_note, keeping every function under 100 lines.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh, .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-dispatch.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-fixtures.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktrees.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing-cases.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh

title: t18997: feat(recovery): maintainer replies on held issues wake the AI supervisor; unexplained holds get a stated why
body:
## Summary

A hold-for-review issue had no wake path: a maintainer's answer changed nothing until someone launched an interactive session, and a hold could sit with no stated reason. This refused retirement spuriously and flaked the Worker Lifecycle Linux contract (run 43633794824). The thread listing, per-task inspection and per-fd reference checks now treat (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError) as vanished, keeping the existing exists() re-check so a still-present task fails closed.

Did not widen require_predating_daemon: it wraps all errors into ValueError and then defers to require_protected_references, which keeps its own fail-closed behaviour.

title: GH#38348: reclaim decision function, journaled authorization and evidence CAS (phase 3 of #38051)
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of #38051. `reclaim/decision.py` adds:

- `classify(verdict)`, which returns `remove`, `archive` or `refuse`.
- `fingerprint(path)`, a sha256 of the worktree directory's instance identity (`st_dev:st_ino`), HEAD, porcelain status and unpushed count. It is bounded by the live pass budget.
- Deterministic `uuid5` event IDs derived from the full canonical payload under the store installation.
- `record()`, which appends `reclaim-authorized` and `reclaim-removed` journal events through `LifecycleRegistry.connection(write=True)` and `append_event`.

The other changes:

- **`evidence.py`:** reports `finished=True` only for `work-finished` work once every registered owner has ended. Finished work whose only blocker is `uncommitted-changes` or `unpushed-commits-N` therefore classifies as `archive`: queued for phase 5, counted as `archive_queued`, and not refused. Unreadable state, open work (including idle review trees, whose PR is still open) and live owners stay `refuse`.
- **`sweep.py`:** takes the fingerprint *before* collecting evidence, and records a decision and fingerprint per result. With `--apply` it journals `reclaim-authorized` before removal. It then removes through a compare-and-swap verifier, which refuses with `evidence-changed` when the fingerprint moved after judgement started. Finally it journals `reclaim-removed`.
- **Fail-closed paths:** a missing journal, fingerprint or budget refuses removal, and journal errors never end the pass. Dry runs write nothing.
- **`journal.compact`:** archives reclaim events older than retention, archive-first, keeping digest tombstones so replays stay idempotent.

## Files Changed

.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reclaim.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/journal.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/decision.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/evidence.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/host.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/sweep.py

## Decisions

- `archive` requires the evidence pass to have proved the work finished (`work-finished`, not `review-idle`) and every owner ended. A live writer, an open issue or an open PR can therefore never reach it.
- Event IDs hash the whole payload. Changed reasons or references append a new event instead of colliding into a permanent `journal-conflict`, while an identical replay stays idempotent.
- The tree instance is part of the fingerprint, so a tree recreated at the same path never inherits an earlier instance's authorization. Reclaim events are new in this PR and unreleased, so no ID migration is needed.
- The CAS refusal is reported unprefixed as `evidence-changed`; `host._removal_blocked` otherwise prefixes `changed-`.
- Payloads carry no clock value, so replays match exactly; `recorded_at` already timestamps the row.
- A failed post-removal `reclaim-removed` write is surfaced as `verdict.journal` rather than hidden, since the tree is already gone.

## Review

- A fresh-context review of the blind packet (research-only agent) found two valid defects, both fixed: dirty `review-idle` trees could classify as `archive`, and `TypeError`/`RuntimeError` from the journal could escape the pass. A third finding, that the owner had no `store`, was a false positive: `RegisteredOwners.store` exists at `owners.py:60`.
- Three CodeRabbit threads were all valid, fixed in `fdc3c6ce1a` and resolved: the budget-bounded CAS, the tree-instance identity, and the fingerprint taken before judgement.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified. Evidence:
  - **Live dry run:** `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worktree-reclaim.py` against the real worktree base and lifecycle registry (`--limit 40`): `owner_observation=registry`, a decision on 40/40 results, 0 removals, no registry writes.
  - **Applied path:** exercised against real git worktrees and a real `LifecycleRegistry` in fixtures, not on production trees. title: t19009: GH#38358 fix(checkpoints): a failed continuation launch no longer holds a stalled draft for a maintainer
body:
## Summary

When Pulse's exact-head continuation of a stall-released worker draft fails to launch, the runtime releases with CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_not_launched. _pcc_stall_release_evidence then found no current stall release, blocked-attention posted BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION reason=worker_not_launched, and nothing re-armed the draft. A 2026-11-14 sample found 11 of 38 open BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION issues across the managed fleet held only for this reason, idle 2-23h (e.g. #38282 / draft #38284). Changes: (1) worker_not_launched joins _PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN (launch failure = runtime stall, no worker decision, head unchanged, like GH#36597). (2) _PCC_JQ_LAUNCH_DEFS unlaunched_episode also accepts the PR session's own worker_not_launched release, but only when its whole episode (from the in-session claim it closes) had no ready lease or Dispatching worker, so the earlier stall release stays current like GH#38103. (3) count_since and the per-PR release list skip transparent episodes so the failed-launch count is the only place each failed launch counts; the stall classification defs move to _PCC_JQ_STALL_DEFS to keep _pcc_stall_release_evidence under the 100-line function gate. (4) _PDCU_RELEASE_REASON_PATTERN keeps parity; its parity test now also strips the synthesized orphaned_terminal_lease (failing on main since GH#38236). (5) checkpoint-revision-recovery.md documents the reason (kept at the 500-line file-size limit). title: GH#38355: fix: closed worker checkpoint draft no longer strands its issue or resumes rejected work
body:
## Summary

A worker draft checkpoint removes auto-dispatch so no second branch opens beside the open draft. When that draft is closed unmerged, nothing restored dispatch (dispatch-stalled acts only on open drafts), and a later worker reusing the kept worktree resumed the rejected head. (1) pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh: once per fresh partial-continuation traversal, scan recently closed unmerged same-repo feature/auto-*-ghN PRs and restore auto-dispatch (status available; the checkpoint runner is released when it is the sole in-review assignee) only when the newest trusted ownership event is that PR's CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_draft_checkpoint, the PR is this issue's branch and was opened before and closed after the release, the newest auto-dispatch label event is the checkpoint's own removal (within an hour before the release), no hold or circuit-breaker marker exists, no other open PR references the issue, and no restore was recorded for this PR. Posts an ops audit comment. (2) pulse-dispatch-sealed-worktree.sh _dlw_reuse_head_rejected, called from _dlw_select_issue_worktree: a non-sealed reuse candidate ahead of the default branch whose HEAD is at or descends from a closed unmerged PR head on its branch (and no open PR on it) is skipped and preserved, so the launcher creates a fresh timestamped branch from the default.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-sealed-worktree.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh

## Decisions

Any closer counts, not only a maintainer: workers often share the maintainer's login, and the label removal's only reason (an open draft) is gone either way; explicit holds (no-auto-dispatch, hold-for-review, needs-*, lockdown, persistent, parent-task) and a person's own label removal are respected. Repeated-stall backoff in pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh is unchanged. The worktree fence skips rather than resets or removes, preserving dirty or extra commits (GH#27138); sealed generations keep their existing recovery path; unproven evidence keeps the existing reuse decision and is logged. Scan reads one page of 30 recently updated closed PRs per traversal with a 7-day lookback (PULSE_CLOSED_CHECKPOINT_LOOKBACK_SECONDS).

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh 214/214 (25 new closed-checkpoint cases: positive restore for any origin, in-review runner release, every hold label, replacement open PR, merged PR, wrong issue branch, PR closed before release, newer owner, other release reasons, recorded restore, person's later and mid-run label removal, never-labelled issue, unreadable timeline). test-precreation-failure-skip.sh 62/62 incl. a real-Git fence test (exact rejected head and later local commits are skipped and preserved; open, merged, no-PR and unreadable evidence keep same-runner resume; zero-ahead trees spend no GitHub read). title: GH#38376: reclaim cursor and repeat-unreadable quarantine (phase 4 of #38051)
body:
## Summary

Phase 4 of #38051. The reclaim sweep now persists a scan cursor in the lifecycle state dir (`reclaim-cursor`). When a pass is stopped by its budget or `--limit`, it records the last tree reached, and the next pass resumes after that tree, wrapping around. A slow head of the listing can no longer starve the tail.

A tree whose own local state is unreadable on two consecutive passes is deferred through a path-keyed `CleanupQuarantine`. The qualifying reasons are `repository-unknown`, `status-unreadable`, `unpushed-state-unreadable`, `owner-registry-unreadable`, `owner-unobservable` and `fingerprint-unavailable`. The quarantine lives in `reclaim-quarantine`, a separate file from admission cleanup. Backoff is exponential: 15 minutes, doubling, capped at one day. Any readable outcome clears the entry. Pass-wide `owner-observation-unavailable` and GitHub lookup failures are never deferred. Deferred trees are skipped before `--limit` applies.

Reference prefetch is capped at half the remaining pass budget, so a stalled batch cannot leave judgement without time to advance the cursor (CodeRabbit finding, fixed in `1bddf2dfb8`).

Dry runs honour the cursor and backoff but write neither. The receipt gains `quarantine_deferred`, `cursor_start` and `resume_after`. The Pulse log line now reports `deferred` and `resume_after`.

`CleanupQuarantine` gains a name, `deferred()`, `retain()` and an optional threshold. Admission-cleanup behaviour is unchanged (default threshold 1).

This changes scheduling only: nothing here can authorize a removal. Also filed #38381: retirement lock files are never removed (5,730 on this host).

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh, .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_reclaim.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_quarantine.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/progress.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/sweep.py

## Decisions

- **Threshold 2:** a single transient failure is retried on the next pass.
- **Excluded failures:** network/GitHub and pass-wide failures are never deferred, so an outage cannot defer every tree.
- **Writes only under `--apply`:** the cursor and backoff are persisted only then, keeping the dry-run no-write contract.
- **Cursor validation:** the cursor is a bare directory name in a private file. Anything else is ignored, and the pass falls back to a full scan from the start.
- **Pruning:** stale quarantine entries for vanished paths are dropped on each applied pass.
- **Prefetch cap:** prefetch is limited to `PREFETCH_SHARE` = 0.5 of the remaining budget.
- **Complexity:** progress plumbing lives in `reclaim/progress.py`, which keeps `sweep.py` under the Qlty file-complexity threshold.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (scheduling of a removal pass; no new removal authority)
- **Verification:** self-assessed, plus a live dry run.
  - Tests, from `.agents/worker-lifecycle` at `1bddf2dfb8`:
    - `tests.test_reclaim`: 66 passed. 8 are new: rotation, cursor validation (including a non-private file), threshold deferral and clearing, pass-wide/network exclusion, dry-run no-write, resume point, the end-to-end CLI cursor advance (`--apply` moves it, a dry run does not), and a stalled prefetch that still leaves judgement budget.
    - Earlier `tests.test_reclaim` + `tests.test_retirement` run: 173 passed (11 skipped).
    - `tests.test_legacy_cleanup`: 46 passed.
  - Lint and static checks:
    - ruff 0.11.13: clean.
    - mypy 1.15.0: only the existing `macos.py:17` ctypes error.
    - shellcheck: clean.
    - `qlty smells` on the changed files: none.
  - CI at `664fcee30b`: all required checks passed.
  - Live dry run against the real worktree base and registry (`--limit 15`):
    - `owner_observation=registry`
    - 15 scanned: 6 archive-queued, 9 refused, 0 removed
    - `resume_after` set
    - no `reclaim-cursor` or `reclaim-quarantine` file written

Resolves #38376

body:
## Summary

Workers now own their PR through merge, as interactive full-loop does: after commit-and-pr they wait for required checks with full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks --timeout 220 (at most 8 calls, about 30 min), repair failures their changes caused, then merge. Layer 6 clears any older hint before it runs and only writes one for rc=1 with empty output; layer 7 passes it via DISPATCH_ASSIGNMENT_VERDICT_FILE and deletes it after the claim. _dispatch_negative_cache_record now logs 'negative_cache_record_skipped reason=<fingerprint|boundary|pr_head> detail=<assigned|unavailable>' once per issue revision (sibling .skip marker; record format and readers unchanged). title: GH#38394: reclaim stage 2 archive, verify, journal, remove (phase 5 of #38051)
body:
## Summary

Adds stage 2 to the worker_lifecycle reclaim sweep. After stage 1 judges every candidate, trees classified archive (finished work, all owners ended, but with uncommitted changes or unpushed commits) are archived with worktree-archive-helper.sh archive --bundle-commits, verified with verify-local, journaled as reclaim-archived with the archive id (path + manifest sha256), then removed only if the judgement-time evidence fingerprint is unchanged and source-matches confirms the archive is still faithful. --bundle-commits makes the archive carry its own commits even for published heads (remote_branch_state: bundled) so it never depends on a remote branch the merge flow deletes (#38056); default archive behaviour is unchanged. Any failure keeps the tree; a verified archive is kept either way. Archive timeouts/capacity failures feed the phase-4 repeat-unreadable quarantine. title: GH#38399: fix(setup): npm global install no longer falls back to sudo for a fresh user prefix
body:
## Summary

The Linux sudo decision for global npm installs tested -w <prefix>/lib, which is false when lib/ does not exist yet, so a fresh user prefix (e.g. ~/.npm-global) caused a root-owned sudo install. Added _npm_global_prefix_needs_sudo in setup/_common.sh: it tests the nearest existing ancestor of <prefix>/lib (npm creates missing dirs) and keeps sudo for unknown/relative prefixes. The issue's broken-shim follow-up was not changed: setup_opencode_cli already rejects a managed shim whose target is missing (test 5e), and a user-prefix install now survives system-disk rebuilds.

## Decisions

Nearest-existing-ancestor check instead of the issue's -w prefix + mkdir -p: npm creates prefix dirs itself, and a writable prefix with a root-owned existing lib/ must still use sudo. The _common.sh vs _runtime_helpers.sh bun/npm policy shadowing is left unchanged here (separate behaviour question).

title: GH#38405: phase 6 of #38051 — Reclaim evidence-backed authorization replaces operator confirmation
body:
## Summary

Adds `reclaim-unowned`: a never-owned enrolled worktree (no bound run, no created-worktree receipt) is retired without operator --confirm when Reclaim proves nothing would be lost. Order: process census (moved before authorization, since such a tree has no runs to observe), evidence fingerprint, nothing_to_lose (clean + HEAD contained in a remote), fingerprint re-taken (compare-and-swap). Then one writer transaction (AdmissionRegistry.close_unowned) re-checks no binding/creation receipt, writes `reclaim-unowned-authorized` (owner check, git state, references, fingerprint, checked_at) keyed uuid5(generation, type), and closes admission. Replay re-checks facts and never rewrites the first event. Retirement stays archive-first through the existing cleanup executor. Readers (cleanup_plan.never_owned_authorized, retirement owner evidence, recovery evidence, legacy takeover) accept the Reclaim event or the legacy operator_confirmed event; the reader requires every recorded fact. The profile README fallback calls reclaim-unowned and treats only status=retired as success. Never-owned operations move from cleanup.py to never_owned.py (Qlty complexity); the registry zipapp bundles the new modules. CLEANUP.md documents the command and stays within the 500-line limit. The legacy retire-enrolled-only path and its worker-lifecycle-state.sh hint stay until phase 7.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/profile-readme-publication-lib.sh, .agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md, .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_retirement.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/admission.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/bundle.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_plan.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cli_errors.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/journal.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_takeover.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/never_owned.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/reclaim/unowned.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/recovery.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/refusal.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/retirement.py

title: GH#38420: force title/small_model onto the local provider when bound (GH#34125 follow-up)
body:
## Problem

Operator-bound local-only sessions (GH#34125, `AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_POLICY=local-only`)
enforce the egress gate (`assertLocalOnlyEgress`) inside `chat.params`, which
covers the main turn, subagents, and compaction (GH#35893). Title generation
does not: OpenCode's title sub-call never invokes `chat.params` at all.

Confirmed live with a throwaway config (`enabled_providers: ["mac-local",
"anthropic"]`, no `small_model`/`agent.title.model` pin) and
`AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_DEBUG=1`: a bound session's main turn correctly ran on
`mac-local`, but the plugin log recorded a `provider-auth: redistributed ...
to stay under third-party detection threshold` line and a matching
`cache-stability: ... family=aux` line for that same session — both of which
only fire inside the Anthropic-native-provider request-transform pipeline.
No `VAULT_POLICY_DENIED` was ever logged for that session. The aux (title)
request reached Anthropic's request-body construction with zero gate
visibility.

`applyCompactionRouting` (compaction-routing.mjs) can't be extended to cover
this: it only acts inside `chat.params`, and the comment there already notes
(GH#35893) that OpenCode reads the compaction model only from
`agent.compaction.model` at config time, while compaction's actual *request*
does cross `chat.params` (confirmed: it's always visible there as
`agent=compaction` and denied like any other call when bound). Title has no
such hook visibility to react to at all.

## Fix

New `title-routing.mjs` exports `applyLocalOnlyTitleRouting(config, opts)`,
wired into `config-hook.mjs` right after `applyCompactionRouting`. When the
session is bound and its primary `config.model` already resolves to a local
provider (egress-gate-verified), it forces both `agent.title.model` and
`small_model` onto that same primary model — **unconditionally overriding**
any existing non-local pin, unlike compaction's "only when unpinned"
residency preference for unbound sessions. Bound policy is absolute: there is
no hook fallback for title, so the config-time force is the only guarantee.

If the primary model itself isn't local (shouldn't happen in a real bound
session, since the main turn would be denied anyway), nothing is forced; the
main-turn egress gate still covers that case.

## Testing

- New `tests/test-title-routing.mjs` (6 cases): no pin → both forced; existing
  non-local pin → overridden; existing local pin → left untouched (no-op

title: GH#38417: Reclaim never-owned refusal names a standing authorization; legacy recovery evidence no longer blocks Reclaim
body:
## Summary

Case 1 (stale authorization after a refused replay): reclaim-unowned refusals now report `standing_authorization: true` when an earlier check already authorized and closed admission (for example a crash before the retirement plan, then an edit). Admission never reopens and the first event is never rewritten, so that generation stays authorized and a cleanup pass retires it archive-first, preserving the edit; the flag makes the output truthful instead of implying the tree is kept. A first refusal is unchanged (admission open, no flag). Case 2 (legacy/Reclaim recovery-event collision): recovery.prepare_retirement reuses a stored `retirement-recovered` record that differs from the current evidence only in proof kind (`operator_confirmed` vs `authorization: reclaim`), instead of raising event-id-payload-conflict; a record for a different tree (any other field) still conflicts.



## Files Changed

.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_retirement.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/never_owned.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/recovery.py

## Decisions

Chose the brief's distinct-status option for case 1. Reopening admission was rejected: no code path reopens a closed admission (a monotone invariant that retirement and admit rely on), and a concurrent retirement holds only a flock. Reader-side fingerprint comparison was rejected: because the first event is never rewritten, one edit would leave the generation closed and permanently unretirable by Reclaim. Case 2 strips only the two proof keys when comparing, so identity fields (path, directory and git identities, admitted runs) must still match.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Before rebase, ten neighbouring suites (test_retirement, test_reclaim, test_absence, test_admission, test_admission_recovery, test_cleanup_policy, test_legacy_cleanup, test_bundle, test_events, test_retirement_processes): 268 tests OK (10 platform skips). After rebasing onto #38193 (other Reclaim modules): test_reclaim, test_bundle, test_admission_recovery, test_absence 102 OK, and the reclaim/enrolled-only/retirement subset 20 OK. New tests: refused replay after authorization reports standing_authorization with admission closed, while a first refusal reports none and stays open; legacy recovery evidence is reused by prepare_retirement and a different-tree record still raises StoreConflict. title: GH#38428: fix(worktree-clean): attest unforgeable session tasks, opt-in root census, refusal diagnostics
body:
## Summary

On shared Linux hosts the same-UID path census marked every non-dumpable task uncertain, so `clean --auto` kept nearly every worktree. The census now excludes an unreadable task only when facts the user cannot forge attest root-installed session code:

- `user-manager`: the exec'd child of a root `systemd` PID 1 that PID 1 itself records as both `MainPID` and `ExecMainPID` of `user@UID.service` (root-owned `systemctl`, empty environment, 5 s timeout), with its start time unchanged across the query.
- `pam-session-keeper`: that manager's first never-exec'd child, forked within five seconds.
- `privsep-session`: a never-exec'd unprivileged child of a root `sshd`/`sshd-session`.

Attestation requires the census, the task and its parent to be in the initial user namespace, and is disabled when the census runs as root. Process names, cgroups and executables never grant an exclusion. Remaining uncertainty can be resolved by the opt-in root inspector `--census` mode (`AIDEVOPS_PROTECTED_PROC_INSPECTION=1`). That mode returns device/inode-bound counts only, refuses a `/proc` from another PID namespace or a `hidepid`/`subset` mount, and can only confirm clear or held. Cleanup skip lines now carry the census summary (status, counts, classes, `privileged_census`), and only when the whole seal line matches the census format. Any other stderr falls back to fixed text. New modules: `worktree_process_attestation.py`, `worktree_census_resolution.py`. Docs: `reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md`.

## Files Changed

.agents/reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-cwd-inspect.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-process-census.py, .agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree-cwd-inspect.py, .agents/scripts/worktree_census_resolution.py, .agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_quiescence.py, .agents/scripts/worktree_process_attestation.py, .agents/scripts/worktree_process_census.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_retirement_processes.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/protected_proc.py

## Decisions

- Fail closed throughout. Unattested non-dumpable tasks (ssh-agent, gpg-agent) stay uncertain because they run user-controllable code; only the opt-in root census can clear them. Name-based exclusions are not reintroduced (see PR #37730). Root census output is counts bound to the directory identity, never deletion authority.
- **Independent review, two cycles.** Cycle 1 found the original user-manager rule forgeable. An orphan re-parented to PID 1, moved into the user-delegated `init.scope` cgroup and exec'd as a root-owned binary named `systemd`, passed every check, so its hidden child was excluded. I reproduced this chain over SSH in the test host. The rule now binds to PID 1's `MainPID`/`ExecMainPID` record, and the same chain stays uncertain. Cycle 1 also fixed: initial user namespace required (D2), skip text restricted to the census line (D3), and the inspector's proc-view check (D4). Cycle 2 added the `ExecMainPID` agreement (a `MAINPID=` notification can repoint `MainPID`), the systemd PID 1 guard, and whole-line matching for the skip text.
- The root census deliberately shares the unprivileged census's PID-namespace view rather than requiring the initial PID namespace. Processes in other namespaces that share a bind-mounted tree are invisible to both, so the root census adds no visibility either lacks. Requiring the initial namespace would make every container fail closed. This is documented in the reference file and the inspector docstring.
- Known residual: a ptraceable (dumpable) user manager could be driven by the user. Such a manager is readable, so the census inspects it directly rather than attesting it.
- Hosts without a root-owned `/usr/bin/systemctl` or `/bin/systemctl` (for example NixOS) get no `user-manager`/`pam-session-keeper` exclusion. Those tasks stay uncertain.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified on head 66bfc96a60; the only later commit, 4bd9ac7fc5, flattens one test (no runtime change). Test host: a disposable Ubuntu 24.04 systemd + sshd container, unprivileged user with lingering enabled, all commands over a real `ssh` session. GitHub is a stub reporting no PRs. Grace and cooldown guards stay on at their minimums: fixture aged 3 h against a 1 h grace, 1-minute dead-owner cooldown.
  - `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto` with merged worktrees whose owner had exited:
    - Ordinary holder in the busy tree: busy skipped with `same-boot process census active or unavailable: status=available references=1 uncertain=0 excluded_nondumpable=3(pam-session-keeper=1,privsep-session=1,user-manager=1)`; idle tree removed (`AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_REMOVAL_COMPLETED=1`).
    - Hidden (non-dumpable) holder with the opt-in root inspector installed: busy skipped with `privileged_census=held`; idle removed.
    - Hidden holder without opt-in: both trees retained (`uncertain=1(nondumpable=1) ... privileged_census=inspection-not-enabled`).
  - The review's D1 chain, reproduced: the attacker process A had ppid 1, comm `systemd` and sat in `user@1001.service/init.scope`, while PID 1's `MainPID` was 91. A's hidden child came out unattested (`uncertain=1`). The genuine manager, `(sd-pam)` and the sshd privsep child still attested.
  - Root inspector on the real proc view: direct census `references=0 uncertain=0`; `clear` with an unrelated ssh-agent; `held` with a hidden holder.
  - Skip-text sanitizer: census lines pass; tracebacks, crafted path lines and control characters fall back to fixed text; output capped at 400 characters. Checked on Bash 5 and macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.
- **Checks:**
  - `test-worktree-process-census.py`: 24/24 on macOS (4 Linux-only skips), Linux unprivileged, and Linux root (1 skip).
  - `test-worktree-cwd-inspect.py`: 24/24 on macOS and Linux.
  - worker-lifecycle `test_retirement_processes`: 18/18 on Linux.
  - Clean: ruff 0.11.13 (the repo-pinned version), mypy `--platform linux` and `darwin`, shellcheck, qlty smells, and the pre-commit/pre-push hooks.
  - `qlty-regression-helper.sh`: base 36 / head 36, delta 0. The first push regressed +1 file-complexity in the test file; it was fixed in code, with no `ratchet-bump` override.
  - `test-worktree-owner-lifetime.py`: 27 pass; 5 CreationProducer failures reproduce identically on origin/main in that container (environment, not this change).

Resolves #38428

title: t19021: fix(gh): stop shim temp-file leaks that bloat agent tmp and slow dispatch
body:
## Summary

The gh shim leaked per-invocation scratch into the shared agent tmp root at about 430 files per hour. The root reached 101,078 entries, 93k of them leaked `gh-*` files. Every glob over that root then paid for the backlog, including the per-dispatch `setup_worker_log` cleanup. This PR stops the leaks, reaps what only SIGKILL can leave, and throttles one per-dispatch walk that never needed to run every time.

- **`gh auth *` leak:** the shim created its attempt-state file and then called `exec` for native gh, so the EXIT trap never ran. `_shim_exit_cleanup` now runs before the `exec`.
- **TERM/INT/HUP leak:** REST-read `gh-transport-meta/error` and `gh-identity` scratch now go into a per-process registry (`_GHGT_LIVE_TEMPS`) that the shim's EXIT trap removes. Paths leave the registry as they are removed, so the trap never deletes another process's reused mktemp name.
- **SIGKILL residue and backlog:** `gh_sweep_orphan_temps` (hourly from `gh_trim_log`, on demand via `gh-api-instrument.sh sweep-temp`) runs one `find -delete` per kind. Scope: exact mktemp names, depth 1, user-owned, older than 24h.
- **Per-dispatch research-staging walk:** `_aidevops_research_staging_sweep` enforces a 7-day retention but walked about 60k entries (1.2s) on every dispatch. It is now throttled hourly.
- **Test isolation:** `test-gh-api-instrument.sh` now isolates `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`. An unisolated run swept the host root; that deletion stayed within the sweep's own scope, which was verified afterwards.

## Evidence (local machine, 2026-11-15)

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Agent tmp root entries | 101,078 | 20,920 |
| Leak probe: auth status / auth token / TERM-interrupted read | 1 / 1 / 2 files | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `aidevops_pulse_tmp_cleanup` isolated run | 8.87s | 1.63s |
| Tmp-root globs inside it (`_ptsw_*`) | 7.1s | 0.11s |

In the live pulse, `dedup.setup_worker_log` took 65–381s per dispatch between 06:19Z and 06:39Z. The isolated run explains about 9s of that. The rest is attributed to concurrent load as a hypothesis; the post-deploy stage samples will confirm or refute it.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: 335 passed, 0 failed. Includes the new assertion that `gh auth token` leaves no `gh-request-attempts.*` file.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`: 328 passed, 0 failed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-worker-temp-dir.sh`: 7 passed, 0 failed.
- `shellcheck -x` clean on all changed scripts. `_gh_transport_run_rest` went from 101 to 97 lines, now under the complexity limit.

Resolves #38443

title: t19022: perf(dispatch): keep layer-6 verdict hints out of the shared tmp root scan
body:
## Summary

Layer 6 of the dispatch dedup (`dedup.layer6_assignee`) went from about 10-20s to 100-450s per candidate on 2026-11-15. It was the largest single stage in the dispatch ceremony, for example 238.6s of 749.7s for one candidate in a private managed repo (`<webapp>`).

Cause: t19006 (#38398, shipped in v3.39.200) writes a layer-6 "not assigned" hint for the pre-claim guard. Before each write it pruned old hints with `find <shared tmp root> -maxdepth 1 -type f -name 'dispatch-assignment-verdict.*' -mmin +30 -delete`. That find stats every entry in the shared agent tmp root. It ran on every free verdict, and parallel dispatch children ran it at the same time. The root held about 101k entries at the time (the leak fixed in t19021 / #38444).

Fix:

- `_dedup_assignment_verdict_path` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`) now places hints in a private `dispatch-assignment-verdicts/` directory under the temp root.
- `_dedup_assignment_verdict_record` creates that directory with mode 700. It refuses a symlinked or foreign-owned directory, and the prune scans only that directory.
- `_dch_assignment_verdict_file_valid` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-runtime.sh`) accepts only a regular, user-owned file directly inside the private directory. The directory must also be user-owned and not a symlink.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged. The hint stays an optimisation: if the reader rejects it, the full pre-claim assignment guard runs, and the post-consensus final guard always does a fresh read. Hint files with the old root-level names are now inert. Only a handful exist (1 on this host).

## Evidence (local runtime logs, 2026-11-14/15)

- Gap between the helper's last recorded layer-6 sub-gate (`dedup.layer6.cost_budget`) and `dedup.layer6_assignee` completion:
  - 0-1s for every call from 2026-11-14T11:55Z to 2026-11-15T01:29Z (30 calls).
  - 101-452s for every call from 03:29Z to 06:37Z (16 calls).
  - This is a step change after the v3.39.200 deploy at 03:00Z. In v3.39.199..v3.39.201, t19006 is the only change to the layer-6/claim paths.
- After `cost_budget` the helper does only local `jq` work on a free issue. A standalone `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned` on a free issue completed in 3.9s with sub-gate rows matching the pulse's.
- Calls that layer 6 blocked log `already assigned — DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON`. None of the slow calls logged it, so they were all free verdicts, which is the only path that runs the prune.
- Five pairs of parallel candidates finished layer 6 in the same second with identical or near-identical elapsed times (one pair at 232.6s each). This fits concurrent scans of one directory.
- At 07:27Z, after the tmp root was cleaned to about 21k entries, the gap was 20s. The same `find` over the 21k-entry root took 1.70s standalone. Over a small directory it took 0.00s.

## Runtime Testing

- Scratch round-trip with an isolated `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`, under Bash 5 and /bin/bash 3.2. All 10 checks pass:
  - The hint path is inside the private directory, and the hint is written.
  - A stale hint is pruned, and unrelated root files are untouched.
  - The reader accepts the hint, and rejects a legacy root-level hint, `..` traversal, a symlinked hint and a symlinked directory.
  - The writer refuses a symlinked directory.
- Existing tests that load the changed files:
  - `test-dispatch-dedup-is-assigned-timing.sh` 9/0
  - `test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` 48/0
  - `test-pulse-dispatch-core-pr-guard.sh` 12/0
  - `test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh` 11/0
  - `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh` 97/0
  - `test-stale-recovery-crash-evidence.sh` passes
  - `test-precreation-failure-skip.sh` 62/0
- `test-no-worker-process-fix.sh` has 8 failures that also occur on the earlier main checkout without this change. They are content checks on `headless-runtime-lib.sh`, `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` and the claim exit paths, all outside this diff.
- ShellCheck is clean, and pre-commit passed: return/positional/string ratchets and the bash 3.2 parse.
- Post-deploy check: `dedup.layer6_assignee` minus its last sub-gate should return to 0-1s in `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`.

Risk: low. Two files, and the change only moves where an optional hint is written and read.

title: t19024: perf(session-time): project message role and completion time in SQL instead of sorting raw message JSON
body:
## Summary

The hourly profile README job (r908) is still taking hours after t19016 (#38427) because the session-time engine has the same defect. SESSION_QUERY selected the raw m.data column under ORDER BY s.id, m.time_created. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN reports USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY, so SQLite copied every message JSON blob in the one-year window into a temp file before Python saw a row. Recent rows average about 83 KB and some exceed 60 MB. On the Pulse host, session-time-interval-engine.py --period profile --all-dirs had been running for 3 h 50 m with a 1.67 GB etilqs temp file. The last r908 run took 27,671 s and failed. The reader also held the live OpenCode WAL (2.2 GB) open, which stops checkpoints for every session and worker that shares that database. The query now projects only json_type(data), json_type(data, '$.time') and a multi-path json_extract(data, '$.role', '$.time.completed'), so only small rows are sorted. parse_message applies the same rules to the projected columns, and session_time_db_roots.py reuses the shared projection.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/session_time_db.py, .agents/scripts/session_time_db_roots.py, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19024-brief.md

## Decisions

Kept ORDER BY s.id, m.time_created. With small projected rows the sort is cheap, and the per-session role sequence stays the same. Multi-path json_extract returns a JSON array, so JSON booleans stay booleans and safe_int still rejects them. Empty or NULL data still reads as '{}'. SQLite json_valid is strict RFC 8259, so NaN and Infinity literals, which OpenCode never writes, now count as skipped.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Ran the origin/main engine and the patched engine side by side with an identical --now-ms and an isolated HOME. Cases: an edge-case fixture (invalid JSON, array root, null and string time, boolean, string and float completed, empty data, missing time, non-string role, child session) for --period profile, all, month and day; one-root and multi-root --batch; and five real per-launcher OpenCode DBs. All outputs are byte-identical; the fixture reports 4 skipped malformed rows on both. test-contributor-session-archive.sh: 12/12 pass. py_compile is clean. Projected query on the 69 GB main DB: 174,351 rows (366 days) in 11.2 s. A full patched --period profile --all-dirs run over every DB on the host finishes in 83 s, against more than 3 h 50 m (still running) for the deployed engine.

Resolves #38451

title: t19030: fix(auto-update): make t2119 plist drift detection converge instead of running full setup every 6 hours
body:
## Summary

The t2119 plist drift check and its recorder hashed different files (schedulers.sh vs schedulers-pulse.sh since the GH#22419 split), so every 6-hourly check on every macOS install reported drift and ran a full setup.sh --non-interactive (11-23 min each, ~100 min/day) without converging, while real scheduler-template changes such as t19026 ProcessType=Interactive still never reached the installed plists. Adds one shared scheduler_template_hash (setup/modules/schedulers-template-hash.sh) over every schedulers*.sh template plus _scheduler_runtime.sh, used by both sides. setup captures the hash of the templates it loaded and records it only after a full scheduler pass; the checker compares every cycle, repairs a new template revision at once and rate-limits only repeated repairs of the same revision.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/auto-update-freshness-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-template-hash.sh, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-reliability-self-heal.sh, TODO.md, setup.sh, todo/tasks/t19030-brief.md

## Decisions

Kept full setup.sh --non-interactive as the repair command: real drift is now rare and full setup deploys agents before plists reference new scripts. Pulse-only paths no longer record, so a pulse-only template change gets one full repair that also regenerates the watchdog plist. The attempt and stamp are written before setup starts so a run killed by the update timeout cannot retry every cycle.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — test-worker-reliability-self-heal.sh 16/16 pass (Part A updated to the shared-hash contract; Part C extraction path fixed for headless-runtime-worker-invocation.sh, which failed identically on main). ShellCheck clean on all six files. 10/12 related scheduler suites pass; test-routine-tracking-updates and test-resolve-pulse-runtime-binary fail identically on unmodified main (follow-up filed separately).; macOS: native platform detection, model replay sandbox and PATH portability checks passed at 4a347b411f9ea6dfff840947c52662585abc36bf.

title: t19035: perf(pulse): census defers doomed clamped scans and reuses last-good candidates on repo timeout
body:
## Summary

Candidate supply collapsed to 1-4 per cycle (with 10-19 free slots) whenever the largest backlog repository's census scan timed out, and reached 120-133 when it completed; the latest live log still shows a clamped budget=3s scan followed by candidates=4 with 14 free slots. Two fixes in build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json/_dispatch_census_enumerate_repo: (1) a known-slow repository (learned budget > base) reached with less census time than it needs now stops the census before it is polled, leaving its poll stamp and the rotation cursor untouched so it leads the next census with its full budget; the first repository of a census is never deferred, so every census makes progress. (2) Each completed scan stores that repository's candidate list (atomic mktemp+mv, JSON via stdin); a timed-out scan (rc=124 only) reuses it when at most PULSE_CENSUS_LAST_GOOD_MAX_AGE_S old (default 3600, 0 disables), logs the reuse with count and age, and still returns 124 so scan_failed and product incompleteness are reported. Schedule/interval/defer admission moved into _dispatch_census_admit_repo so the census loop stays under the 100-line complexity gate (98 lines).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19035-brief.md

## Decisions

Not raising PULSE_REPO_ENUMERATION_BUDGET_MAX_S or the 180s census budget: the large repository also times out at the 60s cap under live contention (13s isolated vs 25-60s+ live), and a bigger budget only shifts starvation to other repositories. Reuse is limited to rc=124 so auth/rate-limit/source outages never drive dispatch from stale data; reused candidates are hints that still pass every live dispatch gate (state check, gh_issue_view, 7 dedup layers). Root-causing the live snapshot cost for 1000-issue repositories is left out of scope.

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: real GitHub enumeration of the largest backlog product repository (private) through the changed worktree code with isolated pulse caches, cursor, stamps and log (no live state, label or lock writes): A full-budget scan rc=0 in 13s produced 123 candidates and stored them as last-good; B a clamped 3s scan (the live failure mode) returned rc=124 with the identical 123 candidates and logged 'Candidate census reused last-good candidates ... count=123 age=3s'; C a 45s census scanned the small first repository then logged 'deferred slow repository to the next census ... budget=60s remaining=43s' with the cursor left on the first repository; D the next 180s census returned 125 candidates including all 123 from the deferred repository. title: GH#38491: fix(opencode-db): disable worker snapshots and expire terminated worker events in the active DB
body:
## Summary

`opencode.db` grew from 4.4 GB to 70 GB in about four days. 58 GiB of it is the `event` table. This PR removes the source and cleans up dead worker events in the active DB, without VACUUM and without restarting interactive sessions.

### Root cause

1. Checkpoint-continuation workers merge their base branch into old PR branches. GH#37981 allowed this, so a single merge changes thousands of files.
2. OpenCode snapshot tracking stores the full before/after content of every changed file in the message's `summary.diffs`. One sample: 4,410 files, 152 MiB.
3. OpenCode re-emits that message as `message.updated` after every step. One worker wrote it 68 times, which is 10.1 GiB.
4. Worker sessions leave the active DB only after 7 days. VACUUM is blocked while TUIs hold the DB. Nothing is reclaimed.

### Changes

- **Source** (`headless-runtime-invoke.sh`): regular headless workers launch with `snapshot: false` merged into `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`. If an existing inline config is present, it is merged with `jq`. The private profile already did this. Opt out with `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_OPENCODE_SNAPSHOT=1`.
  - The OpenCode 1.19.5 binary loads `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` into the merged config.
  - The session-summary step returns before computing diffs when `snapshot === false`.
- **Cleanup** (new `opencode-db-archive-worker-events.sh`, wired into `opencode-db-archive.sh`): a new pass deletes `event` rows from the active DB for sessions that meet all of these conditions:
  - they are in the headless ledger `worker_sessions` (recorded only after the worker's isolated DB was merged back, i.e. after the worker ended);
  - they have been inactive at least `--worker-event-expiry-minutes` (default 60; 0 disables);
  - they are not named in active pulse logs and not held by an OpenCode holder (idle gate).
- **What the pass keeps**: `message`/`part`/`todo` and `event_sequence` are never touched, the same split as the existing archived-event expiry. Interactive sessions are never in the ledger.
- **Batching**: each transaction deletes at most 500 rows and 64 MiB of payload. Sizes come from `octet_length()`, which reads only record headers, so no payload is read to plan a batch. Candidates are found through the aggregate index.
- **Logging**: the log line reports the freed pages and bytes.
- **Schedule** (`opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`): after the day's full pass, the hourly timer still runs `archive-all --worker-events-only`. Dead worker events now expire within about an hour instead of waiting for the next day or for the 7-day retention. This pass does not count toward full-pass deferral escalation.
- New options: `--worker-events-only`, `--worker-event-expiry-minutes N`, `OPENCODE_DB_ARCHIVE_WORKER_EVENT_{MINUTES,BATCH_SIZE,BATCH_BYTES}`.

A continuation worker that resumes a recorded session copies that session's events into a fresh isolated DB and replaces them on merge. Expiring the shared copy therefore cannot lose its state.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`: all 75 pass, including the new dry-run, the real-run test (byte bound of 1, so one row per batch) and the async hourly-pass test.
  - The new real-run test checks that terminated worker and child events are removed, while live-worker and interactive events stay and the session/message/part counts are unchanged.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-warm-start-opencode.sh`: 19/19.
- `shellcheck` is clean on all changed scripts.
- Read-only check against the affected live DB:
  - 1,627 terminated worker sessions hold 1.68M of 2.02M events and 59.8 GiB of payload;
  - 339 non-worker sessions would be untouched;
  - the batch planner uses `event_aggregate_type_seq_idx` and plans the first batch (500 rows, 1.5 MB) in 4 s, cold cache.
- `test-worker-network-egress.sh` fails with the same failure on unmodified `main`. It is not related to this change.

Resolves #38491

title: GH#38492: fix(issue-sync): treat superseded coordinator checkpoint as cleanup no-op
body:
## Summary

The coordinator-artifact-maintenance apply job failed whenever this run's own just-uploaded checkpoint (protected_artifact_id) was absent from the newest inventory page. In bursts of Issue Sync runs, a newer run's cleanup (which keeps only its own checkpoint plus the newest fallback) prunes an older run's upload before that run's cleanup starts, so a successful sync run turned red with nothing left to do (verified on run 43704856171: artifact 14157741707 now 404, two later runs uploaded newer checkpoints before its apply started). cleanup_state now classifies an absent protected ID with a direct artifact lookup: 404 with >=2 live exact-name checkpoints and a newer live ID -> superseded no-op; live exact-name artifact missing from the listing -> deferred no-op. Both paths delete nothing and exit 0 with a ::notice. Any other absence (wrong name, expired, non-404 error, ID newer than every live checkpoint) keeps the existing integrity failure, so a wrong ID cannot silently disable pruning (#32024/#32055 storage invariant).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/forge-coordinator-state-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-forge-event-workflow.sh

## Decisions

Did not adopt the issue's blanket exit 0: test-forge-event-workflow.sh pins fail-closed behaviour for a missing protected ID, and silent success would hide a mis-wired ID forever. Did not serialise sync and maintenance via a shared concurrency group: GitHub keeps one pending job per group and cancels the rest, which would cancel sync jobs. Uses artifact-ID ordering as the 'newer checkpoint exists' signal; IDs can interleave slightly within a burst, which only falls back to the previous fail-closed behaviour, never a deletion.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime (read-only plan mode, real GitHub API, this repo): cleanup-plan with the actually-pruned ID 14157741707 — main: 'not a live exact-name checkpoint' rc=1; this branch: ::notice superseded, 'deleted=0 stop=protected_superseded' rc=0; wrong ID 99999999999 still rc=1. tests/test-forge-event-workflow.sh passes (run as CI does with PyYAML==6.0.3 via uv): existing missing-ID 99 case still fails closed (now via 404 + ID ordering), new cases cover wrong-name ID (fails), superseded ID 5 and not-listed ID 40 (exit 0, no DELETE call). shellcheck clean on both changed files. title: t19043: fix(full-loop): merge reads use the intended 60s timeout instead of the shadowing 15s generic default
body:
## Summary

Governed merges were refused with `PR head read failed (exit 124)` after checks and review gates passed, because GH#33673's 60s merge read budget never took effect. `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` assigns `AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT=15` when sourced, so `${AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT:-60}` in `_flm_gh_read_once` and `_merge_author_has_write_authority` always resolved to 15. `gh-transport-governor.py` spends up to `min(10, timeout-5)` seconds on local pacing inside that timeout, which left paced merge reads about 5s for HTTP. `gh-api-calls.log` shows 50+ `full-loop-helper-merge-transport.sh` timeouts at about 15050ms in about 43h, in bursts of about 10 per 15 minutes. Merges of PRs #38517 and #38533 hit it today.

The change adds `_flm_merge_read_timeout`. An explicit `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_GH_READ_TIMEOUT` (positive integer, no leading zero) wins. Otherwise the timeout is 60s, or a larger operator-raised generic value. Both merge read sites resolve it before their `local` declaration shadows the generic value. The two tests that `unset AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT` (a state production never reaches) now keep the sourced 15s default and assert 60, plus the override and invalid-value cases.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-authority.sh, .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-transport.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19043-brief.md

## Decisions

I used a dedicated `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_GH_READ_TIMEOUT` rather than distinguishing explicit and defaulted generic values. Pulse can export the generic 15s into worker environments, so an 'explicit' check would still shadow the merge budget there. The generic value only raises the merge timeout, never lowers it. The deadline clamp in `_gh_timeout_budget_seconds` is unchanged.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — - Production-chain probe (sources `shared-constants.sh` then `full-loop-helper-merge.sh`): on `main`, `flm_read_effective=15 authority_effective=15`; with this branch, `60` / `60`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`: Ran 241 tests, 0 failed (includes `post-verification reads: 60s merge budget over sourced 15s default, overrides`).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh`: Tests run 89, failed 0 (slow-gate admission reads now run with the generic 15s default present).
- `shellcheck` on all four changed shell files: clean.

title: t19044: fix(ci-wait): keep a cancel-only failure pending while other checks are still pending
body:
## Summary

`gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait` gives a concurrency-cancelled check a 180s grace window (GH#35830), counted from when the cancellation is first seen. Under CI queue pressure, the superseding run can still be queued after 180s. On 2026-11-15, jobs for PR #38533 started up to about 8 minutes after creation, with 20 runs queued in the repository. The window then expires while other checks are still pending, and the helper prints `FAIL: required checks reached a terminal failure` as soon as the last other check finishes. For PR #38533 it flagged only `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate: cancel` (run 43765832020). About one minute later the same gate showed `pass` (run 43765831983) and the PR merged. Callers treat `FAIL` as a real CI failure.

Now, when the failing set is cancel-only and any other check is still pending, `apply_cancel_grace` keeps the classification pending and clears the grace clock. The window starts once nothing else is pending. Real failures are still terminal immediately (including a mixed cancel, failure and pending set), the overall `--timeout` still bounds the wait, and per-attempt windows are unchanged. The new branch reuses `$_GCW_BUCKET_PENDING`, which keeps the string-literal ratchet unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19044-brief.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — - Probe sourcing the helper and calling `apply_cancel_grace failure` with `[cancel Gate, pending Lint]` at grace 0: `main` gives `classification=failure`, this branch gives `classification=pending`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`: 120 passed, 0 failed. New cases: a cancel beside pending checks reaches its queued replacement's pass at grace 0; a real failure beside cancel and pending stays terminal; the timer clears while pending and starts the window after settle (`pending:` then `pending:1500` then `failure:1500`).
- `shellcheck` on both changed files: clean.

Resolves #38537

title: t19045: fix(ci-wait): default wait-checks to the 200s worker chunk in headless sessions
body:
## Summary

t19011 made headless workers own their PR through merge, waiting in bounded chunks: `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks <PR> --repo <slug> --timeout 200`, at most 8 times. A worker that omits `--timeout` gets the helper's 1800s default instead. That is longer than the 600s shell-tool limit and the 600s activity-watchdog stall window, so the call emits no worker output for 600s. The watchdog confirms a stall and, once elapsed time passes the 1500s cap, kills the worker as `hard_kill_cap_active`. In the 24h to 2026-11-15T22:28Z there were 6 `elapsed_cap_while_active` kills out of 120 terminal outcomes. Two of them died inside `wait-checks`, one after its shell tool hit 600000 ms with no `--timeout`.

Now `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait` uses `AIDEVOPS_GH_CHECKS_HEADLESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 200) when a headless worker marker is set (`FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`, `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS` or `OPENCODE_HEADLESS` = `true`/`1`), no `--timeout` was passed, and `AIDEVOPS_GH_CHECKS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is unset. It prints a one-line `NOTE:` so the model knows to call again while checks are still pending. Explicit `--timeout` (including `full-loop-helper-merge.sh`'s `--timeout 0`), the env override, and interactive sessions are unchanged. The other four kills (raw `gh pr checks --watch`, a piped `pnpm install`, a filesystem-wide `fd`) are out of scope.

title: GH#38543: fix(pulse): escalate census budget above the cap for repos timing out at it

A repository whose candidate scan times out after the full 60s cap now escalates to PULSE_REPO_ENUMERATION_BUDGET_ESCALATED_MAX_S (default 120s, log reason=timeout_at_cap). The budget file records the escalated mode ('120 escalated'), so only escalated repos may exceed the base cap; a completion within 5s of the cap may also keep a 1.5x budget above it. title: GH#38562: fix(gh-permission): accept ETag 304 when gh api -i prints headers
body:
## Summary

t19029 made collaborator permission lookups conditional, but it treated a reply as 304 only when stdout was empty. On the default REST route, gh api -i writes the 304 status and headers to stdout, so every lookup after the first successful one returned rc=2 api-failure and failed closed for good. Interactive claims on org repos, write-permission guards, merge author checks and dispatch-claim trust were all affected. The lookup now accepts either 304 shape when an ETag was sent, the transport failed and there is no body. A 304 still reuses only a verdict stored from an earlier 200 for the same repo, user and route; without one it fails closed. Locals in the two helpers that write the caller's output variable are now prefixed, so callers that name their output perm get the verdict back.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-collaborator-permission-etag.sh

## Decisions

The trust boundary is unchanged: a 304 is never a grant by itself. The fix only stops a confirmed not-modified reply being misread as a transport failure. The 304 detection is its own helper so the lookup stays within the 100-line function limit.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — New .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-collaborator-permission-etag.sh: 7/7 pass with the fix. Against the previous helper it fails the 304-with-headers case as rc=2 http=304 reason=api-failure, which matches the live defect. Existing collaborator cache (29), current-user and actor-authority (17) tests pass. shellcheck is clean. Live probe with the worktree libraries: a private org repo and marcusquinn/aidevops both return rc=0 permission=admin http=304 reason=ok; the deployed runtime returns rc=2 api-failure.

Resolves #38562

title: GH#38566: perf(gh-transport): revalidate governed REST GETs with ETags so unchanged reads cost no quota
body:
## Summary

The owner's REST-core quota now runs out before each hourly reset: 4,622 used about 50 minutes into the window ending 1794791541, then 403 rate-limit-exceeded about 10 minutes before reset. Logged gh-pat attempts account for about 94% of that usage, so the drain is aidevops' own traffic. Most of it is repeated reads of the same issues, PRs, comment pages and /user. The transport governor now keeps the ETag and exact stdout of each eligible GET, keyed by the credential digest and the full gh api argv. Repeats send If-None-Match. When GitHub answers 304, the governor replays the stored stdout with exit 0 and drops gh's 'HTTP 304' diagnostic. The attempt row records status 304 and cost 0, which _response_metadata already did. Other statuses keep native behaviour; a 200 replaces the entry and a 404 or 410 drops it. Ineligible shapes always go out unconditional: --include, --silent, --template, a --jq that references now, env, $ENV or input, a caller-supplied validator header, non-core resources and rate_limit. AIDEVOPS_GH_CONDITIONAL_CACHE_DISABLE=1 turns the feature off. Entries are 0600 in a 0700 directory under the transport state dir, are capped at 1 MiB, and are pruned after 6 idle hours.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py, .agents/scripts/gh_conditional_cache.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh

## Decisions

The stored value is post---jq stdout, so gh's own gojq semantics are preserved without re-implementing jq. A replay happens only after GitHub validates the representation for the same credential and request, so it is equivalent to a live read and never a stale guess. A 304's rate headers still feed admission, as the existing collaborator-permission 304s already do.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — New .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py: 10/10 pass. It runs the real governor as a subprocess against a fixture gh that honours If-None-Match, and covers replay, change, 502/404, no-ETag, per-credential isolation, ineligible shapes, caller validators, corrupt entries and pruning. Existing tests: test-gh-transport-budget.py 78 OK (1 skipped); test-gh-shim.sh 328 passed, 0 failed. Live with the worktree governor and the native gh on a real issue: attempt 1 got 200 (cost 1); attempts 2 and 3 got 304 (cost 0), rc=0, byte-identical --jq stdout and empty stderr. Separately, 8 back-to-back raw 304s left x-ratelimit-used unchanged across three consecutive calls (197, 197, 197); 200s advanced it on every call.

Resolves #38566

- `localdev-helper-init.sh`, `yt-dlp-helper.sh`, `comfy-cli-helper.sh`: first three integrations

Risk: medium. Testing: runtime-verified on Linux.

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-install-record-helper.sh` passes all seven groups: routed report/help, 16 concurrent adds producing one record, broken shebang detection, report read-only behavior, unsafe metadata rejection, strict-mode source API, all three installer integrations and re-runs, npm-prefix discovery and disabled-source APT warning. Package managers are stubbed and fixtures use private temporary directories; no real installs or host tool scans occur.

Bash syntax, shfmt, diff whitespace, pre-commit quality and pre-push privacy/complexity gates pass. The runner's ShellCheck wrapper cannot locate its underlying binary; `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` / ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest) covers it. TypeScript dependencies are absent; the repo verification hook explicitly defers typecheck to CI. No TypeScript was changed. Native macOS verification has not been performed; the regression is portable and can be run there with the same command.

## Regression Evidence

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-install-record-helper.sh` preserves the runtime checks above using the repository's existing shell/Python tooling. The canonical issue scope was corrected before adding this required regression script after the Platform Fix Regression Evidence gate identified the missing durable test.

## Acceptance review

- Install metadata includes name, method, absolute path, installer, UTC date, reason and update path; file locking prevents duplicate concurrent records.
- Reports recorded and untracked local/bun/npm/uv/runtime/tool installs, broken shebangs and suspect APT versions. Scan-root override isolates directory discovery.
- mkcert package managers and download fallback, isolated yt-dlp and comfy-cli record successful installs. Existing preinstalled tools are not falsely attributed.
- Sensitive metadata is rejected before creating a ledger; this is defense in depth, not a substitute for never supplying secrets.
- CLI routing/help and Linux inventory pointer are present; status and update implementations are unchanged.
- Self-review: inspected the entire branch diff against the original criteria. Native macOS execution remains explicitly unverified, not claimed as a Linux test result.

## Decisions

Python 3 standard library provides portable JSON encoding, advisory file locking and package-output parsing. The record identity is name/method/normalized install path, preserving distinct copies. `AIDEVOPS_INSTALL_RECORD_FILE` overrides the ledger; `AIDEVOPS_INSTALL_SCAN_ROOT` replaces the directory scan home and disables host package-manager queries. User-facing documentation is the CLI help and helper usage comments; no updater behavior changes.

## Safety

Report only; no updates or deletion. Python 3 standard library and advisory record failures preserve successful installs. Scan and ledger overrides allow isolated verification without scanning host tool directories.

title: GH#38580: fix(pulse): keep drain starvation escape deferred across repeated drains
body:
## Summary

A cooperative drain with the GH#38162 starvation escape due no longer runs the LLM supervisor synchronously in a drained cycle that already deferred it (GH#38210). That synchronous run kept the scheduler from starting the activated bundle for the whole supervisor session (up to 55 min) with every worker slot empty, since the supervisor cannot dispatch (GH#36343). A repeat drain now keeps the deferral pending (first-deferral epoch preserved, bundle updated) and exits, so the activated bundle starts, runs its dispatch wave, then evaluates the deferred supervisor in its undrained supervisor phase. Backstop: once the deferral reaches PULSE_LLM_DRAIN_ESCAPE_MAX_DEFER_SECONDS (default 14400s, about 6h without a supervisor, aligned with the GH#34000 degraded escape; 0 never runs it while drained) the drained cycle runs the escape so persistent drains cannot starve recovery. PULSE_LLM_DRAIN_ESCAPE_DEFER=0 keeps the old immediate behaviour. Detaching the supervisor (option 1) was rejected: systemd kills service-cgroup descendants at wrapper exit, and the LLM lock is owned by the wrapper PID.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh

## Runtime Testing

title: GH#38585: fix(opencode-browse): reject xdg-utils browse alias on PATH
body:
## Summary

`browse_bin()` accepted any executable named `browse` on PATH. Debian/Ubuntu xdg-utils installs `/usr/bin/browse -> xdg-open`, so with the CLI absent every `aidevops opencode-browse` command ran xdg-open, `installed` exited 0, `install` skipped the download, and setup/update never offered the install.

- **Helper** (`.agents/scripts/opencode-browse-helper.sh`): new `is_browse_cli()` accepts a PATH `browse` only when `--version` prints a bare semver (the CLI prints `0.0.17`; xdg-open prints `xdg-open <ver>`). The installer location (`${XDG_BIN_HOME:-~/.local/bin}/browse`) is unchanged and unprobed. Every command (`installed`, `install`, `status`, `pair`, `doctor`, `mcp`, `run`) resolves through `browse_bin()`.
- **Plugin** (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`): `opencodeBrowseBinary()` treats a PATH `browse` whose real path is `xdg-open` as missing, without spawning (config-hook no-spawn rule), so the lazy `browse` MCP is not registered until the CLI exists.
- **Test** (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-browse-helper.sh`): xdg-open stub and fake-CLI regression for the helper.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/opencode-browse-helper.sh, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs, .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-browse-helper.sh

## Decisions

- Positive identity probe over an xdg-open denylist: npm installs keep the PATH fallback legitimate, and a denylist only catches the one symlinked collision.
- The plugin uses the non-spawning realpath subset because the config hook must not spawn (`tests/test-startup-nonblocking.mjs`); the helper still fails closed at MCP connect for any other impostor.
- `cmd_installed` already delegates to `browse_bin()`, so it needed no separate change.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified with the worktree helper.
  - xdg-open stub (`browse -> xdg-open`, xdg-utils argument handling) first on PATH, temp `HOME` without `~/.local/bin/browse`: `installed` exits 1; `status` prints `browse CLI: not installed (aidevops opencode-browse install)` with no stub output; `pair --list` prints `browse CLI is not installed`; `install --no-wait` now reaches the installer download (stub curl).
  - Positive paths: installer-location CLI `installed` exits 0 and `status` is unchanged under `/bin/bash` 3.2.57; a PATH-only symlink to the real CLI (0.0.17) is accepted and `run -- --version` works.
  - Plugin: `getMcpRegistry()` `browse.requiresBinary` is the missing installer path with the alias on PATH (MCP skipped), the PATH path for a real CLI, and the installer path when installed. `node --test` of the 10 mcp-registry test files (67 tests) passes; the push validator ran the full plugin `npm run test`.
  - `shellcheck` clean; pre-commit Bash 3.2 parse passed.
  - Not run on a real Ubuntu host; the stub mirrors xdg-utils.

## Regression Evidence

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-browse-helper.sh` (6 checks) passes under Bash 5 and `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 with `CI=true`, and fails at its first assertion (`installed exited 0 with only the xdg-utils browse alias on PATH`) when run against the pre-fix helper from `origin/main`.

Resolves #38585
