The three duplicated secret check/inject blocks in api_call, fleet inventory and cron are replaced by hostinger_secret_mode (inject / use env-config / refuse) plus hostinger_secret_reexec, which re-runs the helper under `aidevops secret NAME --`. In the re-executed child the selected value is copied into HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN for that process tree only and the source variable is unset, so api_call and the Python engines are unchanged; the token still reaches curl on stdin (-K -). An explicit selector wins over an exported HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN; an invalid or unstored selector is refused before any request. Docs: services/hosting/hostinger.md auth line and legacy-helper section, credential-inventory.md resolution table, helper help text and the missing-token hint now describe the account-specific name plus provider default.

The reporter's alias workaround keeps working but is not documented, since aliases are for retired names. `aidevops secret organise` will now offer a Hostinger default decision and flag a stored bare HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN; that is intended per the naming rule.

title: plan: capture pulse and DB health findings as worker-ready tasks
body:
## Aim

Capture the findings from an interactive pulse and database health review as worker-ready tasks, so the two genuine defects and one dead capability are tracked instead of living only in a log file.

## What this PR contains

Planning metadata only — no code changes.

- `TODO.md` — three new entries
- `todo/tasks/t19060-brief.md`, `t19061-brief.md`, `t19062-brief.md` — the local copies of the briefs already inlined into the linked issues

## Findings filed

Ref #38619 — `tier:thinking`, `priority:high`. GitHub transport admission binds credentials without bound: the `binding` table held **779** credential fingerprints in one scope on a host with a single configured GitHub account, so `credentials_share_proven_owner()` can never return true and `scope_mode` stays `unresolved` with `stale_multi_credential_scope: true` permanently. REST admission was pinned at `remaining: 42 / 5000` while `live-windows.json` already held a newer reset for the same scope. Both documented resolutions are unreachable: automatic owner accrual cannot attribute retired or `ghs_` bindings, and `reconcile` requires `AIDEVOPS_GH_QUOTA_OWNER` set "consistently for every caller" with no supported configuration surface that reaches the gh transport path. Follow-up to the closed GH#33701 / GH#33725.

Ref #38620 — `priority:medium`. The fix-the-fixer detector reported `classified=0 ... skipped:auth-error=10` across 7 cycles. Reproduced directly: the isolated runtime cannot authenticate the Anthropic OAuth provider for the simple tier and the host has no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` fallback. The GH#23430 cooldown works as designed, so the noise is suppressed while the capability stays dead and invisible to `pulse-check report`.

Ref #38621 — `priority:medium`. `worktree-recovery-timings.jsonl` (36 MB, single file) and `worker-progress-blockers.jsonl` have no rotation, while `rotate_pulse_log` already caps four sibling files. Observed quota exhaustion on this host produced 47 `Disk quota exceeded` errors that propagated into a sqlite `disk-io-error` and `[worker-lifecycle] reconcile-gap exit=2`.

## Deliberately not filed

- **Runtime bundle and backup retention.** Measured 5.0 GB across 30 bundles and 1.6 GB of backups, then found both already enforced: `agent-deploy-bundle.sh:602-604` caps at 30 days / 30 bundles / 8 GiB with live-lease and pinned-root protection, and `agents-backups` at 10 snapshots / 180 days / 4 GiB. Working as designed, so #38621 was narrowed to the two unrotated files rather than filed as broad artifact growth.
- **Two git-safety test failures seen in the pulse log.** Re-ran `test-git-safety-guard.sh` at HEAD: 21 tests run, 0 failed. Already fixed, so no issue was filed.

## Verification

```text
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh   # 21 tests run, 0 failed
pre-commit: Pre-commit checks passed
pre-push:   Pre-push checks passed
```

Pulse itself is healthy and was not changed: 36 cycles in the preceding 2 hours, 16 reached dispatch, last dispatch 7 minutes before the review. `memory.db`, `admission.sqlite3` and `work.sqlite3` all returned `PRAGMA integrity_check` → `ok`.

title: t19060: fix(gh-transport): age out retired bindings and add quota owner surface
body:
## Summary

Retired credential fingerprints no longer pin a single-account host to conservative REST accounting, and the quota owner now has one supported configuration location that every caller reads.

Binding lifecycle, option (a) with a mixed-version-safe shape:
- New `binding_seen(credential, last_seen)` table plus an `AFTER INSERT ON binding` trigger (`gh_transport_schema.py`). The trigger stamps every binding write from any runtime bundle inside the writer's own transaction. `user_version` stays 2, so older bundles keep their positional `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO binding VALUES(?,?)` and their schema check. An `ALTER TABLE binding ADD COLUMN` would have broken that positional insert, so it was rejected.
- The migration (`ensure_binding_recency`) is idempotent: a read-only trigger check, then one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. A losing or locked racer returns False and leaves every binding live. Existing rows are backfilled as seen at migration time, so they age out one window later.
- `live_binding_credentials()` is shared by `bound_credentials()` (allowance decisions) and `status`. A binding counts as live if it was seen within 3600 + 180 s (one core window plus the maximum reservation age), if its credential holds any reservation, or if it has no recency evidence (older writer or failed migration). A credential outside that window cannot own a stored reset that is still in the future, so the GH#33701/GH#33725 guarantee holds.
- Rejected (b), pruning rows: deleting a binding loses the merge-into-previous-scope protection when that credential comes back, and could race live reservations. Rows are filtered, never deleted.
- Rejected (c), a separate scope for `ghs_` tokens: it changes scope keys and would hand installation tokens a fresh allowance. A live `ghs_` binding still keeps `credentials_share_proven_owner()` False, and retired ones age out.

Owner configuration surface:
- `quota_owner()` falls back to the mode-600 `quota-owner` file in the shared transport state directory. Pulse, workers and interactive callers already resolve that directory, and `setup.sh` never regenerates the file. `AIDEVOPS_GH_QUOTA_OWNER` still overrides it per caller, and `unresolved` opts that caller out.
- New `gh_transport_budget.py set-owner` proves the authenticated `gh` login and stores only its digest (no login and no owner string). It refuses `ghs_` tokens and refuses when any live binding is not proven to be the same login. It is idempotent and never replaces a different configured owner. `reconcile` now points at `set-owner`.
- `reference/github-api-transport.md` documents only these reachable resolutions.




## Files Changed

.agents/reference/github-api-transport.md, .agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py, .agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget_cli.py, .agents/scripts/gh_transport_identity.py, .agents/scripts/gh_transport_recovery.py, .agents/scripts/gh_transport_schema.py, .agents/scripts/gh_transport_status.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py

## Runtime Testing

- **Verification:** runtime-verified — - `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`: 84 tests OK. New coverage:
  - 200 retired bindings plus 2 live same-login credentials accept the newer window and clear `stale_multi_credential_scope`.
  - Retired rows plus live different logins stay isolated at (540, 2000).
  - Reserved and unknown-recency bindings stay bound; a dropped trigger or table falls back to every binding.
  - Migration backfills existing rows and older positional writers still stamp recency.
  - The owner file surface works, including the `unresolved` env opt-out and refusal of a different owner.
  - `set-owner` refuses a live unproven binding and stores a 64-hex digest only.
- Negative proof: the new retired-bindings test fails on the old unfiltered `bound_credentials()` with `(42, 2000.0) != (4999, 2200)`, which reproduces the reported pin.
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-conditional-cache.py`: 10 OK.

title: GH#38627: fix(pulse): wake worker-exit refills from the active bundle
body:
## Summary

Worker-exit refill wakes from workers launched by an older runtime bundle were skipped (GH#32546) and left freed slots empty until the next Pulse cycle. Runtime activations happen about every 36 minutes, so 103 of 183 worker-exit triggers in the last 24h were skipped as inactive-bundle. In cycle 06:10-07:17Z six exits during a 30-minute lock-free housekeeping and supervisor window were all skipped. The signaler now wakes the validated active bundle's pulse-wrapper.sh; its entry re-exec from GH#33113 validates the bundle again before any lease or lock. The GH#32546 hazard is narrowed to its real window: while the runtime transition lock (setup activation or Pulse reconciliation) has a live owner, the wake is skipped and the trigger kept. A refill-only run also defers before and after it takes the instance lock.

Kept the inactive-bundle skip as a fallback when no valid active wrapper exists. Used the runtime transition lock (held across reconcile stop, wait and start) rather than removing the guard outright. An empty-pid transition lock counts as held only while it is under 2 minutes old, so an abandoned lock cannot suppress refills.

title: t19064: perf(pulse): let an admitted dispatch round finish under a bounded cooperative-drain grace
body:
## Summary

Deploy reconciliation writes LOCKDIR/drain_requested on every runtime activation (GH#37907). The serial and parallel dispatch loops stopped at the next candidate boundary, so drained rounds processed 636/2676 (24%) of ranked candidates versus 67% for normal rounds, and the first post-activation launch waited a median 11.1 min (28 activations/24h). New _pulse_drain_stops_admitted_round in pulse-dispatch-lib.sh lets an already-admitted round keep starting candidates while the drain is younger than AIDEVOPS_PULSE_DRAIN_ROUND_GRACE_S (default 600s; 0 restores the immediate stop). Age counts from the earlier of the marker mtime and this process's first sighting, so marker rewrites by repeated activations never extend it. Unchanged: _dispatch_compute_capacity, floor refill, t19015 stage fast-exit and GH#38048 census handoff still read _pulse_drain_requested_bundle, so no new round or census starts under a drain; launched candidates are recorded in the snapshot .consumed ledger that the handoff transfers.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19064-brief.md

## Decisions

Rejected removing the mid-round stop entirely: early-dispatch rounds run up to 3655s, which would delay the activated bundle by up to an hour. 600s default covers ceremony p90 (~430s) so a parallel round can fill admitted slots. Any helper failure (unreadable mtime, future-dated marker, bad clock) fails closed to the previous immediate stop. title: t19068: fix(recovery): a changed recovery policy ends human_decision suppression
body:
## Summary

A recorded human_decision suppressed supervisor re-assessment for 24h and ended early only on a maintainer reply. When a repo restored, added or edited its recovery policy, decisions recorded as human_decision because no delegated authority existed stayed parked for up to a day (plus the next 3h supervisor slot). Observed on a managed private repo: 40 human_decision records, most of them outlier/source choices its outlier_hold and session_cap_split actions delegate; one explicitly names the missing session_cap_split policy. Now record stamps human_decision with the policy actions fingerprint (none without a policy) and _tbr_decision_active ends suppression when the current fingerprint differs. Fingerprinting the actions, not the pinned default-branch revision, keeps unrelated commits from waking decisions. Legacy records count as none; an unreadable policy keeps the suppression; other wakes are unaffected. One per-process cached loader (_tbr_policy_load, global state rather than command substitution so the cache survives) feeds _tbr_policy_enabled and the fingerprint; _tbr_policy_read is the loader seam.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/recovery-policy.md, .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19068-brief.md

- **Verification:** self-assessed — bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh: 35 run, 0 failed, including the new case (none stamp, restore wakes, re-record suppresses, edited policy wakes, legacy unstamped wakes, unreadable keeps suppression and _tbr_policy_enabled returns 2, dependency_change unaffected). bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh (sources the discovery and capability fragments): 62 run, 0 failed. ShellCheck clean; pre-commit return/positional/string/Bash 3.2 ratchets pass. Runtime proof follows after deploy: the supervisor re-assesses the parked decisions once the repo policy loads.

title: GH#38669: resolve fixture helper paths with type -P instead of /usr/bin/true
body:
## What

Two test suites hardcoded absolute `/usr/bin/true` (and `/usr/bin/false`) as stand-in helper executables. On hosts where `/usr/bin` contains only `env`, those paths do not exist, so the fixtures silently took a different branch and the suites failed with assertions that look like product defects.

## Why it failed, exactly

`bash -x` trace of the dispatch failure:

```
+ _dsi_origin_identity_prerequisite /tmp/.../repo owner/repo
+ [[ true == true ]]
+ [[ -x /usr/bin/true ]]
+ return 0
+ [[ '' == repository_identity_drift ]]
+ exit 1
```

`.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-origin.sh:85` is `[[ -x "${_DSI_TOKEN_HELPER:-}" && -x "${_DSI_ASKPASS_HELPER:-}" ]] || return 0`. That gate is correct — it declares itself inapplicable when the helpers are not executable. The fixture was wrong: it pointed both helpers at a path absent on this platform, so the gate never ran and the expected `repository_identity_drift` was never produced.

`test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh` had the same shape, where `/usr/bin/true` was the "snapshot helper succeeds" fixture and `/usr/bin/false` the "snapshot helper fails" fixture. With neither present, the success case broke while the failure case passed by accident.

## Why not `command -v`

`$(command -v true)` is not a fix and I verified that before finding the right one: `command -v` resolves the shell builtin and returns the bare word `true`, so `[[ -x true ]]` is still false and the suite still fails. `type -P` forces external-binary lookup and returns a real path.

## Scope

Fixtures only. The applicability gate in `dispatch-single-issue-origin.sh` is deliberately unchanged.

Two other `/usr/bin/true` matches were checked and left alone because they are inert string literals, never executed: `test-command-policy-helper.sh:949` (argv in a denied-override assertion) and `test-scheduler-dedup-linux.sh` (crontab line contents).

## Verification

Run on Linux/NixOS, aidevops 3.39.212, deployed SHA `0719998ae`:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` | 98/99, exit 1 | **99/99, exit 0** |
| `test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh` | exit 1, first assertion failing | **exit 0** |
| `shellcheck` on both files | — | clean |

Found while running the focused dependency tests for the Pulse lifecycle rollout, where this failure would otherwise have been misread as a rollout regression.

## Follow-up, deliberately not in this PR

A gate that self-disables when its helpers are missing is right for dispatch, but it means pre-claim origin-identity drift detection quietly does not apply on a host where the token or askpass helper is absent. I have no evidence of that happening with the framework-provided helpers in production, so it is recorded as an open question on the issue rather than changed here.

Resolves #38669

title: t19071: fix(pulse): fix-the-fixer detector caches verdicts, gates dispatch repos and stays inside its stage bound

title: GH#38675: perf: single-pass procfs cwd scan in recovery process guard (GH#38675)
body:
## Summary

First slice of GH#38675. Profiling (strace execve) of one `retire`/`retire-plan`/`restore` case (`test_retirement_confirmed_and_independent_restore`) showed 5,991 of ~6,700 process spawns were `readlink /proc/N/cwd`, one per host process per process-guard scan (`_capture_worktree_proc_cwds`). A single python pass (`worktree_process_proc.py cwdmap`) now reads every cwd link; readable entries are final, provably irrelevant ones (vanished, zombie, foreign UID) are skipped, and everything else is handed back to the unchanged shell per-entry logic (privileged inspector, degraded visibility). A shell-level `readlink` override still selects the legacy loop. The guard is evaluated live on every scan; nothing is cached across guard re-checks.

## Files Changed

`.agents/scripts/worktree-process-providers.sh`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_process_proc.py`, plus a regression case in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib-process.sh` (registered in `test-worktree-removal-audit-lib.sh`). The two provider files were added to the issue's Files Scope with the profile evidence before editing.

## Timing (same host, loaded; one case)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_retirement_confirmed_and_independent_restore` wall | 60.6 s | 21.3 s |
| execve count (strace, whole case) | ~14,500 | ~3,800 |
| `readlink` execs | 5,991 | 0 |

Remaining fan-out (not addressed here): ~400 git, ~170 jq, ~165 dirname, ~100 python3 per case.

## Not yet met

The issue's suite target (<300 s, 3 slowest cases <10 s) is not met by this slice: a full-suite run with this change did not finish inside a 30 min budget on the loaded host (120 of 183 cases completed). The follow-up work is the git/jq/dirname repeats listed in the issue How section. Hence `For`, not `Resolves`.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** `test-worktree-removal-audit-lib.sh` 71/73. The 2 failures (`recoverable_archive_does_not_authorize_removal`, `snapshot_backend_requires_visible_target`) are host-environment dependent: the first also fails on an unmodified origin/main extract; the second passes or fails on identical code depending on whether the sandbox's privileged cwd inspector can read every process.

## Regression Evidence

New case `proc_snapshot_single_pass_map_matches_shell_loop` in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib-process.sh` asserts the map classifies readable (`R`), foreign-UID (`S`) and unknown (`F`) entries and that the capture output/status match the shell loop. Existing provider cases (degraded, foreign, zombie, same-UID, privileged) still pass.

For #38675

title: GH#38680: fix(pulse): stale-blocked sweep prefilters in jq, hands failed reads to retry, adds ready lane
body:
## Summary

Large repositories made almost no stale-blocked progress per Pulse pass: ready dependants (every native blocker closed) waited hours, the ordinary cursor stayed frozen (`resumed_after=19145` on consecutive passes), and one unreadable issue ended the whole pass.

## Root causes

- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh` `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues`: the open-blocker prefilter ran inside the deadline-checked loop. Each settled candidate still counted against `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_MAX_CANDIDATES` and cost several `jq` forks plus a cursor `mv`, so large repos spent their share before reaching a candidate that needed an API call.
- Same loop: a failed `gh api repos/{repo}/issues/{n}` read did `break`, so one bad issue ended the pass and headed the next one too.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`: ready dependants were only visited when the rotating sweep reached that repo (about once per rotation), and that share was mostly spent on the listing.

## Changes

- `_der_stale_candidates` drops open-blocker ordinary candidates in the single candidate `jq` filter; `_der_stale_prefiltered_count` keeps `prefiltered_open_blocker` and `pending` truthful (Pulse backlog weight is unchanged in meaning: `pending - visited - prefiltered`).
- `_der_stale_read_failed`: a failed read (or malformed body) is appended to the existing retry ledger. The drain re-reads it and still decides through `_der_try_unblock`. The pass continues; only `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES` (default 3) consecutive failures stop it, with the cursor after the issues handed off. If the ledger write fails, the cursor is kept and the pass stops.
- `DER_STALE_BLOCKED_READY_ONLY=1`: visit only ready candidates and never move or reset the ordinary cursor. The summary line adds `retry_queued=` and `ready_only=`.
- Pulse ready lane (`_pulse_stale_blocked_run_ready_lane`): every cycle, before the cadence check, ready-only passes run for pulse repos whose `.ready` hint is positive, with a fair share each.
  - The `stale_blocked_reconcile` stage is extended by `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_READY_SECONDS` (default 60, `0` disables) only while such a hint exists (local file reads, no API).
  - That extension is passed as `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_READY_RESERVE_S`. `_pulse_stale_blocked_sweep_deadline` holds it back, and the lane reports its unused part, so the claim fallback and the rotation keep their previous budget.
  - Hints converge to zero as ready issues are released or memo-recorded.
- `_pulse_stale_blocked_claim_fallback` and `_pulse_stale_blocked_pulse_repos` are extracted, so `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due` stays under the 100-line function gate (81 lines). `test-maintenance-selector-contract.sh` now registers `_pulse_stale_blocked_pulse_repos`, the one selector used by the claim fallback, the ready lane and the rotation, so the `.maintenance != false` predicate is still enforced at the place that selects repos.

Unblock decisions are unchanged: every release still goes through `_der_try_unblock` and its hold/maintainer checks.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`: 155 passed, 0 failed. Cursor assertions are updated to the hand-off contract. New checks cover: a failed read does not end the pass and is queued; consecutive failures stop after the queued issues; prefiltered candidates do not consume the candidate budget; ready-only leaves the ordinary cursor alone. One stdin `paste` call was made portable (`paste -sd' ' -`) for macOS.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh`: PASS (the existing contract "prefer the enclosing stage deadline" is preserved).
- PASS: `test-dependency-event-reconciler-partial`, `test-upstream-release-gate`, `test-dispatch-claim-helper`, `test-pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock`, `test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority`, `test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone`, `test-pulse-diagnose-helper`, `test-planning-pr-guard`.
- Ad-hoc lane wiring check (18/18). It covers hint selection, extension grant/disable, the ready-only env, the lane deadline reserve and stage clamp, unused-reserve accounting, the rotation budget being unchanged, and the lane running when the cadence is fresh.
- `shellcheck -x` clean on all three scripts. `complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base 9e1d2821cc`: function-complexity and nesting-depth `new: 0`.

## Runtime evidence to watch after deploy

- `pulse.log`: `stale-blocked ready lane completed repos=N/M reserve=60s (GH#38680)`.
- Per-repo `stale sweep ... ready_only=1 ready_visited=` lines for large repos.
- `retry_queued=` instead of `failed=1 complete=false` passes that stop at one issue.

Resolves #38680

title: GH#38685: fix(worktrees): retire provably complete stale lifetime rows so worktree add stops failing with bare ValueError
body:
## Summary

begin-create no longer fails with a bare ValueError when a retired worker left an unsealed lifetime row for an absent default path. For an absent path, `worktree_lifetime_owner.begin_creation()` now seals the stale owner-cgroup or Pulse generation from present-tense evidence (the existing `seal()` unit/process drain proof plus a live-owner-lease check), then applies the existing fresh proof and pre-Git fence. `prepare_creation()` moves the superseded Pulse generation into `worktree_lifetime_history` like an owner generation. If completion cannot be proven (a live, drained-but-unprovable or unknown owner), creation still refuses: `StaleLifetime` carries a fixed path-free message, and `shared-worktree-registry-owner.py` prints `WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_ERROR_REASON=stale-lifetime-record` with remediation (retry after the worker drains, or pass an explicit alternate path). Present paths and unknown managers keep the previous refusal.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-registry-owner.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_owner.py

## Decisions

I sealed via the existing `worktree-managed-lifetime.seal()` (loaded with `managed_module()`) instead of adding a new prune command. Reconciliation then uses the same drain contract as cleanup and never deletes a row; a superseded generation goes to history. Pulse rows qualify only when the path is absent.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — `tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh` passes, with 2 new cases: (1) an absent path with a stale running Pulse row whose completion cannot be proven fails at lifecycle:begin-create with the reason and remediation, and the row is unchanged; (2) a provably complete stale Pulse row is sealed into history and `worktree-helper.sh add` creates the worktree. Probe on a copy of the live registry, rolled back: 8/8 real stale running Pulse rows with absent paths (the issue's case) sealed and fenced; 3/3 stale running owner-cgroup rows refused with StaleLifetime because the path census was unavailable. test-worktree-managed-lifetime, -owner-native and -managed-run pass. The failures in test-worktree-owner-lifetime (persistent producers cleanup) and test-worktree-maintenance (3 removal/archive cases) also fail on main without this change. shellcheck is clean.

Resolves #38685

The supervisor-phase active refill could never launch: it ran after lock release with the cycle budget spent, so in-process dispatch_max stopped before enumeration (3/3 attempts, remaining=-2249s..-3519s, 0 launches; pool sat at 1/19 with 246 runnable). It now wakes a detached --refill-only --refill-source=active-pulse run through pulse_event_refill_signal, which takes the instance lock with a fresh refill budget from the active bundle and keeps rebase, transition deferral, wake coalescing and the failed-drain cooldown. title: GH#38713: fix(headless): escalate repeated model_unavailable backoff instead of hourly re-probes
body:
## Summary

Entitlement rejections (Codex 'not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account', model_not_found) are definite, but the 1h model backoff row was deleted on expiry, so each hour 1-4 concurrent dispatches re-probed openai/gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra and lost the whole attempt (58 rejections between 2026-11-16 16:27Z and 2026-11-17 04:39Z; 27 of 32 local-runtime-error sessions in 24h). Expired model_unavailable rows now stay as history; a repeat under the same auth doubles the previous duration (1h, 2h, 4h ...) up to AIDEVOPS_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_BACKOFF_MAX_S (default 86400). A rejection during an active backoff does not escalate it, an auth change still resets it, and a successful run on the model clears the history. The worker watchdog no longer treats model_unavailable rows as provider-wide backoff (it could kill healthy workers on other models of the same provider), and the orchestration efficiency collector no longer counts them as rate-limit slot loss.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh, .agents/scripts/orchestration-efficiency-collector.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-routing-retry.sh, .agents/scripts/worker-watchdog-checks.sh, .agents/tools/context/model-routing.md

## Decisions

Kept history in the existing provider_backoff row (no schema change): retry_after in the past plus reason=model_unavailable is the history marker, so readers that only check retry_after > now are unaffected. Doubling from the previous duration rather than counting rows keeps state to one row per model and makes the cap a single comparison. Watchdog/collector exclusions are reason filters on existing queries.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: ad-hoc isolated-HOME run of the real provider/backoff functions against a real state DB (19 checks): 1h base, concurrent rejection keeps active duration, 2h/4h escalation, 24h default cap and configurable cap, auth-change reset, stale-history reset, success clears history, other reasons still expire normally, watchdog query excludes model_unavailable. shellcheck -x clean on all modified scripts. test-headless-openai-routing.sh 8/8, test-worker-stall-diagnosis.sh 20/20, test-headless-routing-retry.sh PASS (added the clear_model_unavailable_history stub beside the existing clear_startup_no_model_feedback stub), test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh and test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh exit 0. test-headless-runtime-helper.sh: only 2 FAILs, both Claude sandbox admission 'filesystem-path-externally-writable', identical on unmodified main (environmental, pre-existing).

title: GH#38720: perf(pulse): census skips inline dependency normalization when candidates are already runnable
body:
## Summary

Full candidate censuses (`dispatch_max` and the worker-exit refill, both in `normalize` mode) ran dependency-readiness normalization inline for every repository whose snapshot contained any `status:blocked` issue. On the largest backlog this cost about 58s: a full-body graph rebuild plus a 30s relabel batch. With the ~11s issue list, the scan overran its 60s census cap and timed out. Once its last-good list expired, the repository contributed zero candidates and the runner idled at 1-2 of 20 workers.

`list_dispatchable_issue_candidates_json` now normalizes inline only when blocked work hides every candidate, which is the all-blocked roadmap case from GH#27145. If the snapshot already yields candidates, the read uses the existing `skip` semantics. Those semantics never claim completeness while blocked work is present. This change removes work rather than adding another census budget heuristic.

Evidence: 399 inline `dep-graph-cache: refresh` runs over 4 days changed 4 labels in total. All 38 runs on the large backlog logged `blocked=0 unblocked=0`. The same backlog had 64 census timeouts (rc=124), 12 slow-repo deferrals and 22 last-good reuses. Mixed repositories still release dependency-ready children through the dependency reconciler's stale sweep and ready lane (GH#38680), the unchanged housekeeping graph stages, and dispatch-time dependency guards.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-repo-meta.sh`: the new `_pulse_candidate_runnable_beside_blocked` helper decides whether a normalizing read has blocked work beside at least one candidate. If so, the read switches to skip mode. Adds the `_PULSE_CANDIDATE_NORMALIZATION_SKIP` constant, which replaces repeated `"skip"` literals.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-readiness-normalization.sh`: the mixed snapshot fetches once, skips, returns the runnable issue, makes no completeness claim and logs the skip. The all-blocked roadmap still normalizes and refetches.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-role-guard.sh`: fixes a pre-existing failure. The test sourced `pulse-repo-meta.sh` while `SCRIPT_DIR` still pointed at `tests/`, so the `infrastructure-advisory-lib.sh` sibling did not resolve. The test failed identically on `main`.

## Decisions

The decision logic was extracted into a helper so `list_dispatchable_issue_candidates_json` stays under the 100-line function-complexity gate. The role-guard test fix is bundled here because it exercises the same module, and a separate PR round trip would cost more than the one-line change.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (pulse candidate enumeration; behaviour narrows an existing optional step)
- **Verification:** self-assessed.
  - `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-readiness-normalization.sh`: 89 passed, 0 failed
  - `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-role-guard.sh`: 16/16 passed (previously exited with rc=1 before running any assertions)

- **Post-deploy check:** `inline dependency normalization skipped for <repo>` lines appear in `pulse.log`, the large backlog's census scans finish without rc=124, and dispatch rounds report candidates in the hundreds.

Resolves #38720

title: GH#38724: fix(pulse-merge): unassigned active status label no longer holds idle interactive PRs forever

title: GH#38727: fix(pulse): census carries fresh last-good candidates for repositories it did not reach
body:
## Summary

A full census that stops early (180s deadline, or a slow-repository deferral) now walks the remaining rotation rows without polling them and appends each unreached repository's fresh last-good candidate list (GH#38483 cache, max age PULSE_CENSUS_LAST_GOOD_MAX_AGE_S, default 3600s, 0 disables). Previously those repositories contributed nothing, so dispatch rounds alternated between ~130 and 1-5 candidates while 7-13 slots were free. Carried repositories get no poll stamp, no cursor advance and no source API read; product discovery stays incomplete. Carried lists drop issues launched after the snapshot was stored (one local dispatch-ledger pass per stopped census), respect pulse schedules, and reapply the PR-backlog and capability-cooldown filters. First waves are unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh

## Decisions

Carry happens after the census loop from the first unpolled row, so the loop and its rotation/deferral semantics are unchanged. Issues dispatched at or after the snapshot time are dropped rather than retried, because the snapshot predates their claim; the next real scan rediscovers them. The PR-backlog filter can perform one cached open-PR read (120s TTL) per carried repository with candidates, matching the existing timeout-reuse path. Interval-throttled repositories are not carried: no registered repository sets pulse_interval.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh: 24/24 PASS including the new GH#38727 case (deadline stop, slow-repository deferral, post-snapshot launch filter, expired list, max-age 0, first-wave no-carry, no stamp/cursor for carried repos). title: GH#38706: fix worker_lifecycle TypeGuard import on Python 3.9; gate 3.10+ typing imports
body:
## Summary

pull_requests_graphql.py imported typing.TypeGuard (3.10+) at runtime since t18923 (v3.39.148), so on macOS CLT Python 3.9 every registry cleanup subcommand (cleanup, cleanup-worktree, retire-enrolled-only, reclaim-unowned, release-vacant-path, release-replaced-path) crashed at import; the profile README routine failed every run and left worktrees. TypeGuard now imports under TYPE_CHECKING (annotations are postponed), preserving mypy narrowing at pull_requests.py:36 and pull_requests_graphql.py:63. The existing Python 3.9 CI/local gate (python-annotation-compat-check.py, GH#34098) now also rejects runtime `from typing import <3.10+ name>` outside TYPE_CHECKING, `sys.version_info >=` guards, or ImportError fallbacks. worker-lifecycle README states the 3.9 runtime floor.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/linters-local-analysis.sh, .agents/scripts/python-annotation-compat-check.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/README.md, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/pull_requests_graphql.py, .github/workflows/code-quality.yml

## Decisions

Rejected typing_extensions (package is stdlib-only) and `-> bool` (drops TypeGuard narrowing; mypy would fail). Did not lower mypy python_version to 3.9: mypy 1.15 then also demands __future__ in two files with local-only unions and newer mypy cannot target 3.9, so the stdlib AST gate is the durable 3.9 enforcement point. Gate covers `from typing import` only; `typing.X` attribute use at runtime is out of scope.

The regression guard is the blocking CI step "Python 3.9 annotation compatibility (GH#34098)" in `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` (also `linters-local.sh` via `check_python_annotation_compat`), extended here. Run against the pre-fix `origin/main` copy of `pull_requests_graphql.py` it fails with `:13: typing.TypeGuard does not exist on Python 3.9`, so any reintroduction blocks the PR. An import test under `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/` would not catch this class of bug: GitHub-hosted runners and every maintainer's `python3` used by the suite are 3.10+, where the import succeeds. Reproducing the failure needs a 3.9 interpreter (macOS CLT `/usr/bin/python3`), which CI does not provide. The 3.9 runtime was exercised manually; see Runtime Testing.

title: GH#38730: perf(pulse): bounded-parallel full candidate census
body:
## Summary

Full dispatch candidate censuses now run repository scans concurrently, up to `PULSE_CENSUS_MAX_PARALLEL` at a time (default 4; 1 = serial; capped at 16). Previously each scan made 5-6 GitHub reads one after another, so a serial census of about 25 awake repositories hit its 180s deadline in most cycles while worker slots sat idle.

Resolves #38730

## Evidence (pulse.log, before)

- 22 of the last 40 full censuses hit the deadline; mean census time was 143s.
- 20 of the last 40 `Dispatch_max` rounds had ≤5 candidates and ≥5 free slots.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
  - `_dispatch_census_parallelism`: validated limit. First waves always stay serial, because they stop as soon as they have enough candidates to fill free slots.
  - `_dispatch_census_scan_repo`: one scan (enumerate, then the capability-cooled filter) writing per-scan `.json` / `.complete` / `.rc` files, so it can run in the background.
  - `_dispatch_census_start_scan` / `_dispatch_census_wait_for_slot`: the census waits for a free slot *before* measuring the remaining deadline, so every scan's budget is still clamped to the census deadline.
  - `_dispatch_census_absorb_scans`: collects results in launch order, so ranking input never depends on completion order. It keeps scan-failure, product-completeness and partial-wave semantics as flag bits.
  - `_dispatch_census_await_scan`: a scan still running 30s after the deadline is terminated and counted as a failed scan, so the census can never wait without limit.

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`: `_dispatch_finish_ranked_census` no longer takes the removed shared completeness file (its only caller is updated).

  - a failed scan excluded

  - real process-group timeouts draining under concurrency with no leaked output

title: GH#38747: fix(pulse): bounded stage starvation fuse
body:
## Summary

Elastic dispatch (GH#37874) now fills whole Pulse cycles, so every stage measured against the cycle-start clock defers. Stages that take 2-12s and feed throughput have gone unrun for about 28h: `reap_orphan_workers` frees slots, and `stale_queued_runs` deletes ghost Actions runs (524 were queued). This PR adds a bounded **stage starvation fuse** to the deferral branch of `_pulse_stage_cycle_timeout`.

Resolves #38747

## What changed

`.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`:

- `_pulse_stage_note_start`: when this process owns the instance lock, record when each statically named stage starts. Dynamic `dispatch_candidate_<n>` names are skipped.
- `_pulse_stage_starvation_fuse`: runs only when a stage would otherwise defer. If the stage has never started, or last started more than `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_STARVATION_S` (default 3600) ago, it runs once. Its timeout is the smallest of:
  - the stage timeout;
  - `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_FUSE_TIMEOUT_S` (default 120);
  - what is left of the per-cycle shared budget `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_FUSE_BUDGET_S` (default 300);
  - the owner lock lease: heartbeat + `PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S` − reserve − now. Contenders use this same lease in `_instance_lock_publication_age` before force-reclaiming.
- No fuse runs:
  - without a valid owner heartbeat;
  - when the stop flag exists;
  - when the grant would be under 15s;
  - while a main-dispatch reserve is protected.
- `_pulse_stage_fuse_finish`: charges the fused stage's real duration (or its timeout) to the cycle's budget. The budget is keyed by owner PID and `PULSE_START_EPOCH`, so spend from earlier cycles is ignored.
- Each fused run is logged: `Stage starvation fuse: <stage> last_start_age=<s> timeout=<s>s fuse_spent=<s>s (GH#38747)`.
- `_pulse_stage_record_timing`: the timing-record `printf` that was duplicated in the timeout and completion paths of `run_stage_with_timeout` now lives in one helper, which also charges the fuse budget. This keeps the function under the 100-line complexity gate.

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh`: its fixture copies `run_stage_with_timeout` from source and stubs `_pulse_stage_cycle_timeout`. It now stubs the two new helpers the same way.

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`: new `assert_stage_starvation_fuse_contract`. It drives the real `run_stage_with_timeout` with a file-backed clock and covers:

- a starved stage is fused, stamped and logged;
- a recent stage still defers;
- the same stage is not fused twice in one cycle;
- an exhausted shared budget blocks the fuse;
- a new cycle resets spend;
- real duration is charged;
- dynamic names, a foreign lock owner, an expired lease, the stop flag and a protected dispatch reserve all defer.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`: 98 tests, 0 failures, including `PASS: starved stages run once from a bounded fuse inside the owner lease (GH#38747)`.
- All 21 other suites that source `pulse-watchdog.sh` or call `run_stage_with_timeout` pass, including `test-runner-capability.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`, `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`, `test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh`, `test-watchdog-no-false-kill.sh`, `test-pulse-prefetch-stage-budget.sh` and `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh`.
- Two suites fail identically on `main` without this change, so their failures predate this PR:
  - `test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh`: a stale lease-recovery assertion from before t18978, filed as #38753.
  - `test-pulse-watchdog-tick.sh`: fails after its systemd cases on macOS; follow-up to be filed.

After deploy, I'll check that `rg "Stage starvation fuse" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` shows fused runs, that `reap_orphan_workers` and `stale_queued_runs` complete at least hourly, and that the queued Actions run count falls.

title: GH#38779: fix(pulse): retry blocker recovery after failed supervisor attempts; fall back from backed-off thinking tier
body:
## Summary

Terminal-blocker recovery, the only path that clears `needs-ai-recovery` holds, went 20h without running on a busy host. This PR fixes the two causes behind that.

- **Recovery cadence** (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh`, `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due`): the 3h window was stamped before the failure-cooldown check and before the run. After one failed or restart-killed attempt, recovery waited 3h, not the 30-minute failure retry. A check inside the cooldown also used up the window without running. Now:
  - when the latest attempt is newer than the latest success, the interval drops to `PULSE_LLM_FAILURE_RETRY_INTERVAL` (default 1800);
  - the cooldown is checked before the stamp is written;
  - the second, redundant cooldown check is removed.
- **Tier fallback** (`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`): if the thinking-tier supervisor child exits `75` within `PULSE_SUPERVISOR_TIER_FALLBACK_MAX_SECONDS` (default 300), all thinking-tier models were backed off at selection and nothing ran. In that case it retries once at `PULSE_SUPERVISOR_FALLBACK_TIER` (default `standard`; empty disables). It never retries an explicit `PULSE_MODEL` pin or a session that ran. Launch-and-watch moved into `_run_pulse_supervisor_child`; the log, blocker reconciliation and return contract of `run_pulse` are unchanged.

## Evidence

From one host's `pulse.log`, the last supervisor success was at epoch `1794845588`. Three recovery attempts followed and none succeeded:

- two `rc=75` exits at 60s, each stopping after `pre_model_select tier=thinking`;
- one attempt killed by a bundle-activation restart.

Each failure pushed the next check about 3h out. Over the same period `needs-ai-recovery` holds aged to 52h while pulse health reported `workers=5/20`.

## Verification

- `test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`: 19/19 pass, including the new cases (g)–(j). Against `main`'s supervisor module, (g) and (i) fail and (h) passes, so the new cases detect the defect.
- `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh` and `test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` all pass.
- ShellCheck is clean, and pre-commit passes, including the Bash 3.2 parse check.
- After deploy: `rg "LLM supervisor (attempt started|completed successfully|failed)|Supervisor tier fallback" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`

Follow-up, not in this PR: a bundle-activation restart still kills an in-flight supervisor. With this change that costs 30 minutes instead of 3h.

Resolves #38779

title: GH#38785: fix(pulse): fetch lagging canonical tip objects so the large-file gate stops deferring
body:
## Summary

The large-file gate measures pinned remote blobs when a canonical mirror lags, but _pulse_refresh_repo never obtained the remote tip objects, so worker-merged tips (created on the forge) left the gate in a permanent benign deferral. Refresh now fetches the pinned tip objects into a pulse-owned bare sidecar cache that borrows canonical objects via objects/info/alternates; the gate reads pinned blobs from the canonical store or that cache. Canonical refs, HEAD, index, worktree and object store are never written: the canonical Git guard forbids canonical fetches (fetch is not in READ_ONLY; object writes such as hash-object -w are treated as mutations), so this design needs no guard-policy change. Upstream-added targets are now measured from the pinned tree (exactly one regular-blob resolver variant) instead of deferring; ambiguous or non-blob entries still fail closed. Persistent fetch failure escalates to a local advisory after PULSE_TIP_OBJECTS_ADVISORY_AFTER_SECONDS (default 3600) and clears on recovery. Deferral log lines now state the specific cause.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gate-pull-before-measure.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-large-file-gate-continuation-verify.sh

## Decisions

Rejected automatic sync-mirror (canonical synchronization requires explicit authorization) and rejected loosening canonical_git_policy to allow object-only canonical fetches (security-boundary change). Sidecar cache is rebuilt per new tip and swapped atomically, bounding disk to one delta; it is removed once the canonical checkout holds the tip. Cache and advisory state live under ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/supervisor and ~/.aidevops/advisories (overridable for tests).

An earlier iteration fetched objects directly into the canonical store; sandbox tests passed but the live run failed because the sandbox was not a managed canonical root, so the guard never engaged. The regression now registers its sandbox through AIDEVOPS_REPOS_FILE and runs under the repository guard shim, with a probe asserting the guard blocks canonical fetch (exit 42).

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified against the live guarded canonical checkout with the real git guard shim on PATH: the sidecar fetch succeeded (84K cache via alternates negotiation) and canonical HEAD, refs, count-objects and status were unchanged; the gate read a pinned blob through the object-source resolver. New regressions in test-gate-pull-before-measure.sh run under the real canonical Git guard (sandbox registered as a managed root; probe confirms canonical fetch is blocked): remote tip absent locally -> cache holds tip, canonical objects/refs/HEAD/index/worktree unchanged, gate measures pinned blob without deferral; advisory escalation and self-clear. Updated test-large-file-gate-continuation-verify.sh for upstream-added targets (58/58). shellcheck clean; 14 related suites pass after rebase onto current origin/main.

Resolves #38785

title: t19074: perf(pulse): bound cooperative-drain tail skips so maintenance cannot starve
body:
## Summary

Drained Pulse cycles no longer skip their maintenance tail indefinitely. When the last completed tail is older than a bound, a drained cycle runs its remaining non-dispatch stages once. Dispatch from the old bundle stays suppressed throughout.

## Why

The t19015 (GH#38413) drain fast exit skips every remaining stage of a cooperatively drained cycle. The GH#38747 starvation fuse only acts on stages that start, and skipped stages never start. Pulse logs showed the gap:

- Since 2026-11-16T06Z, 12 of 33 cycles ended at a drain exit. `preflight_early_dispatch` averaged 1192s (n=35), and bundle activations recur about hourly.
- `stale_queued_runs`, `reap_orphan_workers` and `redirect_spam_sweep` went more than 30 hours without a start. Graph stages ran 6 hours apart.
- One managed repo built up 282 queued Actions runs, 70 of them job-less runs from six days earlier.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`:
  - `_pulse_drain_tail_note_complete` stamps `maintenance_tail.complete` in the stage-state directory. Only the lock owner writes it.
  - `_pulse_drain_tail_starved` decides once per cycle whether the tail is starved, caches the verdict and logs once. The bound is `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_DRAIN_TAIL_STARVATION_S`, defaulting to `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_STARVATION_S` (3600s); `0` disables it. A missing stamp counts as starved.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` `_pulse_cycle_drain_exit`: returns "continue" when the tail is starved. `cycle_final_refill` always keeps the fast exit, because `pulse_event_refill_drain` never reads the drain marker and would consume the retained trigger with no launch.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` `_pulse_run_deterministic_pipeline`: stamps completion after `_pulse_pipeline_maintenance_stages`.

## Safety

- **No dispatch from the drained bundle:** `_dispatch_compute_capacity` (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:959`), `_dispatch_min_worker_floor_refill` (`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1876`) and the capacity floor (`pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh:211`) still read `_pulse_drain_requested_bundle`. The event-refill path keeps its fast exit.
- **Escape hatches unchanged:** `PULSE_DRAIN_FAST_EXIT=0` still disables fast exit, and `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_DRAIN_TAIL_STARVATION_S=0` restores pure t19015 behaviour.
- **Bounded cost:** cycle-budget clamps and the lifecycle hard cap (7200s) still bound a drained cycle that runs its tail. Activation waits for at most one tail per bound.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` on the three files: clean.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: all local checks passed. The shfmt advisory differences predate this change and are outside the diff.
- Existing suites passed: `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`, `test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`, `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`, `test-permission-block-breaker.sh` (it extracts `_pulse_run_deterministic_pipeline`) and `test-pulse-event-refill.sh`.
- Ad hoc probe (not committed) ran the real extracted functions against a lock-owner fixture. 14/14 cases passed:
  - A missing or stale stamp overrides; a fresh stamp keeps the fast exit.
  - The verdict is cached and logged once.
  - `cycle_final_refill` exits even under an override.
  - A bound of `0` or a non-numeric bound disables the override.
  - A non-owner neither overrides nor stamps.
  - The no-drain and `PULSE_DRAIN_FAST_EXIT=0` paths are unchanged.

Post-deploy check: `rg "maintenance tail starved" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, then confirm that `stale_queued_runs` in `pulse-stage-timings.log` starts within the bound.

Resolves #38802

title: t19075: perf(pulse): park 403-undeletable ghost runs so the stale-queued watchdog stops re-probing them
body:
## Summary

The stale-queued watchdog (`.agents/scripts/pulse-stale-queued-runs.sh`) re-probed every known job-less ghost run on every scan. GitHub refuses `DELETE` on a still-queued ghost with HTTP 403 (`Could not delete the workflow run`), so each ghost cost about 10 REST calls per scan, every scan, forever. A standalone run spent its full 900 s budget on 75+ ghosts in the first repository and never reached later repositories.

This PR parks a refused ghost as `<run-id>.undeletable`. Later scans skip it with no API calls until `AIDEVOPS_STALE_QUEUED_GHOST_REPROBE_HOURS` (default 24) expires. After that, at most 5 expired ghosts are re-probed per repository scan. Only an explicit 403 parks a run. Other DELETE failures, REST admission denials and read errors keep today's retry behaviour.

This matters now because t19074 (PR #38804) makes the maintenance tail run hourly again under cooperative drains. Without this fix, each tail would burn shared REST budget on ghosts that cannot be removed.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-stale-queued-runs.sh`:
  - `_sq_api` now classifies `HTTP 403`.
  - New helpers `_sq_ghost_park` and `_sq_ghost_parked` (TTL check and per-scan re-probe cap).
  - `_sq_handle_run` skips parked ghosts before any API call, and parks a ghost after a 403 in both `delete-failed` branches.
  - `SQ_GHOST_REPROBES` resets per repository scan.
- `.agents/reference/github-runner-stale-queued-watchdog.md`: adds a row for the new setting and explains the 403 park.
- `TODO.md` and `todo/tasks/t19075-brief.md`: task entry and brief.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x -P .agents/scripts .agents/scripts/pulse-stale-queued-runs.sh`: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-orphaned-job-rerun.sh`: PASS. It shares `_sq_api` and the scan paths.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: passed, with no new complexity or nesting violations.
- An ad hoc probe against a stubbed `gh` that counts calls passed 7/7 cases (not committed):
  - The first 403 probe costs 10 calls, logs `delete-failed` and writes the marker.
  - Within the TTL, a parked ghost costs 0 API calls and logs nothing.
  - After expiry, a ghost beyond the 5-per-scan cap stays skipped. One under the cap is re-probed and re-parked with a fresh epoch.
  - A non-403 (500) DELETE failure does not park the run.
  - A corrupt marker reads as expired, is re-probed once and is rewritten.
- Runtime check after deploy: a standalone `pulse-stale-queued-runs.sh` run parks the ghosts and reaches later repositories. On a second run, parked ghosts cost no REST calls.

Resolves #38810

title: t19076: fix(pulse): repair worktrees left half-deleted by interrupted cleanup before reusing them
body:
## Summary

Workers kept inheriting worktrees that a cleanup pass had killed halfway through `git worktree remove`. Those trees are still registered, but tracked files such as `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `turbo.json` and `tooling/` are gone from disk. Dispatch preserved them as "dirty same-runner resumes", workers could not install or build, and they reported `runner_capability_unmet`.

This PR changes two things:

- **Dispatch repair** (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`): added `_dlw_restore_missing_tracked_files`. Before a reused worktree is classified as dirty, this function restores missing tracked files from HEAD with `git checkout -- .`. It acts only when unstaged deletions (` D `) are the only tracked change. Untracked files are never touched, and any modified, staged or renamed tracked file means nothing is done (GH#27138 resume preservation is unchanged). The restore is logged with the file count.
- **Cause fix** (`.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh`): `_recover_interactive_capacity` now passes `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_CLEAN_DEADLINE_EPOCH` to `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --capacity`. `_clean_capacity_checkpoint` then starts no new removal once that deadline has passed. The hard `timeout_sec` is now a backstop: it fires only after a grace period (`AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_CLEAN_REMOVAL_GRACE_S`, default 90s). Without the env deadline, behaviour is unchanged.

## Evidence

- A read-only scan on one runner found 33 linked worktrees whose only change is unstaged tracked-file deletions. Deleted counts range from 126 to 27,567.
- In `cleanup_worktrees.log`, 17 of 81 `Removing feature/auto-…` lines are immediately followed by `interactive-capacity budget exhausted; progress unverified … rc=124`.
- One managed-repo issue lost two worker attempts to "tooling/* and turbo.json still deleted from disk". `runner_capability_unmet` is that repo's largest blocker family: 36 attempts over 30 issues in 24h.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x -P .agents/scripts` on all three files: clean.
- `tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh`: 62/62 pass.
- `tests/test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh`: 5/5 pass.
- `tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`: 45/45 pass.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: all checks pass. The shfmt advisory diffs are on pre-existing lines only.
- An ad hoc probe against a real git repo and linked worktrees passed 7/7. A deletion-only tree is restored and untracked files are kept. Mixed deletion+edit trees and staged deletions are left untouched. A clean tree is a no-op.
- A deadline probe passed 6/6. No deadline or a future deadline admits removal, and a past deadline stops the pass without advancing the cursor. An invalid value is ignored, and non-capacity mode is unaffected.

Runtime check after deploy: `rg -c "tracked files missing after an interrupted worktree removal" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` should be > 0 when a carcass is reused. New `budget exhausted` lines should stop appearing right after `Removing` lines.

Resolves #38818

title: GH#38803: fix(blender-render): Runpod cloud type, capacity retry, verified Blender bootstrap, fetch-gated pod removal
body:
## Summary

Fixes the gaps in `.agents/scripts/blender-render-helper.sh` (Runpod adapter) found by code review in #38803 and by today's live smoke tests ([findings](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/38803#issuecomment-6952923410)).

- **Cloud type**: `submit --cloud-type SECURE|COMMUNITY` (default SECURE, runpodctl's default). It is passed to `pod create` and included in the contract text and approval token, so the quoted rate matches the tier.
- **Capacity**: the Runpod `bad_request` "no longer any instances available" refusal creates nothing. It is retried a bounded number of times (`BRH_CAPACITY_RETRIES`=3, `BRH_CAPACITY_RETRY_SECS`=20), followed by a clear stop. All other create errors keep the existing never-retry behaviour.
- **Pinned Blender without a custom image**: `package --blender-sha256 <published hash>` writes `render_worker.sh`. On the pod it downloads the official `blender-X.Y.Z-linux-x64.tar.xz`, verifies the SHA256 and renders. The hash is in the manifest, so it is covered by the token, and `stage` refuses a modified worker script.
- **sshd under `--docker-args`**: the pod command starts the image's `/start.sh` (sshd from `PUBLIC_KEY`) before waiting for `stage`.
- **Fetch-gated removal (defect)**: pods used to delete themselves right after rendering, before `fetch` could copy the frames. They now write `.rendered` and wait up to `--fetch-minutes` (default 10, added to the worst-case ceiling). `fetch` releases a pod (`.fetched`) only if the pod had finished before the copy.
- **Logs**: `status --live` prints each pod's `BRH_STAGE`/`BRH_GPU`/`BRH_RESULT`/`BRH_FAIL` lines from `runpodctl pod logs`, so progress needs no SSH.
- **Docs**: `3d-render-backends.md` (helper flags, lifecycle, measured timings), `runpod.md` (no-capacity error, community SSH, `/start.sh`), `saladcloud.md` (pending state, render with CUDA not OptiX, `aidevops secret` dropping the second `--`).

## Evidence

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/blender-render-helper.sh`: clean. Pre-commit ratchets pass.
- Dry-run harness (helper product path):
  - `package` with and without `--blender-sha256`; a bad hash or an `X.Y` version is refused.
  - The token changes with `--cloud-type` and with `--fetch-minutes`.
  - The create command includes `--cloud-type COMMUNITY`, and the in-pod command passes `bash -n`.
  - Over-budget and invalid cloud types are refused.
  - `fetch` dry-run prints the release step.
- Local run of the generated `render_worker.sh` (Metal, image-PATH mode): `BRH_RESULT rc=0 frames_written=2`.
- Live, Runpod: three `submit --live` runs (4090 COMMUNITY) each showed `retry 1/3..3/3`, then the stop message. `runpodctl pod list` returned `[]`, so nothing was created.
- Live smoke tests behind these changes:
  - Runpod RTX 4090 community: Blender 5.3.0 verified in 120 s, OptiX render 1.7 s, about $0.02.
  - SaladCloud RTX 3090 low priority: CUDA render 1.4 s. OptiX failed with error 7804 because `libnvoptix` is absent.

## Regression Evidence

No repository test was added. The changed behaviour depends on billable, credentialed provider APIs (Runpod pod create and logs, an SSH-reachable pod, NVIDIA drivers) that CI cannot reach without spend, and the repo has no existing `blender-render-helper` test suite to extend. Per the gate policy (no new test infrastructure by default), regression evidence comes from the product paths instead:
- `shellcheck` and the pre-commit ratchets.
- The dry-run harness that drives the real helper (`package`/`submit`/`fetch`), with its outputs listed under Evidence.
- A local run of the generated `render_worker.sh`.
- Live Runpod create attempts that exercised the capacity-retry branch with no pod created.

## Remaining

The full live helper flow (`submit` → `stage` over SSH → `fetch` → `teardown --live`) on a real pod is still unverified. Runpod had no RTX 4090 community capacity during this session. #38803 stays open for that operator-approved run, so this PR uses `For`.

Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.3 - 04 Nov 2026

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

4.39.2 - 03 Nov 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072

Updates `anomalyco/opencode/github` from 2.2.5 to 2.2.7
Release notes

Sourced from anomalyco/opencode/github's releases.

v2.2.7

Highlights

  • GitHub Copilot Auto: Pick Auto in the model picker when your Copilot account has an Auto pool, and Copilot's router chooses the model for each session at the Auto discount. If routing fails, OpenCode falls back to the account's default chat model. (#62997)
  • Side Panel Tab Shortcuts: Right-click a side panel tab and choose Close tabs to the right. ⌘W now closes side panel tabs wherever focus is, ⌥⌘W or Ctrl+Alt+W always closes the session tab, and ⌘⇧T reopens the last closed tab of either kind where it was. (#62922)
  • Mark Sessions Read or Unread: Open the menu on a tab, Home row, project row or inbox card and choose Mark as unread to keep its dot until you next visit. (#62889)

Breaking changes

@opencode/ai: ImageResponse.image is removed

This affects code that imports @opencode/ai directly. Read response.images[0] instead of response.image. (#63011)

SDK: fewer endpoints wait for plugins to load

On a Location that is still loading plugins, agent.list returns the agents loaded so far, and integration.list, usage.limits, vcs.init, rpc.call and artifact.* no longer wait up to 5 seconds. Entries and actions that a plugin provides appear when it finishes loading, so refresh on the matching *.updated event. Model, provider, generate.*, voice.* and websearch.query endpoints still wait. (#62796, #63040)

Core

Improvements

  • MCP Logins Stay Signed In: Remote MCP servers that rotate refresh tokens no longer sign you out when several clients refresh at once or the token endpoint fails for a moment. (#62827, #63012)
  • read accepts a negative offset to read from the end of a file, such as -50 for the last 50 lines. An offset past the end returns the last lines and the file's line count instead of failing. (#62147)
  • When read can't find a file, it suggests close names: different capitalization, another extension, a small typo, or the matching path inside the project. (#62147)
  • Shell results end with Exit code: N. Commands killed by a signal show the signal name, and timeouts say how long they waited and suggest a larger timeout. (#62141)
  • Prompt cache warming times its pings from the model's cache.ttl by default (interval: "auto"), or every 4 minutes without a TTL. Models whose cache outlasts the warming duration are no longer pinged. (#62831)
  • When MCP servers connect, disconnect or change tools, Code Mode sends the model a short list of what changed instead of the whole tool catalog. (#62176)

Bug fixes

  • GitHub Copilot session costs use the amount Copilot charged instead of the catalog estimate, and content-filter errors name the filter that blocked the response. (#62034)
  • GitHub Copilot picks up a new API endpoint after a plan change on its next model refresh, so you no longer have to sign in again. (#62171)
  • Remote MCP servers that rotate refresh tokens no longer log you out when the TUI, desktop app, background service or several projects refresh the same login at once. (#62827)
  • A temporary failure while refreshing an MCP OAuth token keeps your login for the next try instead of marking the server needs_auth. (#63012)
  • MCP tool calls no longer fail when the server's result doesn't match the tool's own output schema, so completed actions aren't reported as failed. (#61254)
  • MCP prompts stay available when refreshing a server's prompt list fails. (#62266)
  • With background_compaction on, a background summary no longer stops a running Claude Agent session mid tool call. (#63025)
  • After opencode auth logout on a .well-known integration, its remote providers and policies stop applying until you log back in. (#62760)
  • OpenCode Console workspace policies still apply when Console's instructions or skills fail to load. (#62702)
  • Cloudflare AI Gateway providers set up with only gatewayApiKey now send that key. (#62574)
  • A v1 model override that sets only some capabilities no longer resets the others, so catalog capabilities like PDF input are kept. (#62573)
  • A v1 provider config that sets both api and options.baseURL keeps options.baseURL. (#62570)
  • Legacy model references with an inline variant, such as "openai/gpt-5#high", keep the variant. (#62254)
  • A fresh install imports saved provider credentials from the legacy auth.json, and skips an invalid one with a warning instead of stopping setup. (#62568)
  • Cache warming stops for a session when a ping rebuilds the cache instead of reading it, counts its interval from when a request was sent, and no longer pings during compaction or after the session is deleted. (#62926, #62941, #62972)
  • Tokens and cost from session.generate requests, including cache warming pings, count toward the session's totals. (#63006)
  • Under zsh, a glob that matches nothing, like rm *.tmp, is passed through as bash does instead of stopping the command. (#62141)
  • Truncated shell output that starts mid-line drops the partial first line, so the "showing lines X–Y" notice is exact. (#62141)
  • On Windows, multi-line commands no longer lose everything after the first line with PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store. (#62522)
  • read no longer cuts an emoji in half when it shortens a long line. (#62575)

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from anomalyco/opencode/github's changelog.

Changelog

Release notes for OpenCode V2, newest first.

v2.3.0 — 2026-11-13

Highlights

  • Background Subagents by Default: Subagents now return immediately, continue in the background, and report back whenever they become idle. You can keep working in the parent session while multiple subagents run concurrently. (#63382)
  • Quieter Transcripts by Default: The TUI now summarizes each run of tool calls and thoughts into one collapsible activity row, so the answer is easier to follow. To see every step again, set Verbosity to medium or high in settings, or set session.verbosity in your TUI config; an existing setting is kept. (#63207)
  • Jump to an Earlier Prompt: In the desktop app, open Jump to message from the command palette or press Cmd+Alt+G (Ctrl+Alt+G on Windows and Linux) to search prompts across the current session and jump directly to one. (#63585)

Core

Improvements

  • Subagents now always run in the background, return their session ID immediately, and report results to their parent whenever they become idle. (#63382)
  • Added experimental support for MCP events, behind the mcp_events flag. (#63254, #63261, #63269)
  • Shell commands now survive server handoffs and keep their output when interrupted.
  • Added experimental support for moving a shell command to the background when its timeout expires, behind the shell_timeout_background flag. With the flag on, an explicit timeout on a background command stops it. (#63024, #63703)
  • Local Windows shell commands now run through the process daemon.
  • Added support for freeform tool input on compatible models.
  • Added LM Studio decision-model support.
  • Agents are now told when their session is a fork. Thanks @​hasta84. (#63235)
  • Tool output truncation now keeps the beginning of the output and preserves a usable preview if the full output cannot be saved.
  • Tail reads no longer load the entire file into memory.
  • Providers can present a client certificate for gateways that require mutual TLS. Set settings.tls with cert, key and an optional passphrase on the provider; values accept {file:} and {env:} like apiKey. (#61832)
  • When a subagent goes idle while its own background work is still running, its report to the parent now says it is still running, so the parent waits for the final report instead of treating the partial answer as done. (#63675)
  • Code Mode gets simpler structured results from file and skill tools: write and edit return their confirmation as a string, patch returns an empty result, and skill returns the skill's directory and content. (#63616, #63635, #63618, #63623)

Bug fixes

  • Fixed case-only file renames in patches on case-insensitive filesystems.
  • Fixed stale thinking being retained after Claude Agent prompts or tools change.
  • Fixed directly driven child sessions not resuming after a restart.
  • Fixed plugin replacement stopping when cleanup of an earlier plugin fails.
  • Fixed MCP OAuth refreshes and localhost redirects when a server rewrites 127.0.0.1.
  • Fixed saved API keys being omitted from local-model discovery.
  • Local model discovery (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) waits up to 15 seconds per request instead of 1, so remote or tunnelled endpoints list their models, and a slow endpoint no longer delays other endpoints or config reloads. (#63700)
  • In Code Mode, calling a namespace as if it were a tool now suggests up to three real tools under it. (#63697)
  • Fixed retryable provider streams losing completed work when interrupted.
  • Fixed GitHub Copilot requests using the wrong endpoint before models finish loading.
  • Fixed exhausted request rate limits being treated as terminal. Thanks @​Kyle-j-bush. (#59816)
  • Fixed LM Studio models with a null context length and accepted decision-type models. Thanks @​tomzhu1024. (#56214)

TUI

Improvements

  • Transcript verbosity now defaults to low, which summarizes each run of tools and thoughts into one activity row. A session.verbosity you already set is kept. (#63207)

title: GH#38824: reuse resolved admin dir in archive restore (partial)
body:
## Summary

Partial step: this PR alone cannot meet the timing targets within the authorized scope.

For #38824

Falls back to the old call when there is no bundle. No guard re-check is crossed.

## Profile (baseline, before this change, this machine)

- `test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`: 178 tests in 2126 s (target <300 s). Slowest: 56.5, 55.6, 54.8 s (target <10 s each).
