title: GH#38840: fix(pulse): let starved critical stages borrow a bounded slice of the protected dispatch reserve
body:
## Summary

A starved safety stage that runs before the main dispatch round can now start again. When the main-dispatch reserve is protected, a budget-priority `critical` stage starved past the existing bound borrows a capped slice of that reserve once. Deferrable stages still defer.

## Why

The GH#38747 starvation fuse refuses any grant while `_PULSE_MAIN_DISPATCH_RESERVE_S` is protected (`dispatch_reserved == 1`). On a runner where early dispatch fills the cycle clock, the reserve is protected for every stage before the main round. That includes the stages the fuse was written for. Runtime evidence from v3.39.222 on one 20-slot runner, 2026-11-17T17:30Z:

- `pulse.log` has 98 `Stage deferred: … cycle budget exhausted` lines each for `stale_queued_runs` and `reap_orphan_workers`, 85 for `preflight_capacity` and 77 for `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger`.
- `Stage starvation fuse:` appears twice, both for post-dispatch drain-tail stages.
- `reap_orphan_workers` and `stale_queued_runs` last started at 2026-11-16T06:06Z, 35 hours earlier. The released GH#38810 ghost-run parking has never executed, and the GH#38802 acceptance criterion (starts within 2 hours) failed.
- These stages are short: the reaper averages 2.1 s, stale queued-run cleanup 11.9 s and capacity refresh 2 s.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`:
  - `_pulse_stage_reserve_borrow_budget` (new): prints `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_RESERVE_BORROW_S` (default 120; `0` disables) for stages that `_pulse_stage_priority_class` reports as `critical`. It fails closed when the classifier is not loaded.
  - `_pulse_stage_starvation_fuse` takes an optional borrow budget. The budget caps the per-cycle fuse budget, and the log line adds `reserve_borrow=<n>s`.
  - `_pulse_stage_cycle_timeout`: under a protected reserve, a stage that may borrow is fused with the finalisation reserve for the lease check, because the dispatch reserve is the thing being lent. All other paths are unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`: new `assert_stage_reserve_borrow_contract`, kept separate from the GH#38747 contract so both stay under the 100-line function gate. It checks five cases:
  - With no classifier, the stage defers.
  - A deferrable stage defers.
  - A borrow budget of `0` defers.
  - A starved critical stage is granted 120 s minus the 40 s already spent (80 s).
  - Once less than 15 s of borrow is left, the stage defers.

## Safety

- **Bounded dispatch cost:** the main round loses at most the borrow budget per cycle, which is under 10% of its ~1290 s reserve. This only happens in cycles with a critical stage starved past `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_STARVATION_S` (3600 s). The `.start` stamp stops a second borrow by the same stage inside that window.
- **Unchanged:** deferrable stages (graph, sync, dirty-PR sweep, Dependabot), dispatch candidates, nested stages, foreign owners and stop flags. The GH#37811 unadmittable-round release and the normal post-dispatch fuse are also unchanged.
- **Rollback:** set `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_RESERVE_BORROW_S=0` at runtime, or revert.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x -P .agents/scripts` on both files: clean. `/bin/bash -n` on the test (Bash 3.2 parse): clean.
- `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`: 99/99 under `/bin/bash` 3.2. The GH#38747 fuse contract is unchanged and still passes.
- `test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh`: PASS. `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`: 85/85.
- Real classifier probe (`pulse-budget-priority.sh`): `reap_orphan_workers`, `stale_queued_runs`, `preflight_capacity`, `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` and `redirect_spam_sweep` are `critical`. `build_dependency_graph_cache`, `dirty_pr_sweep` and `dependabot_alert_monitor` are `deferrable`.

Post-deploy check: `rg "Stage starvation fuse: .*reserve_borrow" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, then confirm new `reap_orphan_workers` and `stale_queued_runs` rows in `pulse-stage-timings.log`.

## Decisions

Borrowing is limited to the critical class and capped at 120 s per cycle, so long deferrable stages cannot consume the main round. Moving these stages ahead of early dispatch was rejected.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed. Shellcheck and `/bin/bash -n` are clean. Suites: `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh` 99/99 under `/bin/bash` 3.2, `test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh` PASS, `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` 85/85. A probe of the real classifier confirms the critical/deferrable mapping.

Resolves #38840

title: GH#38822: fix affected worktree/pulse suites on a clean runner
body:
## Summary

Fixes fixture and environment assumptions in 6 of the 8 suites listed in #38822 (two already passed on a fresh HOME) so they pass on a fresh HOME as a non-root user. Production changes: worktree-archive-helper.sh capacity estimate no longer refreshes the source index (diff.autoRefreshIndex=false); worktree-clean-lib.sh index-readable check treats an absent source as nothing to read, so stale-metadata pruning proceeds. Tests: isolated repos.json/lifecycle state/registry DB, registry-enrolled fixture worktrees (GH#38667), portable grep instead of rg, bash on TEST_PATH, retargeted greps for logic that moved to headless-runtime-canary.sh. title: GH#38803: fix(blender-render): stage without chown on Runpod SECURE MooseFS; require teardown after fetch
body:
## Summary

These fixes come from the first live run of the full `blender-render-helper.sh` flow (`submit` → `stage` → `status` → `fetch` → `teardown`). It ran on 1× Runpod A40 SECURE at $0.59/hr, approved by the operator, for about $0.04.

- **`stage` on SECURE pods**: `/workspace` is a MooseFS FUSE mount (`mfs#eu-se-1.runpod.net:9421`), where `rsync -av` fails to `chown` (`Operation not permitted`, exit 23). `stage` then aborted before writing `.staged`. It now uses `rsync -rtLv --no-owner --no-group`. The live pod was staged by hand with the same flags minus `-L`, which succeeded. `-L` was added after review: without `-a`'s `--links`, rsync skips symlinked inputs (`skipping non-regular file`, reproduced locally), and `-L` sends their hashed target contents.
- **Pod removal after `fetch`**: the pod was released by `fetch`, but at `teardown` it was `EXITED`, not deleted, and a stopped pod can still bill storage. The `fetch` messages, help text and contract text now say to run `teardown --live`, and so does `3d-render-backends.md`. The contract text change also changes approval tokens.
- **Docs**: added the measured A40 run to `.agents/tools/design/3d-render-backends.md`.

## Evidence

- Live run: on the 3rd capacity attempt (RTX 4090 and 3090 were refused on both tiers), pod `BRH_GPU NVIDIA A40, 595.112.07`. Log: `blender 5.3.0 verified and ready in 85s`, OptiX render, `BRH_RESULT rc=0 frames_written=1`. `fetch` reported `All 1 expected frames present`. `teardown --live` returned `deleted: true` and then `pod list` was `[]`.
- `shellcheck`, `lint-shell-portability.sh` and pre-commit ratchets pass.
- A `stage` dry run prints the new rsync flags. The local dry-run harness and the generated `render_worker.sh` (Metal, 2 frames) pass.

## Regression Evidence

No repository test was added. The fixed behaviour needs a live Runpod SECURE pod (MooseFS `/workspace`) and the provider's pod lifecycle, which CI cannot reach without credentials and spend. The repo has no `blender-render-helper` test suite. The evidence is the live run above, plus the dry-run output that shows the exact flags.

## Remaining

- Why the pod's own `runpodctl pod delete $RUNPOD_POD_ID` left it `EXITED` is unknown, because the pod's logs were gone after deletion. `teardown --live` is now the documented removal step either way.

Resolves #38803

title: GH#35043 GH#38701: feat(sandbox): opt-in SRT egress prototype, qualified on NixOS
body:
## Scope of this PR

Two commits. `main` does not yet contain the prototype, so this PR introduces
both:

| Commit | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `d0691b4c90` | `GH#35043` — the opt-in SRT egress qualification prototype (backend, test, reference doc, pinned npm project) |
| `1b691afef1` | `GH#38701` — require a `which(1)` envelope tool so the prototype qualifies on NixOS, plus the NixOS evidence |

887 insertions, of which the NixOS fix is 55. Reviewers should read the
prototype as the substance and the fix as the delta.

The prototype is **opt-in and never auto-enabled**: no runtime selects this
backend by default, `node_modules` is gitignored, and the committed
`package-lock.json` pins dependencies without installing them. It supplies **no
provider authentication**, no TLS interception and no credential rewriting; it
is not a ready-to-use model-client launch command.

GH#35043 records that implementation was not authorized at the time it was
filed. Landing the prototype in `main` through this PR is an explicit operator
decision taken after the NixOS evidence below.

## The NixOS defect

SRT resolves every dependency by spawning the external `which(1)`
(`dist/utils/which.js:15`) rather than testing the configured absolute path:

```js
const result = spawnSync('which', [bin], { ... });
```

`cleanEnvironment()` (`backend.mjs:311`) deliberately builds `PATH` only from the
envelope's tool directories. `which` was not an envelope tool, so the spawn
failed and every lookup returned `null` — reporting tools that were present and
already configured by absolute path as missing. The probe failed with
`dependencies-not-ready`.

This is invisible on FHS distributions because the tools share `/usr/bin` with
`which(1)`, so the sanitized `PATH` incidentally contains it. On NixOS each
package has its own `bin` directory, so nothing resolved.

Confirmed by adding only that one directory to the sanitized `PATH`:

```
before: errors: ["ripgrep (<store-path>/bin/rg) not found"]
after:  errors: []   warnings: []
```

## The fix

- `backend.mjs`: `which` accepted and required as an envelope tool on every
  platform. It passes the same `executable()` validation as the others
  (absolute, not group/other-writable, outside the write root), so the trust
  boundary is unchanged — this adds no new grant, it stops refusing a tool the
  host already provides.
- `test-worker-egress-srt.mjs`: resolve `which` in native tool discovery.
- `worker-egress-srt.md`: document why `which` is mandatory, record the NixOS x64
  qualification, and capture the `read` bound as the binding platform constraint.

## Verification

Real synthetic qualification on NixOS 26.05, kernel 6.18.60, x64, bubblewrap
0.12.0, socat 1.8.1.3 — `ready: true`, all 13 checks true:

```
host-read-denied, approved-read, input-write-denied, host-write-shadow-or-denial,
host-file-unchanged, input-file-unchanged, unix-denied,
unix-socket-creation-denied, nested-userns-denied, descendant-and-argv,
proxy-live-and-denying, AF_INET, AF_INET6
```

No provider contact: `provider_connectivity: "not-tested"`, the proxy check uses
`blocked.invalid` and expects 403. No credentials, synthetic data only.

```
AIDEVOPS_SRT_REAL_CHECK=1 node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-egress-srt.mjs   4/4
node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-egress-srt.mjs                            3 pass, 1 skip
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-network-egress.sh                                 13/13
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-command-policy.sh                                61/61
shellcheck .agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-network-egress.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh                                                         ALL PASSED
```

Prior evidence on the prototype commit: Ubuntu 24.04.5 synthetic 4/4 with
bubblewrap 0.9.0.

## NixOS findings worth keeping

- **No AppArmor profile needed.** The host has no AppArmor, so the Ubuntu
  userns/`setgroups` workaround does not apply. The full namespace sequence,
  seccomp helper and nested-userns denial all work unmodified.
- **The 64-entry `read` bound is the binding constraint**, not the sandbox. The
  naive closure of the tools is 94 paths and is correctly refused with
  `bounded-path-list-required`. Dropping Node, preferring `coreutils` over
  `coreutils-full` and `util-linuxMinimal` for `setsid` gives 44 closure paths;
  the whole envelope then holds **57 of 64**. That margin is small — a nixpkgs
  bump can exceed it. Trim the closure rather than raising the bound.
- `bwrap` and `socat` are absent from a stock NixOS system profile and are not
  setuid-wrapped. An unprivileged `nix build` suffices and keeps them
  root-owned and immutable, but unreferenced store paths are deleted by
  `nix-collect-garbage` regardless of age. `which` is already in the base profile.
- Record store paths and the nixpkgs `narHash`, not build commands: the registry
  can be pinned to a store-path flake whose outputs change after a rebuild.
- `/lib` and `/etc/ld.so.cache` do not exist; `/lib64` is nix-ld. The shipped
  seccomp helper is a static executable, so nix-ld is not on the path.

## Known limits, deliberately not addressed here

- **macOS remains held.** The backend refuses readiness on `darwin` by design
  until the DNS and inherited-Mach-IPC boundary is reviewed, and the test asserts
  that hold. Split out as #38861 so it stops blocking the Linux evidence.
- **NixOS arm64 has no evidence.** Qualifying x64 does not qualify arm64; the
  platform table says so explicitly.
- **Dependency advisory open:** zod `GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5`, high but
  availability-only (`C:N/I:N/A:H`), no 3.x fix. It reaches this code through
  `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`'s pinned lockfile over operator-controlled,
  size-bounded inputs (`maximumBytes = 32768`, path lists ≤ 64). Merging the
  lockfile does not install it. Disposition is still required before promotion.

Resolves #38701
For #35043

title: t19079: fix(sandbox): cheap macOS descendant snapshot + close two cleanup identity gaps
body:
## Summary

macOS sandbox wait loop: replace the per-level bash walk and per-descendant ps/tr forks with one ps -axo pid,ppid,pgid,stat,lstart read and one awk pass (130-200 ms -> 45-48 ms per 0.5 s snapshot on a live 5-descendant worker tree; recorded pid/pgid/start rows byte-identical to the previous implementation). Root-caused the pre-existing macOS failure of 'normal exit removes nested process group': (1) snapshot dedup keyed on pid:start, so a descendant first seen between fork() and its own setsid() kept only its stale PGID, failed cleanup revalidation and survived (reparented to PID 1); dedup now keys on pid:pgid:start so the escaped identity gets its own verifiable row. (2) child_pgid was read immediately after 'setsid cmd &', racing the syscall and returning the wrapper's own PGID, so the self-PGID guard silently disabled the group kill; _sandbox_await_child_pgid now re-reads (bounded, /proc on Linux without forking) until PGID == PID. _sandbox_child_state drops a tr fork per poll.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh

## Decisions

Kept the 0.5 s snapshot cadence (lowering it widens the escape window for quickly detaching descendants). The two identity fixes are in the same cleanup path and block this issue's own acceptance criterion (existing nested-cleanup suite passes), so they ship together rather than as separate PRs. Awk reads fields via split($0, col) so the positional-parameter ratchet does not misread awk field refs.

## Regression Evidence

No test file changes because the existing repository suites already exercise every changed path and caught the defect: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh` failed 10/11 on macOS against the unchanged helper (case 'normal exit removes nested process group') and passes 11/11 with this change; `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-timeout-budget.sh` passes 4/4. Both suites source `sandbox-exec-helper.sh` directly, and the advisory "Affected script suites" CI job (Ubuntu) compares affected suites against base, so a regression in the single-read snapshot, the pid:pgid:start dedup or the child PGID wait re-fails existing coverage; the macOS path is covered by running the nested-cleanup suite locally on macOS. The performance claim is runtime-only evidence (live A/B probe on a running worker tree), which a deterministic unit test cannot assert without timing flakiness.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — shellcheck -x clean; /bin/bash -n (3.2) clean; test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh 10/11 -> 11/11 on macOS (same failure reproduced on the unchanged helper first); test-sandbox-timeout-budget.sh 4/4; live A/B on a running worker wrapper tree: identity_match=yes, old 130-200 ms vs patched 45-48 ms per snapshot; dedup probe adds a row only on PGID change; debug trace confirmed child_pgid == child_pid after the fix (previously the caller's PGID).; macOS: native platform detection, model replay sandbox and PATH portability checks passed at e7781fac725487f04ac45866e326d06ba385498b.

title: t19081: perf(pulse): reuse the in-cycle candidate census across rounds (GH#38876)

## Summary

Full-cycle dispatch candidate snapshots stay reusable for PULSE_DISPATCH_CANDIDATE_REUSE_MIN_S (default 1200 s, max 3600, 0 = off) instead of the >=300 s enumeration window. title: GH#38865: add wp-helper.sh --fluentsmtp for FluentSMTP SES connection migration
body:
## Summary

Adds `wp-helper.sh --fluentsmtp <site> list|migrate|test|backups|undo` (new `wp-helper-fluentsmtp.sh` transport + `wp-fluentsmtp.php` WP-CLI payload). `migrate` moves matching FluentSMTP Amazon SES connections to `local@<new-domain>` under FluentSMTP's `md5(sender)` key, carries additional senders, default and fallback references, sets the region, switches `key_store` to `wp_config` with empty DB keys, and writes `FLUENTMAIL_AWS_*` constants into wp-config.php (parse-checked, atomic rename, mode kept). It reads/writes only via `fluentMailGetSettings()`/`fluentMailSetSettings()` so DB secrets stay encrypted. Every real migrate first takes a 0600 backup of the raw option and wp-config.php outside the webroot; `undo` restores both and verifies SHA-256. AWS keys are passed as env-var names under `aidevops secret ... --`, read by jq from the environment and delivered on stdin (never argv/output). Only long-term `AKIA` keys are accepted (FluentSMTP has no session-token field); the new wp-config.php is built before the backup, so a refusal writes nothing. Docs: `services/email/ses.md` "FluentSMTP", pointer in `tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md`. Second and final deliverable issue #38865 after PR #38875 (Purelymail helper).

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/wp-fluentsmtp.php`: entry payload: argument parsing, `list`, `test`, dispatch
- `.agents/scripts/wp-fluentsmtp-store.php`: settings access, field helpers, atomic PHP file replacement
- `.agents/scripts/wp-fluentsmtp-migrate.php`: migration planner (renames, collisions, moved connections)
- `.agents/scripts/wp-fluentsmtp-remap.php`: sender mappings and default/fallback references follow renamed connections
- `.agents/scripts/wp-fluentsmtp-config.php`: STDIN key validation and the wp-config.php define writer
- `.agents/scripts/wp-fluentsmtp-backup.php`: backup, `backups` list, verified `undo`
- `.agents/scripts/wp-helper-fluentsmtp.sh`: transport (local/LocalWP/SSH); uploads all six PHP files side by side
- `.agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh`, `.agents/services/email/ses.md`, `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md`

The payload is split across files to clear Qlty's new-file complexity gate (one 140-complexity file at first).

## Decisions

Keys via `aidevops secret NAME -- ... --access-key-env NAME` (same convention change-plan uses for SSH passwords) instead of self re-exec, so `--tenant` and the caller environment are preserved. Raw option bytes are backed up (not decrypted settings) so undo is exact. `test` lifts staging `pre_http_request` blocks only with explicit `--lift-http-block`. A pre-existing FLUENTMAIL_AWS define the tool cannot remove refuses the run, because PHP keeps the first define.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified on a disposable WordPress (SQLite drop-in) with FluentSMTP 2.4.5 from wordpress.org. The fixture was seeded through the plugin's own `Settings::store()`: 2 SES connections on old.example (including an additional sender and the default) and an SMTP connection, with DB keys confirmed as ciphertext. Re-run in full after the module split. Results through `wp-helper.sh --fluentsmtp` (LocalWP site type):
  - Refusals: missing key env and bad region (rc=1). A temporary `ASIA` key is refused (rc=2) with zero backups written.
  - Dry run printed the plan.
  - Migrate moved both SES connections, remapped billing@ to the new key, the default followed, and SMTP was untouched. A next-process `list` shows keys=wp_config.
  - After a second migrate, wp-config.php has exactly 2 constant lines and passes `php -l`.
  - Rerun with from_domain=old.example refused (no match).
  - `test` with the migrated dummy keys reached real SES and failed with `InvalidClientTokenId` (rc=1), which proves the wp_config key path.
  - A foreign `undo` path is refused (rc=2). `undo` restored the option and wp-config.php byte-identical (checksums verified), and `list` matched the original.
  - SSH transport ran with local ssh/scp shims (no sshd available): all six files uploaded, remote quoting held, keys went on stdin (only the eval call drops `-n`), undo worked, and temp-dir removal was verified.
  - Leak check: dummy key values are absent from all output and the ssh command log.
  - ShellCheck, pipe-early-exit-check, markdownlint, `php -l` and pre-commit ratchets pass.
  - Not exercised: a real SSH host and a real SES key.

Resolves #38865

title: GH#38896: perf(git-shim): cut per-call guard cost without verdict change
body:
## Summary

Shim skips itself by inode when resolving native git (no readlink spawns per shim on PATH); guard memoises identical native-git probes within one `classify_git_argv` call only.

Threat model: probes are read-only and answer the same question about the same pre-execution repository state within a single classification. The memo is a process-local dict cleared at the start of every argv classification, never persisted (no files, env vars or daemons), with no subcommand bypass and unchanged classification logic. The inode skip only omits candidates that are the calling shim itself, which the existing shim detection would have rejected anyway.

Before/after exec counts: unchanged at 6 successful execs for `git add -n` with native git first on PATH (no shim on PATH to skip). A 20-call timing loop could not be run because the worker shell policy blocks loops, so no timing gain is claimed.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py, .agents/scripts/canonical_git_repository.py, .agents/scripts/git, .agents/scripts/runtime-env.sh

## Regression Evidence

This is a behaviour-preserving performance change with no verdict change, so no new test was added (the issue forbids changed expectations). The existing suites are the regression guard: `test-git-safety-guard.sh` 21/21 pass; `test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh` 183 pass and 15 fail, with the identical 15 failures on untouched main in this sandbox (clone, snapshot and credential cases). ShellCheck is clean on `git` and `runtime-env.sh`.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed, as under Regression Evidence; macOS not run on this host, needs-macos-verification.

title: GH#38901: fix(headless): apply the ChatGPT OAuth model denylist to worker same-tier fallback
body:
## Summary

When the Anthropic pool is cooling down, worker same-tier fallback now skips
OpenAI models that the routing table marks unsupported for ChatGPT OAuth. It no
longer spends a launch attempt on a model the provider is known to reject.

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`: `get_configured_models()` drops
  `openai/*` models listed in `chatgpt_oauth_restrictions.openai_unsupported`
  while the OpenCode auth file records OpenAI as `oauth`. Matching covers exact
  IDs and dated snapshots, as in
  `model-availability-probe-lib.sh:_chatgpt_oauth_denylist_check`. The list
  comes from the first routing table that defines it (custom, then
  framework), because custom tables usually omit it. Selection, round-robin
  and the attempt budget all read this list. API-key auth and explicit
  `--model` pins are unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-openai-routing.sh`: three cases asserted
  that Sol is selected under OAuth, which is the defect. They now use API-key
  auth. One OAuth case was added: standard tier selects Terra, and thinking
  tier returns 75 (backoff) when its only OpenAI candidate is denylisted.
- `.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json`: the comment now names the
  worker-side enforcement.

## Evidence

- From 2026-11-16 22:00Z to 2026-11-17 05:14Z there were 7 zero-worker spans
  totalling about 5.6 h. In each one, every launch failed on `gpt-6.1-terra`
  (attempt 1) and then on `gpt-6.1-sol` (attempt 2, `same_tier_fallback`),
  both with `model_unavailable`. The dispatcher had already skipped Sol through
  the denylist (`Resolved standard -> openai/gpt-6.1-terra (candidate 3 ...)`).
- Product-path reproduction with the worktree helper and the runner's real
  OAuth auth:
  `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_PROVIDER_ALLOWLIST=openai,opencode-go headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role worker --tier standard`
  printed `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` before this change and prints
  `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` after it.
- Retry replay on a copied state DB (Anthropic pool unavailable, Terra and Sol
  backed off): configured candidates are now `gpt-6.1-terra`,
  `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, and the exact-tier retry selects
  `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`.
- Logs from 2026-11-16 end with `All configured models are currently backed
  off` after the Sol rejection, so DeepSeek was not reached then. The same
  replay on the current deployed code does reach DeepSeek on attempt 3, so I
  could not reproduce that third-candidate filtering. This PR does not claim
  to fix it.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` is clean on both edited scripts.
- These tests pass: `test-headless-openai-routing.sh` (9/9),
  `test-headless-routing-retry.sh`, `test-headless-provider-round-robin.sh`,
  `test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh`,
  `test-headless-runtime-provider-tests-replay.sh`,
  `test-model-routing-overlay.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-variant.sh` and
  `test-stats-worker-zero-diagnostics.sh`.
- `test-oauth-pre-dispatch-rotation.sh` (canary rotation ordering) and
  `test-headless-runtime-helper.sh` (Claude sandbox signing/timeout) fail the
  same way on an unchanged older checkout, so those failures are pre-existing
  and unrelated.

Resolves #38901

title: GH#38908: perf(pulse): hand the full dispatch census to the next process on every exit
body:
## Summary

Any dispatch process that holds the instance lock now hands a still-fresh full census with unattempted candidates to the next dispatch process. The census is stamped with the full-cycle reuse window (`reuse_window`, default 1200s, capped at 3600s).

Before this change only a cooperative drain handed the census on (GH#38048), with a 300s window. As a result:
- 19 of 22 handoffs were discarded as stale.
- Refill-only runs orphaned censuses of 100-200 candidates under `pid-*` keys.
- The next first wave re-scanned serially and often returned 1-3 candidates while 16-19 slots were free (evidence in #38908).

Where the handoff now happens:
- **Drained cycle** (supervisor phase, before lock release): moves the census and its attempt ledger, as before.
- **Any other cycle** (supervisor phase, before lock release): shares a **copy** of the census and ledger. It keeps its own copy, because the LLM supervisor's early-exit recycle loop still runs `dispatch_max` from it after the lock is released. Its triage marker is also kept, so the per-cycle triage budget is not spent twice.
- **Refill-only run** (before lock release and in its cleanup trap): moves the census.
- **EXIT trap**: hands off only while `_LOCK_OWNED=true`. After lock release a newer process owns the handoff slot, so the trap only deletes its own files.

An expired or fully attempted census is not handed on. Adopted candidates still pass the registry/schedule recheck and every live dispatch gate. Eligibility mutations still invalidate the handoff.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh

## Decisions

- Full (non-first-wave) rounds still scan for themselves. Only first waves adopt a handoff, so `product_discovery_complete` semantics are unchanged.
- The handoff window keeps the GH#38210 rule: the handoff must be inside the window and the capture inside twice the window. It now uses the larger of the base window and the stamped reuse window.
- Copy rather than move for non-drained cycles: the recycle loop and the next cycle already dispatch concurrently and are arbitrated by live dispatch gates. Sharing the ranked list does not add a new overlap.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed.
  - `test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh`: all PASS. New cases:
    - an undrained lock holder hands off with `reuse_window=1200`
    - a process past lock release does not hand off
    - an exhausted census is not handed on
    - a sharing cycle keeps its census and ledger, and the handoff ledger is byte-identical
    - a reuse-window handoff is adopted past the 300s base window and discarded past it or with an out-of-range stamp
  - `test-pulse-event-refill.sh`: 39/39
  - `test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh`: 19/19
  - `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh`: 54/54
  - `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`: PASS
  - ShellCheck clean on changed scripts.
- **Post-deploy check:** `pulse.log` shows `transfer=copy|move` handoff lines, `dispatch_candidate_handoff_adopted` rises relative to `_discarded`, and first-wave candidate counts rise.

Resolves #38908

title: GH#38914: fix(full-loop): treat unreported required contexts as pending before merge
body:
## Summary

Pre-merge readiness now compares the branch-protection required contexts with the non-empty PR check rollup and adds every absent context as {state:MISSING,bucket:pending} (new _full_loop_add_unreported_required_checks), using one shared jq definition (missing_check) with the existing exact-head check-run path. Before, a freshly pushed head whose later required jobs (needs:, gate workflows) had not been created yet passed readiness on the reported subset, printed 'required checks are terminal-success', attempted gh pr merge, was refused by branch policy and exited CHECKS_PENDING, costing every session/worker a retry (observed on PR #38912). Readiness now stays pending and names the missing contexts, so callers wait instead of attempting the merge.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-remote-evidence.sh

## Decisions

Applied after the rollup is validated in _full_loop_query_required_checks, so the pending branch, persistence and terminal-failure precedence are unchanged (a reported failure still classifies terminal-failure). Resolver failures (required_contexts_rc != 0) keep the previous rollup-only behaviour. A required context that never reports (e.g. a zero-job workflow) now reads pending rather than success; GitHub blocks that merge anyway, and gh-checks-wait-helper still classifies zero-job runs as terminal.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified against live PR #38917 while its required checks started: the deployed v3.39 gate reported 'required checks are terminal-success' when the rollup listed only maintainer-gate and review-bot-gate (the GH#38914 bug reproduced live); this branch's gate on the same PR reported 'Required contexts not yet reported at the PR head: Complexity Analysis, Qlty Regression Gate, Framework Validation' and exited 1 pending. ## Summary

Bulk issue-sync close maps open issues to TODO tasks by the leading tNNN in the title. When a completed row already carried a different ref:GH#N, it called fix_gh_ref_in_todo to repoint the historical row to the title-matched issue, and that rewrite then satisfied require_task_issue_mapping in _do_close. Result: GH#38909 ('t2449 merge verdict ...', a topical reference to the April task t2449 / GH#20164) was closed as 'Completed via PR #20283' with status:done + solved:worker while its worker PR #38917 was still open. The row's own ref is now authoritative, matching single-task mode: a differing ref is a title collision, so the row is skipped and logged, with no ref rewrite and no close. Rows with no ref still gain the ref and close as before. Also adds the t19085 TODO entry and brief so the planning push lands with the fix (a TODO-only push before the fix would re-run bulk close and re-close the reopened #38909).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-close.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-completion-evidence.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19085-brief.md

## Decisions

Skipped rather than re-validated against the ref'd issue's state: a completed row whose ref differs from a title match is ambiguous at best, and a left-open duplicate costs one dedup pass, whereas a false close hides live work from redispatch and from the user. fix_gh_ref_in_todo stays in issue-sync-lib.sh (still covered by test-issue-sync-ref-comments.sh) but is no longer called by bulk close. The workflow checks out aidevops main for its scripts, so the fix applies to issue-sync on merge without a release.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified: ran the fixed '.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh close --dry-run --verbose' against the real marcusquinn/aidevops open issues and this branch's TODO.md. Output: 't2449: task-ID title collision — row references #20164; open #38909 left untouched' and 'Close: 0 closed, 161 skipped, 0 refs fixed'; TODO.md unchanged. Tests: test-issue-sync-completion-evidence.sh 25/25 (new live-mode case asserts the collision issue is not closed, the row ref stays GH#20164, and an equal-ref row still closes), test-issue-sync-ref-comments.sh, test-issue-sync-close-signature.sh 11/11; shellcheck clean.

Resolves #38921

title: GH#38925: perf(ci): run Framework Validation as parallel shards behind the required aggregator
body:
## Summary

Framework Validation ran 17 independent steps serially in one job (731s on PR #38920) and was the last required check on most PRs, setting merge latency for every worker and interactive PR. The three slowest groups now run as parallel shard jobs: profile README boundary (165s), profile README contributions fail-closed (167s), and pulse-merge regression suites (160s). The other 14 steps form the core shard. The `framework-validation` job keeps the required context name `Framework Validation`; it runs with `!cancelled()` after all shards and fails unless every shard result is `success`. Like the old single job, it is skipped on version/docs-only PRs. test-ci-runner-routing.mjs now pins 17 hosted `runs-on` selectors.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/tests/test-ci-runner-routing.mjs, .github/workflows/code-quality.yml, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19087-brief.md

## Decisions

Only the three groups over 150s were split. Each shard pays its own ~36s checkout, so finer sharding gains little until core becomes the long pole. The repo is public, so extra runner minutes are free. The aggregator has no checkout, so it adds only seconds after the slowest shard.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low
- **Verification:** self-assessed — node --test test-ci-runner-routing.mjs: 8/8 pass. actionlint: only SC2016 info on the pulse-merge step, also present on origin/main (deliberate bash -c literal). PyYAML diff of origin/main framework-validation steps against the four shards: 17 to 17 steps, none missing or duplicated; the only change is a comment inside the pulse-merge step. No job or check name collides with a required context. Pre-commit actionlint passed. This PR's own run measures the wall-time result.

Resolves #38925

title: GH#38932: fix(release): resolve squash commits with a missing GitHub PR association via verified subject hint
body:
## Summary

Every snapshot release was blocked. `aidevops release patch 38929` failed at capture-authorization with `ambiguous or unmerged snapshot commit` because GitHub returns no commit-to-PR association for `f20bbfcabf`, the squash merge of PR #38890, on both REST `commits/{sha}/pulls` and GraphQL `associatedPullRequests`, more than 3 hours after the merge. `release_snapshot_sources` now branches on the number of associated merged PRs. One PR keeps the existing path. More than one fails closed as ambiguous. Zero tries `_release_snapshot_hinted_record`, which reads the PR numbers in the commit subject (`(#N)` and `Merge pull request #N`) and accepts a hint only when GitHub's own PR record shows MERGED on the release branch with `mergeCommit.oid` equal to this exact commit. Hint read failures and two distinct verified hints fail closed. The existing ancestry checks and the second `pr view` verification still run on the hinted record. Both new checks carry `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19088-brief.md

## Decisions

Commit-SHA search was rejected as the fallback. It returned #38900, a later PR that contains the commit but did not introduce it, which would fail verification. The subject hint grants no authority by itself; the PR's recorded merge commit is the proof. The legacy aggregate-recovery lookup (`full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`) is not on the snapshot path and is unchanged.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified: the changed resolver ran read-only against live GitHub on the exact blocked range 132062a7d9..origin/main and mapped all 21 commits, with f20bbfcabf resolving to #38890. Before the change the same range failed. test-release-snapshot-helper.sh: all 14 sections pass. The existing `empty` association case still fails closed (no hint in its subjects). ShellCheck clean; pipe-early-exit-check clean.

Resolves #38932

title: GH#38942: feat(decisions): cross-repo maintainer decision queue and /decisions command (t19090)
body:
## Summary

Adds a read-only cross-repo **maintainer decision queue** so a maintainer can answer every `needs-maintainer-*` hold from one numbered list instead of opening issue threads.

- NEW `.agents/scripts/maintainer-decisions-helper.sh list [--repo owner/repo] [--format tsv|json|md] [--max N]`: discovers open issues labelled `needs-maintainer-input`, `needs-maintainer-permissions` or `needs-credentials` in managed pulse repos (`repos.json`), and classifies each from trusted comments: `decide`, `permission`, `credentials`, `replied`, `manual`, `no-question`, `answered`, `parked`. Makes no GitHub writes.
- NEW `/decisions` command (`.agents/scripts/commands/decisions.md`): presents the queue with an AI recommendation per item, posts only answers the maintainer gives in-session through `gh-write-helper.sh issue comment` with `<!-- aidevops:maintainer-decision -->`, and adds `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` only on an approved retry. It never accepts secrets in chat.
- EDIT `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md` "Terminal-blocker recovery": a 4-line pointer (kept under the 500-line limit).

## Deviation from the brief: `replied` vs `answered`

The brief classified any later OWNER/MEMBER comment without automation markers as `answered`. Live data disproved that heuristic. All 6 such holds, in one private managed repo, were an app queue notice ("…still blocked after 3 automatic retries…") posted with the owner's token and carrying no aidevops marker. These holds now classify as `replied`, with `reply_excerpt` shown so the caller can tell a typed answer from automation. `answered` now requires an explicit `<!-- aidevops:maintainer-decision -->` marker or a standalone retry directive.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/maintainer-decisions-helper.sh`: clean. Pre-commit ratchets (returns, positional params, string literals, Bash 3.2 parse) pass.
- Live full run across managed repos: 89 records (decide=15, permission=6, credentials=21, replied=6, manual=8, no-question=32, parked=1). Each decide item shows its exact `Input requested:` question.
- A single-repo md run before and after the kind-table refactor gives identical counts (73 total: decide=14, permission=5, credentials=12, replied=6, manual=4, no-question=31, parked=1).
- `--format json | jq -e 'type == "array"'` passes. `--max`, which needs a value, and unknown options both fail with usage.
- Spot checks: a `replied` hold whose excerpt is app queue automation; a `parked` hold with an `outlier_hold` policy newer than the hold; #32273 `manual`.
- Compatibility: `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` counts any non-automation OWNER/MEMBER comment as maintainer input, and `aidevops:sig` is not an automation marker, so signed `/decisions` answers are honoured by the circuit and recovery pass.

Resolves #38942

title: fix(runtime-config): preserve user-owned block in generated AGENTS.md
body:
## Summary

`setup.sh --stage ai-session` (run by auto-update after every release and on
script-drift redeploys) regenerates `~/.config/<runtime>/AGENTS.md` with
`cat >`, so any local rules a user adds to that file are lost on the next
update. This adds a user-owned block that survives regeneration.

**Root cause:** `_generate_greeting_agents_md()` in
`.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config-agents.sh` writes the whole file
unconditionally from a heredoc.

**Fix:**
- New markers: `<!-- aidevops:user-rules:start -->` / `<!-- aidevops:user-rules:end -->`.
- Before regenerating, `_agents_md_extract_user_block` captures the first
  complete block (CRLF-tolerant; an unterminated block is ignored).
- After the framework template is written, `_agents_md_prepend_user_block`
  puts the block back at the top of the file. The file is rewritten in place,
  so symlinks and permissions are kept.
- Everything outside the markers stays framework-managed, exactly as before.
  Applies to every runtime that uses the helper (OpenCode, Claude Code).
- No behaviour change for users who don't use the markers.

**How to use it:** put local rules at the top of
`~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` (or the Claude Code equivalent) like this:

    <!-- aidevops:user-rules:start -->
    ## My local rules
    - ...
    <!-- aidevops:user-rules:end -->

Anything between the markers is kept across `setup.sh` runs and
auto-updates; anything outside them is still replaced by the template.

## Linked issue

Linked issue: Resolves #38952

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor

## Runtime Testing

**Testing level:**

**Test results:** N/A for self-assessed. Local checks:

  Claude Code): fresh generate adds no block; a user block survives
  regeneration exactly once, at the top, content intact, while stray text
  outside it is still removed; repeated regeneration is idempotent; an
  unterminated block is not copied; a symlinked AGENTS.md is updated in
  place and keeps its block.

title: t19091: fix(terminal-blocker): permission_required holds publish the named ask as input_required
body:
## Summary

A `permission_required` terminal-blocker release only says "Resolve the evidenced permission prerequisite through the human-owned approval flow". Unless the worker also posted a scoped grant request with `worker-permission-helper.sh request`, nothing names what to approve. The hold gets `needs-maintainer-input`, whose guidance says the ask is "named in the brief or the latest blocker comment", but no ask exists. Nobody can act, so the hold never moves.

This change publishes the ask when one exists:

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: for a final report with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=permission_required` and exactly one valid `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER`, the Python capture reports the owner and the single `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_QUESTION` line as a candidate ask. It keeps `permission_required`. `_terminal_blocker_permission_ask_class` then reclassifies to `input_required:<owner>` only when `_terminal_blocker_public_line`, the same validator the release envelope uses, accepts that exact question. Otherwise it clears the question. The class therefore never changes without a published ask. The existing envelope then publishes `Input requested:`. That shape is already canonical in `approval-snapshot-v2.sh`, so older runners accept it. A bare denial, an invalid or duplicated owner, or a duplicated, oversized or unpublishable question keeps `permission_required`.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh` (rule 8): workers add the owner and question lines when one named person can grant or approve the blocker by answering in the issue.
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`: documents the reclassification.
- The capture's Python program moves unchanged into a source-time variable (`_TBC_CAPTURE_PY`, run with `python3 -c`). The function stays under the 100-line function-complexity gate; `sys.argv` indexing is the same.

Runtime guards still verify every grant. The reclassified hold uses the `input_required` wake set: a brief or dependency change, or a trusted retry. That matches the post-GH#36342 `permission_required` behaviour after its one window re-arm.

## Evidence

- `maintainer-decisions-helper.sh list` on 2026-11-18: in one managed private organisation, 31 of 73 maintainer holds were "no-question" AI-side gaps. 13 of those were `permission_required` releases with no published ask, including 7 consolidation tasks released within 2-3 minutes of dispatch. The same runner and model completed other consolidation tasks, and no other runner can read the cause.
- This runner's local blocker log has `permission_required` exits that are owner decisions: approving the supersede of live result rows, and authorizing new sign-ins after a rate-limit window. The contract already routes spend and credential-route decisions to `input_required`.

## Verification

- Ad hoc `terminal_blocker_capture_output` on sample OpenCode JSONL (final fingerprint class plus whether the release would publish the question):
  - ask → `input_required` owner `maintainer`, published
  - unpadded 500-character question → `input_required`, published
  - bare, bad owner, two questions, markup, no question → `permission_required`, no question
  - `Approve authorization: staging deployment?` (rejected by the publication validator) → `permission_required`, no question
  - 500 characters plus trailing space → `permission_required`, no question
  - `input_required` with owner → unchanged; `input_required` without owner → `unknown` (unchanged)
- `terminal_blocker_capture_output` + `_terminal_blocker_recovery` for the ask case printed `reason=input_required owner=maintainer`, `Input requested: <question>` and the `needs-maintainer-input` companion line.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: 62 run, 0 failed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lifecycle-comms.sh`: 27/27 passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-capability.sh`: exit 0.
- `shellcheck` on the three changed scripts: clean. Pre-commit ratchets passed.

Resolves #38951

title: t19092: fix(terminal-blocker): a re-armed permission_required hold gives other runners the first claim
body:
## Summary

When a `permission_required` hold re-arms after its window (GH#36232), the runner that released it usually reclaims it in its next cycle, before any peer has seen `status:available`. That runner then repeats the same denial, which spends the window (GH#36342) and leaves the issue waiting for a human. Other runners complete the same task class.

With this change, the releasing login defers to its peers for a bounded grace period after the re-arm:

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: new `terminal_blocker_permission_peer_preference_active comments_json`. It returns 0 and prints `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_PERMISSION_PEER_PREFERENCE retry_after=<epoch>` only when all of these hold:
  - the newest trusted hold event (observation or circuit marker) carries the `permission_required` fingerprint;
  - this runner's login authored that event;
  - a `terminal-blocker-rearmed` receipt follows it, authored by an OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR or by this login. That is the same set whose receipts recovery accepts for replay suppression (`_tbr_project_rearm`); both uses only defer, so recovery's receipt producer needs no change. The set is a new constant, `_TBC_TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS`, defined next to `_TBC_AUTHORITATIVE_ASSOCIATIONS`. `terminal_blocker_permission_request_evidenced` and `terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments` now use it in place of their inline copies of the same set (no behaviour change; checked against every association value);
  - no trusted retry follows it;
  - now is inside `AIDEVOPS_PERMISSION_PEER_GRACE_SECONDS` (default 3600; 0 disables; leading zeros are read as base 10) from the newest receipt.

  Any other case, including unreadable evidence, returns 1 and keeps today's behaviour. The newest-permission-event selection moves into `_terminal_blocker_newest_permission_event`, which `terminal_blocker_permission_rearm_after` now shares (no behaviour change there).
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`: `has_dispatch_comment` (dedup Layer 5) calls the gate right after `terminal_blocker_circuit_active`. This differs from the issue brief, which placed the call inside `terminal_blocker_circuit_active`. `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` also calls that function, and a dispatch-only deferral must not look like an active hold to recovery.
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`: documents the grace period and the dedup log line.

The gate makes no GitHub calls. It reads only the trusted comments that dedup already fetched, grants nothing, never defers another login, and writes no comments or labels. Single-runner installs reclaim after the grace period, so they keep today's behaviour, only later. A peer attempt either completes the task or adds second-runner evidence for the existing fleet hold (GH#35788).

## Evidence

From a managed private repo, 2026-11-17/18 (repo and runner names withheld):

- A consolidation task released `permission_required` on runner A. The 12-hour window re-armed it on runner A, runner A dispatched it again 24 minutes later, and it repeated the denial within 80 seconds. That opened the circuit. An interactive session later closed the task by hand.
- All 9 held consolidation tasks there were released by runner A with one model. In a 20-task sample, every consolidation task dispatched to runners B and C completed.
- When a peer did get first claim after a re-arm, it picked the issue up within 3-10 minutes.

## Verification

- Ad hoc: sourced `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` and called the gate on fixture comments. It returned 0 for self in grace (`retry_after` = receipt + 3600) and for a peer-authored receipt after a self-released hold. It returned 1 for a peer login, grace expired, grace 0, custom grace 300 expired, no login, no receipt, receipt before the hold, `input_required` class, a trusted retry after the hold, a newer peer hold, and malformed JSON. After the review fixes: a COLLABORATOR peer receipt and a self receipt reported as CONTRIBUTOR return 0, a CONTRIBUTOR peer receipt returns 1, and graces `000060` and `000090` give `retry_after` = receipt + 60 and + 90.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: 62 run, 0 failed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lifecycle-comms.sh`: 27/27 passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-capability.sh`: exit 0.
- Permission-request suites after the shared definition: `test-permission-grant-verification`, `test-worker-permission-helper`, `test-permission-approval-content-binding`, all exit 0.
- Dedup suites through `has_dispatch_comment`: `test-dispatch-dedup-multi-operator`, `test-dispatch-dedup-fail-closed`, `test-consolidation-multi-runner`, `test-dispatch-dedup-maintainer-permission-block`, `test-dispatch-dedup-gh-call-budget`, all exit 0.
- `shellcheck` on both changed scripts: clean. `has_dispatch_comment` is 88 lines and the new gate is 31 lines, both under the function-complexity gate. Pre-commit ratchets passed.

Resolves #38957
